Cameroun : une grenade et des munitions trouvées dans un établissement scolaire à l’Est
items.description: © AOAV La découverte a été faite ce mardi au lycée technique de Kpokolota situé dans un quartier de la ville de Bertoua, capitale régionale de l’Est. Le lycée technique de Kpokolota dans la région de l’Est est au cœur d’une découverte étrange ce mardi. Un élève a été trouvé en possession d’une grenade, de trois munitions pour arme automatique et d’un poignard en pleine salle de classe. Après la découverte, une alerte donnée a permis de sécuriser l’engin explosif et de mettre l’élève à la disposition des forces de sécurité. L’élève qui serait l’enfant d’un militaire a été remis aux forces de sécurité pour exploitation, rapporte un média en ligne spécialisé dans l’actualité de la région. Le sujet qui est loin d’être un fait divers, remet sur la table la sécurité des élèves des enseignants et du personnel administratif dans des établissements scolaires. Le cas de Kpokolota montre que malgré les efforts fournis par des établissements scolaires et des forces de sécurité, les occupants des établissements ne sont toujours pas autant en sécurité qu’ils le devraient. La découverte de ce mardi à Bertoua indique qu’au-delà des lames, couteaux, tournevis, machettes ou tout autres armes blanches que les élèves ont l’habitude de faire entrer au sein des établissements scolaires, ils sont capables d’aller plus loin. Les armes de guerre aussi dans une zone qui n’est pas en crise sécuritaire peuvent se retrouver en classe du fait de la volonté d’un élève. Tout comme, à la suite d’un fait, des élèves sont capables de réduire des infrastructures en débris. Ce qui amène ainsi à interroger davantage les dispositions que les chefs d’établissements scolaires prennent pour assurer en permanence la sécurité des personnes et de biens. Et les dispositions que les autorités administratives et sécuritaires prennent pour maîtriser la circulation des armes et des munitions. Au-delà de ce niveau de responsabilité, il est aussi capital de se tourner une fois de plus vers les parents, eux qui sont au contact des élèves chaque matin, chaque soir et la nuit. A tous les niveaux, la surveillance permanente reste de mise et le renforcement des mesures de sécurité est une nécessité. Cet article Cameroun : une grenade et des munitions trouvées dans un établissement scolaire à l’Est est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: Orpaillage clandestin à Siguiri : les 202 prévenus plaident coupables devant la CRIEF, jonction avec le dossier des 22 administrateurs territoriaux
items.description: Le procès opposant le parquet spécial à 202 personnes interpellées dans le cadre de la lutte contre l’orpaillage clandestin à Siguiri s’est ouvert ce mardi 10 novembre 2026 devant la chambre de jugement de la Cour de répression des infractions économiques et financières (CRIEF). À l’issue de l’audience, la cour a ordonné la jonction de cette procédure avec celle concernant les 22 administrateurs territoriaux, déjà pendante devant elle. La suite des débats est prévue ce mercredi 11 novembre. Les 202 prévenus, tous placés sous mandat de dépôt, sont de nationalités guinéenne, malienne, burkinabè, togolaise et béninoise. Ils sont poursuivis pour exploitation illégale de substances minières, dégradation de l’environnement, destructions diverses et pollution des eaux. Appelés à la barre à tour de rôle, les prévenus ont reconnu les faits qui leur sont reprochés. Prenant la parole, la défense a attiré l’attention de la cour sur la présence de 12 mineurs parmi les prévenus. Me Abou Camara a ainsi sollicité la prise en compte de leur minorité dans l’examen du dossier. Une position contestée par le parquet spécial. Représenté à l’audience par Charles Wright, le ministère public a soutenu que l’ensemble des prévenus étaient majeurs, estimant que la défense ne disposait d’aucune preuve permettant d’établir la minorité des 12 personnes concernées. Par ailleurs, le procureur spécial a sollicité la jonction des procédures, estimant que le dossier des 202 prévenus était étroitement lié à celui des 22 administrateurs territoriaux, déjà soumis à l’examen de la chambre de jugement. Après avoir entendu les différentes observations, la cour, présidée par Alpha Camara, s’est déclarée compétente et a ordonné la jonction des deux procédures. L’affaire a été renvoyée au mercredi 11 novembre pour la poursuite des débats. Pour rappel, 1 263 personnes ont été interpellées dans le cadre des opérations menées contre l’exploitation illégale de l’or à Siguiri. Leurs dossiers ont été répartis entre plusieurs juridictions relevant de la Cour d’appel de Conakry, notamment les tribunaux de première instance de Kaloum, Dixinn, Coyah, Dubréka et Forécariah, ainsi que la CRIEF. items.title: Intelligence artificielle : l’Algérie et la Chine préparent un centre de calcul haute performance
items.description: L'Algerie entend renforcer ses capacites en intelligence artificielle grâce a un partenariat avec la Chine. Le 9 novembre, le ministre de l'Enseignement superieur et de la Recherche scientifique, Kamel Baddari, a rencontre une delegation chinoise pour examiner un projet de centre de donnees dedie a l'IA. L'infrastructure doit etre implantee au sein de l'ecole nationale superieure d'intelligence artificielle (ENSIA), a Sidi Abdellah, pres d'Alger. Les discussions ont porte sur les caracteristiques techniques du projet, les equipements necessaires, le calendrier de realisation et les contraintes environnementales. Aucun montant d'investissement ni aucune date de mise en service n'ont ete annonces. L'identite des entreprises chinoises susceptibles de participer a sa construction reste egalement a preciser. Le tournant IA d'Alger L'objectif est de doter le pays de capacites de calcul haute performance (HPC), indispensables a l'entraînement de modeles d'intelligence artificielle et au traitement de grandes quantites de donnees. Ces equipements pourraient notamment beneficier aux chercheurs, aux universites et aux entreprises developpant des applications dans l'industrie, l'energie ou la sante. Au-dela des infrastructures, Alger mise sur le transfert de technologies et la formation d'ingenieurs locaux pour reduire sa dependance aux capacites de calcul etrangeres. Le projet s'inscrit dans une strategie nationale qui prevoit notamment la formation de 50 000 specialistes de l'IA d'ici 2030. Le 19 octobre, les autorites avaient deja engage des discussions avec plusieurs entreprises publiques et privees pour financer l'acquisition de processeurs graphiques (GPU), essentiels au developpement de l'IA. Cette cooperation avec Pekin s'inscrit dans les ambitions de diversification economique de l'Algerie. Le gouvernement ambitionne de faire du pays un pole regional de l'intelligence artificielle, alors que la maîtrise des infrastructures numeriques devient un enjeu strategique mondial.

items.title: RDC : le FRN de Joseph Kabila étend son offensive au Sud-Kivu, plus de 160 000 déplacés
items.description: La situation securitaire continue de se degrader dans la province du Sud-Kivu, ou les combattants du Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) ont enregistre de nouvelles avancees face aux forces armees congolaises. Depuis le lancement de leur offensive, dans la nuit du 6 au 7 novembre, ils ont pris le controle de plusieurs localites situees dans le territoire de Kalehe, notamment dans la zone de Bunyakiri. L'operation s'est concentree autour de la route nationale 3, un axe reliant Bukavu a Kisangani en passant par Walikale. Selon des sources militaires congolaises, les combattants du FRN ont progresse a travers le parc national de Kahuzi-Biega avant de s'emparer de plusieurs positions occupees par l'armee et ses allies. Bitale et Kambali figurent parmi les localites tombees aux mains du mouvement. Le 8 novembre, Bulambika a egalement ete prise a l'issue d'affrontements avec les forces gouvernementales et les combattants wazalendo qui les soutiennent. Le FRN est dirige par l'ancien president congolais Joseph Kabila. Il est issu de l'AFC/M23, mouvement arme dont les activites dans l'est de la RDC beneficierait du soutien du Rwanda. Une progression contestee et des milliers de familles sur les routes L'ampleur de cette avancee fait toutefois l'objet d'appreciations differentes. Alors que des sources de la societe civile de Kalehe evaluent la progression des combattants a environ 60 kilometres, d'autres interlocuteurs locaux evoquent une cinquantaine de kilometres. L'armee congolaise affirme, pour sa part, conserver le controle de plusieurs localites, dont Mubugu et Hombo-Sud. Les consequences humanitaires de cette offensive sont deja importantes. L'administrateur du territoire de Kalehe, Thomas Bakenga, fait etat de plus de 160 000 personnes deplacees depuis le debut des combats. Une partie des habitants a trouve refuge a Hombo, a proximite de la limite entre les provinces du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu, tandis que d'autres ont fui dans les zones forestieres.

items.title: Muere un policía y otro resulta gravemente herido en una explosión en Oviedo
items.description: Un agente de la Policía Nacional ha fallecido este martes y otro ha resultado gravemente herido tras la explosión de un artefacto en el barrio de Villafría, en Oviedo, en un suceso presuntamente relacionado con una disputa vecinal, según han confirmado fuentes policiales. El agente fallecido es un subinspector de Guías Caninos del Cuerpo y el policía herido es miembro de los Tedax ―la unidad de élite especializada en la neutralización, desactivación e intervención de artefactos explosivos―. La Policía ha puesto en marcha una operación en la capital asturiana para localizar al presunto autor, de 64 años, con antecedentes de delincuencia común, que a primera hora de la mañana supuestamente disparó a una vecina menor de edad ―que permanece ingresada en el Hospital Universitario Central de Asturias (HUCA)― y dejó la mochila con los explosivos. items.title: Mobilisation lycéenne et étudiante : l’intersyndicale claque la porte à Matignon, la contestation se poursuit
items.description: Les representants de l'intersyndicale lyceenne et etudiante ont quitte, le 9 novembre, la premiere reunion du comite de reforme de Parcoursup a Matignon, denoncant l'absence de propositions concretes et la presence du syndicat etudiant de droite UNI ainsi que de parlementaires du Rassemblement national (RN). Un nouvel appel a la mobilisation a ete lance pour ce 10 novembre. Deux reunions pour rien, sinon une determination renforcee a poursuivre le mouvement. Tel est le constat dresse par une majorite d'organisations lyceennes et etudiantes a l'issue de leur rencontre avec le Premier ministre Sebastien Lecornu, suivie de la premiere reunion du « comite de reforme de Parcoursup ». Les representants de l'intersyndicale, des elus du Conseil national de la vie lyceenne (CNVL) et les organisations syndicales enseignantes ont quitte la seance, a laquelle participaient les ministres de l'education nationale, edouard Geffray, et de l'Enseignement superieur, Philippe Baptiste. Les organisations mobilisees ont deplore l'absence de mesures concretes et d'engagements budgetaires repondant a leurs revendications. Elles ont egalement proteste contre la presence du syndicat etudiant de droite UNI, de representants du RN et du Medef. Comité de suivi Parcoursup : l'intersyndicale de l'Education quitte la réunion ! Pour le @snesfsu.bsky.social et la @fsu-nationale.bsky.social une réunion sans nouvelle réponse, en présence du patronat et de l'extrême droite. Pas question de continuer les discussions ! — Sophie Vénétitay ( @svenetitay.bsky.social ) 9 novembre 2026 à 19:35 Selon Ryad Rani, president de l'Union syndicale lyceenne (USL), les seules pistes evoquees concernent une circulaire pour transformer les trimestres en semestres et une possible creation de 5 000 places en Île-de-France, en complement des 15 000 annoncees fin octobre. L'intersyndicale reclame 10 milliards d'euros pour financer des mesures d'urgence, notamment la revalorisation des bourses et l'abrogation de Parcoursup. Sophie Venetitay, secretaire generale du SNES-FSU, a denonce une « strategie de pourrissement », alors que la situation devant les lycees reste preoccupante. Ce 10 novembre, l'intersyndicale lyceenne et etudiante ainsi que la coordination etudiante Interfac Île-de-France appellent a une nouvelle journee de manifestations. a Paris, un cortege doit partir a 14 heures du Pantheon pour rejoindre la place d'Italie, selon un itineraire impose par la prefecture de police. Repost de @InterfacIDF Rdv mardi 10 novembre à 18h au 190b avenue de Clichy pour une assemblée générale Interfac. Ne laissons pas le gouvernement ou les directions syndicales décider de nos modalités de mobilisation ! Préparons nous-mêmes les suites dans nos AGs et comités de mobilisation. — Coppélia Moreau (@CoppeliaMoreau) November 9, 2026 Les blocages se poursuivent dans plusieurs lycees et universites. Selon le ministere de l'education nationale, 49 lycees, soit 1,3 % des etablissements du pays, etaient bloques ce 10 novembre au matin, contre 31 la veille. Malgre ces chiffres relativement limites a l'echelle nationale, les organisations syndicales entendent maintenir la pression sur le gouvernement, dont elles jugent les propositions insuffisantes.

items.title: Republic Financial Holdings Limited announces Karen Yip Chuck as Group President Nigel Baptiste retires
items.description: Republic Financial Holdings Limited (RFHL) has announced a historic leadership transition following the retirement of Nigel Baptiste as Group President and Chief Executive Officer of RFHL and Managing Director of Republic Bank Limited, with his last day being November 13, 2026. Persuant to Nigel Baptiste’s retirement, Republic Financial Holdings Limited has appointed Karen Yip Chuck to both roles, effective November 14, 2026. Baptiste retires after a distinguished career spanning more than three decades with the Republic Group, including the last ten years at its helm. He originally retired on May 10, 2026, after agreeing to stay on with the organisation through the end of its financial year. During his decade of executive stewardship, the Group doubled its asset base and expanded its operational footprint across sixteen territories. Under his leadership, RFHL also significantly scaled its corporate social responsibility and community development initiatives across the regions it serves. Reflecting on Baptiste’s tenure, Yashmid Karamath, Chairman of Republic Financial Holdings Limited, highlighted the strength of the institution’s leadership pipeline. “For over thirty years, and especially over the last decade as Group President and CEO, Nigel Baptiste has been a guiding force for the Republic Group,” the Chairman stated. “While our financial milestones, doubling our assets and expanding across sixteen countries, speak to his strategic acumen, Nigel’s true legacy lies in his unwavering investment in our people and our communities. By mentoring and empowering those around him, he has nurtured a brilliant new generation of leaders, continuing our proud, historic tradition of entrusting the Group’s future to exceptional hands. We extend our deepest gratitude to Nigel and wish him boundless joy and fulfillment in his retirement.” Ms. Yip Chuck makes history as the first woman appointed to lead the Republic Group. She is a banker with 36 years of service at Republic Bank and a pivotal member of the Executive Leadership Team and she brings an extensive record of strategic growth, institutional strengthening, and long term sustainability to the role. Throughout her tenure, Yip Chuck strengthened and aligned the Bank’s operational risk framework with global standards, reinforcing world-class corporate governance. She also was responsible for consistently championing forward-thinking products to meet evolving client needs and served as a key catalyst for regional growth by expanding corporate banking relationships across the Caribbean, driving economic diversification through expert advisory support. “Our strength has always come from our people and our shared commitment to the communities we serve,” said incoming Group President and CEO Karen Yip Chuck. “I am deeply honoured to accept the baton from Nigel and to build upon the remarkable foundation he has laid. Throughout my thirty- six years with Republic, I have lived by the belief that the Bank will only thrive when its people thrive. As we enter this next chapter of growth, my focus remains steadfast: empowering our teams, deepening our client relationships, and delivering enduring value for our employees, shareholders, customers, and communities.” Commenting on Ms. Yip Chuck’s appointment, the Chairman added: “Karen steps forward with unwavering dedication, sound judgment, commercial acumen, strong governance credentials and a deep understanding of the diverse markets in which we operate.” “Her proven record of performance and people-centred leadership gives the Board every confidence that she will strengthen our legacy and guide the Republic Group seamlessly into the future. Over a distinguished 36-year career with us, and as a cornerstone of our Executive Leadership Team, Karen has already helped architect the operational strength and vibrant culture we share today. What is inspiring about Karen is her philosophy on leadership. She has spent three decades championing the belief that our institution only thrives when our people thrive. Her faith in the potential of this team is absolute, and because she knows our people, our values, and our strategy inside and out, we move forward with confidence,” he noted.

items.title: Culture : après avoir conquis le Zénith de Paris, Djélykaba Bintou de retour en Guinée
items.description: Après avoir porté haut les couleurs de la musique guinéenne sur la scène du Zénith de Paris, le samedi 7 novembre 2026, Djélykaba Bintou Kouyaté a regagné Conakry dans la nuit du lundi 9 novembre. Avec son spectacle « Audace », la « patronne » a franchi une nouvelle étape de sa carrière artistique dans cette salle mythique de Paris-La Villette, devant plusieurs milliers de spectateurs. La salle était annoncée complète, avec une affluence estimée à près de 7 000 personnes selon plusieurs comptes rendus de presse. Pour ce rendez-vous avec le public parisien, l’artiste a misé sur un répertoire mêlant ses succès populaires à ses nouvelles productions. Elle a revisité plusieurs titres qui ont marqué son parcours, tout en accordant une place de choix aux rythmes et aux sonorités du patrimoine musical guinéen, dans une véritable mosaïque de langues nationales. La soirée a également été marquée par la présence de plusieurs artistes invités, notamment les chanteurs guinéens Petit Kandia et Saifon, ainsi que Sidiki Diabaté, Mia Guissé et Viviane du Sénégal, sans oublier Mariam Bah du Mali. Ces différentes participations ont donné une dimension sous-régionale à cet événement musical. Au-delà de l’affluence, ce spectacle a été une vitrine de la diversité culturelle guinéenne. À travers les langues nationales, les rythmes traditionnels et les influences contemporaines qui caractérisent son univers musical, Djélykaba Bintou a proposé une prestation profondément ancrée dans son identité culturelle. Au lendemain de cette soirée, la chanteuse avait exprimé sa reconnaissance envers ses fans, ses collaborateurs ainsi que les personnalités et institutions qui ont contribué à la concrétisation de ce projet. Cette performance s’inscrit dans la dynamique de promotion de son album « Renaissance », dévoilé en septembre dernier. Composé de 15 titres et de trois bonus, cet opus comprend plusieurs collaborations avec des artistes africains. De retour en Guinée, la « Djély » retrouve ainsi son public après cette expérience parisienne. Elle devrait poursuivre cette dynamique sur la scène nationale avec un concert annoncé le 5 décembre 2026 au stade Général Lansana Conté de Nongo, à Conakry. Avec « Audace », Djélykaba Bintou ajoute une nouvelle expérience internationale à son parcours. Plus qu’un rendez-vous musical réussi, cette prestation aura aussi été une occasion de promouvoir la richesse du patrimoine culturel guinéen et de renforcer la visibilité de la musique nationale au-delà de nos frontières. items.title: TRANSFERT D’ARGENT ET CYBERCRIMINALITÉ, L’URGENCE DE SÉCURISER NOS APPLICATIONS
items.description: Le développement des transferts d’argent par téléphone constitue une avancée importante pour l’inclusion financière au Niger. Des services comme Orange Money, Airtel Money, Nita Transfert, Amana Transfert d’Argent et les applications bancaires facilitent aujourd’hui les transactions quotidiennes de milliers de citoyens. Cependant, cette évolution s’accompagne d’un risque préoccupant. Le vol d’un téléphone portable peut désormais entraîner la perte immédiate des économies de son propriétaire. Pour certains criminels, l’objectif n’est plus seulement de voler un appareil, mais d’accéder aux applications financières qu’il contient, de prendre le contrôle des comptes et de transférer rapidement les fonds vers d’autres numéros. Plusieurs techniques sont utilisées. Le vol d’un téléphone déjà déverrouillé, la récupération des codes confidentiels, le détournement de carte SIM (SIM Swap), l’usurpation d’identité et les manipulations téléphoniques permettent aux fraudeurs de contourner les protections existantes. Une affaire enregistrée au Niger en mai 2026 illustre parfaitement ces risques. La Division de lutte contre la cybercriminalité a interpellé un individu soupçonné d’avoir exploité des données personnelles de clients, falsifié des pièces d’identité et utilisé de fausses procédures de réinitialisation de mots de passe pour détourner de l’argent. Cette affaire montre que les failles peuvent se situer aussi bien dans les applications que dans les procédures internes des sociétés. Les chiffres régionaux et internationaux confirment l’ampleur du phénomène. Selon le rapport 2024 de la BCEAO sur les services financiers numériques, publié en mars 2026, l’UEMOA comptait 248 millions de comptes de monnaie électronique, contre 209 millions en 2023, soit une progression de près de 19 %. Le nombre de transactions a atteint environ 11,9 milliards en 2024, en hausse de 26,66 %. Cette progression considérable montre l’importance prise par les services financiers numériques dans notre espace économique. De son côté, la GSMA, dans son rapport The Mobile Economy Africa 2025, estime que les fraudes liées au mobile money en Afrique ont dépassé 1 milliard de dollars en 2023. Il s’agit d’une estimation continentale qui donne une idée de l’ampleur des pertes financières liées à ces pratiques. Le rapport 2026 de la GSMA sur l’industrie du mobile money apporte également des indications intéressantes. Dans son analyse des typologies de fraude recensées auprès des acteurs du secteur en 2024, les fraudes à l’identité arrivent en tête avec 90 %, suivies de l’ingénierie sociale avec 88 %, des fraudes internes avec 87 %, du détournement de carte SIM avec 79 % et de la cyberfraude avec 60 %. Ces pourcentages correspondent aux niveaux de prévalence rapportés pour les différentes catégories de fraude, et non à la part des pertes financières. Enfin, INTERPOL, dans son rapport 2025 sur les cybermenaces en Afrique, indique que la cybercriminalité représente plus de 30 % des infractions recensées dans les pays d’Afrique de l’Ouest et de l’Est étudiés. L’organisation souligne également que 90 % des pays africains interrogés estiment devoir renforcer sensiblement leurs capacités de lutte contre ces infractions. Les failles que les sociétés de transfert doivent impérativement corriger C’est le véritable enjeu. Les sociétés comme Orange Money, Airtel Money, Nita Transfert et Amana Transfert d’Argent doivent revoir et renforcer leurs mécanismes de sécurité. La protection des comptes ne peut pas reposer uniquement sur la vigilance des utilisateurs. Lorsqu’un téléphone est volé, son propriétaire ne devrait pas se retrouver dans une situation où un individu peut vider son compte en quelques minutes simplement parce que l’appareil était déverrouillé ou que certaines protections étaient insuffisantes. Les applications doivent notamment imposer une authentification indépendante du code de déverrouillage du téléphone, renforcer la vérification biométrique et reconnaître les appareils habituellement utilisés par leurs clients. Toute connexion depuis un nouvel appareil devrait déclencher des vérifications supplémentaires. Il est également indispensable de mettre en place des systèmes capables de détecter les transactions inhabituelles, notamment plusieurs transferts successifs vers différents bénéficiaires en quelques minutes. En cas de comportement suspect, les opérations devraient pouvoir être temporairement suspendues. Autre mesure essentielle, permettre le blocage immédiat d’un compte depuis un autre téléphone ou par un simple appel au service client, avec une assistance réellement disponible 24 heures sur 24. Les changements de carte SIM et les réinitialisations de codes confidentiels doivent également faire l’objet de contrôles renforcés. Ces dispositifs ne sont pas de simples propositions théoriques. La GSMA documente déjà l’utilisation de l’intelligence artificielle pour détecter les comportements inhabituels et identifier les transactions suspectes en temps réel, notamment chez certains opérateurs africains. Elle souligne également l’intérêt des systèmes de vérification des numéros et de détection des changements de carte SIM. Ces sociétés devraient enfin réaliser régulièrement des audits indépendants de cybersécurité afin d’identifier les vulnérabilités de leurs applications et de leurs procédures internes. La BCEAO, les autorités nationales de régulation et les services de sécurité ont également un rôle important à jouer pour renforcer les contrôles et améliorer la coordination dans la lutte contre ces nouvelles formes de criminalité. Le Niger dispose déjà d’un cadre juridique avec la loi n° 2019-33 du 3 juillet 2019 portant répression de la cybercriminalité, modifiée en juin 2024. Il convient désormais de renforcer son application et les capacités d’investigation numérique. Le développement des services financiers numériques est une opportunité pour notre économie. Mais cette modernisation ne doit pas se faire au détriment de la sécurité des populations. Un citoyen qui travaille et économise doit pouvoir conserver son argent sur son compte sans craindre de perdre toutes ses économies à la suite du vol de son téléphone. La sécurité d’une application financière ne doit pas dépendre uniquement de la prudence de son utilisateur. Elle doit d’abord être garantie par les mécanismes de protection mis en place par son exploitant. Il est temps que les sociétés de transfert d’argent opérant au Niger prennent pleinement leurs responsabilités. La confiance des populations constitue leur principal capital. La protéger exige des investissements technologiques, des contrôles permanents et une véritable politique de prévention de la fraude. Par Ousmane Jazy L’article TRANSFERT D’ARGENT ET CYBERCRIMINALITÉ, L’URGENCE DE SÉCURISER NOS APPLICATIONS est apparu en premier sur Tamtaminfo .

items.title: Embattled Pentagon chief slams impeachment effort as 'farce'
items.description: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday denounced a push to impeach him as a “farce” and defended his record leading multiple military operations that have sparked allegations of misconduct against the Pentagon chief. Under pressure after President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance blamed the Iran war for the Republican Party’s sweeping losses in midterm elections, Hegseth now faces a congressional effort to remove him from office. “It’s a farce and it’s a stunt and everybody knows it,” a defiant Hegseth told journalists of the impeachment proceedings launched by Representative Thomas Massie, a Republican, the previous day. “What one disgruntled and defeated congressman is attempting is not oversight, and it’s not accountability. It’s a political spectacle,” Hegseth said. Massie, a fierce critic of Trump, is leaving office after losing a primary contest to a candidate backed by the president. Trump has backed Hegseth so far, and on Tuesday wrote on social media that the Pentagon chief “gets an ‘A’ plus, plus, plus for his defence” against the impeachment efforts. Hegseth on Tuesday defended military interventions in Yemen, Iran and Venezuela as well as strikes targeting alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific. ‘Would do it again’ “I stand behind every one of these operations. I was proud to execute them, and I would do it again tomorrow,” he said, equating the effort to remove him with an attack on US troops. “These resolutions tell every one of them that their service was a crime. Their service was not a crime. These are heroes,” said Hegseth. Several of the articles of impeachment relate to the Iran war, accusing Hegseth of violating the War Powers Resolution, which requires congressional consultation on US military interventions. Hegseth is a staunch defender of the widely unpopular war against Iran, which he has described as a “courageous and historic effort”. The 2025 conflict with Yemen’s Houthis also features in Massie’s articles of impeachment, which charge Hegseth with starting the operation without congressional approval and in the absence of an imminent threat to the United States. Massie also branded strikes on alleged drug-smuggling boats in the Caribbean and eastern Pacific as “extrajudicial killings” and said Hegseth “chilled independent legal review within the Department of Defence.” He also accused Hegseth of suppressing free speech by trying to punish Democratic Senator Mark Kelly over a video in which he and other lawmakers urged military and intelligence personnel to refuse illegal orders. “Using the powers of his office, Secretary Hegseth retaliated against and sought to intimidate United States Senator Mark Kelly for his statement,” one of the articles of impeachment said.

items.description: El último Consejo de Ministros ordinario de este Gobierno de coalición antes de que comience la campaña electoral ha aprobado un real decreto ley que refuerza la protección de determinadas familias. Se creará un título para las familias monoparentales , ahora mismo inexistente en el conjunto del país, y los hogares con un solo progenitor y dos hijos verán equiparados sus derechos a los considerados numerosos, por lo que podrán acceder al mismo nivel de ayudas públicas. items.title: 2027: Duke seeks opposition unity as PRP unveils manifesto
items.description: Presidential candidate of People’s Redemption Party (PRP), Mr Donald Duke, on Tuesday in Abuja unveiled his ‘A Compact for Nigeria’s Renewal’ manifesto. Duke, at the occasion, urged opposition parties to bridge their differences, not for personal ambition, but to safeguard the nation’s democratic foundations. He warned that repeating what he called the miscalculations of the 2023 elections in 2027 would bring ‘lasting shame’. “We erred in 2023, and we are repeating the same in 2027. It is said, Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me. The shame will certainly be on us,” he remarked. Duke called for an unconventional tactical thinking among opposition forces to counter what he termed an ‘unguarded political establishment’. “David did not defeat Goliath in a wrestling bout, but by strategy and unconventional means,” he stated. While building on the party’s strategic outlook, PRP National Chairman, Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, said the occasion served as a vital vehicle to transition the party from mere aspirations to governing reality. Baba-Ahmed praised the party’s presidential candidate and his running mate, Malam Sule Mohammed, alongside more than 500 other candidates. He described them as models of integrity, competence and courage designed to lead the nation out of its current economic and security quagmire. The national chairman acknowledged the immense challenges that plagued the party, including competing against incumbent politicians who relied on state power and immense financial resources. “We will find resistance from politicians who bribe our people for our future, while we ask for trust and the courage to choose quality and integrity,” he said. He also urged supporters to reject vote-buying, declaring, “Nigeria and Nigerians are not for sale. Baba-Ahmed outlined the party’s commitment to historic reforms, including what he termed a groundbreaking initiative that required all candidates to sign a binding compact with their constituents. “This agreement commits aspirants to unprecedented accountability, service and adherence to the foundational values of the 70-year-old progressive movement,” he said. While emphasising the party’s active role in the emerging Coalition for Democracy, Baba-Ahmed urged candidates to reject ‘politics as usual’ and campaign with sincerity, respect and an unwavering dedication to national redemption. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Duke, in an interview with newsmen shortly after the programme, also spoke on the state of the judiciary and the viability of an opposition coalition. According to him, a judge’s ruling is a reflection of their personal integrity and a test for the survival of democracy. “If you go to a match and you have a biased referee, then the integrity of the entire game is compromised,” the former Cross River governor stated. He, however, expressed hope that the newly-appointed jurists would act without fear or favour, reminding them that their decisions would shape the nation’s future. Duke also clarified that forming an alliance involved far more than simply selecting a presidential candidate. He stressed that the coalition must first establish a shared vision for the direction of the country to avoid repeating cycles of poor governance. While emphasising his commitment to democratic principles within any alliance, Duke noted, “You can’t call for a democrat and you’re not submitting to the rules and to the regulations of democracy.” He added that if the group reached a consensus on the best candidate to lead, he would gladly support them. “At the end of the day, I’m a sportsman about it,” the former governor said. Duke decried what he called severe systemic obstacles placed on the path of opposition parties trying to campaign, citing exorbitant advertising hurdles and, sometimes, restricted access to public venues. (NAN) The post 2027: Duke seeks opposition unity as PRP unveils manifesto appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GUTA calls for cheaper credit, lower business costs in 2027 Budget
items.description: The Ghana Union of Traders Associations (GUTA) has urged the government to introduce measures in the 2027 Budget to create a more enabling business environment, improve access to affordable credit and support private-sector job creation. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse ahead of the budget presentation on Thursday, November 12, Vice President of GUTA Joseph Paddy said businesses needed practical support to expand production and create employment. He questioned what specific incentives the government was putting in place to help businesses secure cheaper financing and invest in manufacturing. “What is the government putting in place for us? So that when I go to the bank, I’ll get cheaper credit, maybe a five-year moratorium to open a factory?” he asked. Mr Paddy also challenged perceptions that Ghana imports excessively, arguing that the focus should be on the nature of goods brought into the country and whether they support local production. He cited import-to-GDP figures for Singapore, Malaysia and Ghana to argue that importing is not inherently harmful to an economy. “So it’s not wrong to import in the country, but what are we importing? Are we importing for manufacturing concerns?” he said. He called for government support for businesses seeking to establish manufacturing and production facilities, saying this would help strengthen local industry. Mr Paddy further raised concerns about the cost of borrowing and charges imposed on imported goods at the ports, arguing that these expenses increase the cost of doing business. He claimed that the cumulative charges on imported goods could amount to about 55% of their value. “Just imagine you import goods worth about 100,000. You are paying about 55,000 just for duty,” he said. He argued that businesses ultimately pass these costs on to consumers through higher prices. The GUTA member also raised concerns about foreign businesses operating in Ghana’s retail sector, which he said is reserved for Ghanaians under the country’s investment laws. He called on the Finance Minister to introduce measures to protect local retailers and ensure that existing restrictions are enforced. The 2027 Budget is scheduled to be presented by Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson on Thursday, November 12, 2026.

items.title: 2027: Study our manifesto, judge us by promises kept – Presidency tells Nigerians
items.description: …As APC-PCC unveils 4-point manifesto, 8 priority areas By Soni Daniel (Editor, North), Emma Ujah (Bureau Chief, Abuja) & Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA The Presidency has urged Nigerians to study the past and current manifestoes of the ruling All Progressives Congress APC and judge the party by the promises it has kept since 2023, when it assumed power. The Chief of Staff to President Bola Tinubu, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, gave the charge on Tuesday in Abuja at the unveiling of the APC manifesto, titled ‘From Reforms to Prosperity’. He described the manifesto as a binding pact with the electorate. “A manifesto, in its strictest sense, is simply a contract between the people and their leaders. It is an inviolable contract, and we take the strict interpretation of what a manifesto represents as gospel under this administration,” he said. He admitted that the reforms had put real pressure on households, adding that the people living through it deserve to be heard. “Nobody should have to pretend that life is easy at the moment,” he said. The former House Speaker nonetheless defended President Bola Tinubu’s decision to act, saying Tinubu confronted the subsidy burden and a distorted foreign exchange system when he took responsibility for the country in 2023. “Leaving those problems untouched would have continued to weaken our ability to invest in the future. The difference between a politician and a leader is that while a politician thinks about the next election, a leader thinks about the next generation. And that is exactly what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has demonstrated,” Gbajabiamila said. 4 pillars The manifesto rests on four pillars: a secure and resilient nation; a better quality and more affordable life for every Nigerian; energy, infrastructure and economic growth; and effective and accountable governance. They are tied to the eight priority areas of the Renewed Hope Agenda, which the document says will be carried out on four foundations: macroeconomic stability, the rule of law, institutional capability and national cohesion. By 2031, the document commits to power generation scaled towards 10,000 megawatts, annual economic growth of 6 per cent, and youth unemployment and out-of-school children both halved. It also promises 20,000 additional teachers and health insurance expanded from more than 23 million enrollees to 40 per cent of Nigerians. Primary health centres would function in at least 90 per cent of facilities, up from the current 53 per cent. It further promises to work towards 200,000 homes under the Tinubu Mass Social Housing Scheme, Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN) mortgages and licensed private developers, tracked on a public dashboard. Gbajabiamila added that it commits the government to installing seven million additional electricity meters. He said the document would also expose the government’s own record to public inspection. “The manifesto commits us to publishing targets, identifying those responsible and reporting progress to the public. Citizens should be able to see where delivery is succeeding and where it is falling short,” he said. Gbajabiamila said the party would ask for the electorate’s mandate in 2027 and would earn it. “A party asking to continue in government must be prepared to answer to the people whose mandate it seeks. “The child studying tonight should have a fair chance of becoming the professional she hopes to be. The man opening his workshop tomorrow should be able to grow beyond the struggle to keep it open. Their ambitions deserve a country organised to help them succeed,” he stated. The Minister of Budget and Economic Planning, Atiku Bagudu, who chaired the APC 2027 Manifesto Unveiling Committee, said the administration had made progress but that more remained to be done. He cited the last Nigerian Economic Summit, where he said the private sector acknowledged that the President had delivered on his promises. “But, as we all know, even before anybody tells him, Mr President acknowledges that we have done well. However, until we deliver and ensure that every Nigerian feels the impact of prosperity, especially hard-working Nigerians and those who need support, we still have work to do,” Bagudu said. He recalled how Tinubu, during his campaign in Zamfara State, directed a State House official to give money to a struggling carrot seller. He cited it as evidence of the president’s concern for ordinary Nigerians. “So, Mr President, without being influenced by any outsider, we said we should confront our reality and address these challenges. As I have said, he was not concerned about the next election but about prosperity,” Bagudu said. The spokesperson of the APC Presidential Campaign Council (PCC) and Minister of Solid Minerals, Dele Alake, said the President removed the fuel subsidy and unified the foreign exchange market at a political cost to himself. “Regardless of the political consequences, or even the president’s own political situation and aspirations, he carried out genuine structural reforms,” he said. Alake alleged that powerful interests had exploited the subsidy regime and were resisting its removal. “It takes a man of courage, a man of grit, brains and brawn, to withstand the pressure of the cabal, which would fight back, and they are fighting back over the removal of fuel subsidy,” he said. On the exchange rate, he alleged that some people with connections to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) or top government officials obtained millions of dollars at the official rate. “In the twinkle of an eye, they would become billionaires while sitting in their backyards, making no contribution to production in the economy to shore up the naira. And, of course, the result, as you all knew, was a free fall,” he said. The Minister of Information, Mohammed Idris, answered critics who say only a few Nigerians benefit from the reforms. “When the road between Abuja and Kano is being constructed, I am not aware that anybody needs to show his ID card to prove that he belongs to the APC, is a rich man or belongs to a particular class before he can use it,” he said. On security, he said travellers on the Abuja-Kaduna road no longer have to ask whether bandits are still operating there. “Today, nobody asks such questions. You take your car from here to Kano without asking whether terrorists, bandits, kidnappers or whoever was operating along the road is still there. This was not the situation before,” he said. He pointed to the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND). “So, if you are looking for an example of Nigerians benefiting from these reforms, the 1.6 million young men and women and their parents are there. Nobody asks questions about their political affiliation,” he said. Idris added that the Financial Action Task Force had delisted Nigeria from its grey list and that headline and food inflation were both declining. “That is why we are saying today that, yes, we have laid the foundation for reforms, and we are progressively moving towards a period of prosperity. As I said, by 2031, it will be almost impossible for anybody to reverse this course,” he said. He also appealed to the media. “You do not have to like the administration of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu. You do not have to like him, but all of us must like Nigeria,” he said. items.title: Centre spent Rs5tr on devolved subjects in violation of Constitution, Senate panel head says
items.description: ISLAMABAD: The federal government spent more than Rs5 trillion on devolved provincial subjects and on ministries created on Council of Common Interests (CCI) matters in violation of the Constitution, the head of a Senate panel claimed on Tuesday. Citing data from the report of the Auditor General of Pakistan, Senator Barrister Zamir Hussain Ghumro, chairing a sub-committee of the Senate Functional Committee on Devolution, said the figure was equivalent to more than $18 billion. The convener said the country was facing twin issues of exorbitant federal expenditure and heavy borrowing totalling $135bn. “At present, federal government expenditure stands at around Rs19 trillion, while total tax and non-tax revenue was Rs20tr, leaving nothing for the provinces and forcing the federal government to resort to heavy borrowing,” Ghumro said. The PPP senator contended that had the government implemented the 18th Amendment , devolved provincial matters and handed over CCI matters to the permanent secretariat of the CCI as envisaged under Article 154 of the Constitution, the country would not have needed handouts from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). During the last 15 years, the IMF gave Pakistan $15bn, while the government spent $18bn to $20bn on devolved ministries and institutions, he claimed. “Had this amount been spent on infrastructure and social development, Pakistan would have been a different country. “A taxpayer’s hard-earned money had been consigned to unauthorised expenditure,” he added. The convener said the federal government makes two kinds of expenditure from the Federal Consolidated Fund: “charged expenditure” on remuneration and other perks of the president, Senate chair and deputy chair, National Assembly speaker and deputy speaker, auditor general, high court and Supreme Court judges; and debt servicing, which the NA does not vote on, and “other expenditure” in the form of demands for grants by federal ministries created on federal subjects. “It must not spend a penny on provincial or other purposes,” Senator Ghumro stressed. “This is taxpayers’ money paid to the federal government to be spent for the purposes and services rendered by the federal government under the Constitution. “The federal government is not obliged to provide health, education, housing, sanitation, water or other services for which the Constitution empowers provincial governments.” Senator Ghumro added: “A citizen cannot pay the federal government for purposes and services not rendered by it under the Constitution; hence such unauthorised expenditure of more than Rs5tr amounts to gross misuse of authority under the law and Constitution and must be accounted for legally.” He said neither the Ministry of Finance can send demands for grants for such expenditure nor the auditor general or Accountant General of Pakistan can authorise it. They have to see that the expenditure is for purposes and services to be provided by the federal government under the Constitution, he said. “Those matters are specifically mentioned in the Federal Legislative List . All powers under Article 142 are vested in the provinces except those enumerated for the federation in the Federal List.” Senator Ghumro said that, under Article 154 (functions and rules of procedure of CCI) read with Article 97 (extent of executive authority of federation), executive authority over subjects mentioned in the Federal Legislative List’s Part II is to be exercised by the CCI and not the federal cabinet. The convener noted that the CCI and Cabinet Division had sent summaries to the prime minister to abolish 24 ministries and institutions, thus curtailing federal expenditure, but the prime minister had yet to respond. He said that, even otherwise, such ministries would become redundant as the Auditor General of Pakistan and the finance ministry would not allow such expenditure. He directed the CCI and Cabinet Division to send a fresh note to the prime minister for abolition of ministries on provincial and CCI matters. In July, the Functional Committee on Devolution had expressed serious concerns over the re-establishment of federal ministries on subjects devolved to the provinces under the 18th Amendment. It had also constituted a sub-committee to examine the alleged violations. During a meeting of that sub-committee last month, senators sought a probe into a staggering Rs2.6 trillion expenditure by the federal government on education and health ministries. Provinces’ share in federal appointments The sub-committee also took up the matter of shares of provinces in federal appointments in ministries and corporations. The Establishment Division informed the committee that, as per its instructions, 5,000 jobs of Balochistan had been advertised to rectify its share as required under Article 38(g) of the Constitution. Senator Ghumro said the committee had identified a shortage of more than 30,000 jobs in Balochistan’s share, which must be filled. The convener noted that a shortage of more than 80,000 jobs had been pointed out in Sindh, and that positions must be advertised to rectify it. The Federal Public Service Commission secretary informed the sub-committee that appointments for the shares of Sindh and Balochistan in services would be expedited as they had cleared the earlier backlog. He said a special CSS examination was conducted for these provinces. The sub-committee observed that there was a meagre number of appointments of secretaries, CEOs and other high positions from Sindh and Balochistan. The convener said Article 38(g) envisages shares in all grades, and the federal government must submit a grade-wise position in grades 18 to 22 in 15 days. It must expedite the process through ministries in grades 1-15 positions, by FPSC in grades 16 and 17 positions and in grades 18 to 22 by the federal government and the prime minister. Compliance must be substantive and practical, he said. The Senate panel called for implementation, rather than “statements of intent”. It also expressed displeasure over the non-submission of a report by the information ministry, which had sought a month to devolve print media organisations and functions at the federal level and develop a mechanism to give broadcasting rights to provinces under Article 159 of the Constitution. It directed the ministry to finalise all issues in 15 days and submit compliance. ‘Highly sophisticated silver swapping case’ Meanwhile, a separate Senate panel was briefed by the Federal Investigation Agency’s (FIA) Anti-Corruption Circle on a coordinated multi-city operation in connection with the silver swapping and heist case earlier this year — involving alleged corruption, smuggling and suspected involvement of officials. Senator Saifullah Abro chaired a meeting of a sub-committee of the Senate Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control. The panel was informed that during the investigation, it was revealed that the suspects had allegedly adopted a systematic modus operandi involving fabrication of fake container seals, counterfeiting, substitution of genuine silver with lead bars and concealment of the stolen consignment. The investigation established that approximately 400 kilogrammes of silver had been swapped, out of which 214kg had so far been recovered, while the case involved an estimated financial loss of Rs4m. Legal proceedings had been initiated against the suspects, who were facing proceedings before competent courts. The FIA said the investigation was continuing through digital and financial forensics, asset tracing and other measures to identify all individuals involved and recover the remaining stolen silver. The Safe City director general explained that the theft had been carried out in a highly sophisticated and carefully planned manner. When the consignment reached Lahore, it was discovered that the original silver had been replaced with lead bars. He explained that one vehicle had initially been prepared for the operation. However, as it exited the airport, another identical vehicle approached from behind and carried out the swapping operation. The vehicle carrying the consignment was subsequently taken away. The entire sequence was detected through the Safe City surveillance system. Further investigation revealed that replica boxes had been prepared specifically for the operation, and the individual suspected of manufacturing and supplying these boxes was apprehended after four weeks. The Safe City DG also questioned the allegations of their involvement, stating that had they been involved, they would not have detected and exposed the swapping activity themselves. The chairman appreciated the FIA’s efforts and lauded the recovery of 214kg of silver. Abro remarked that the incident deserved to be made into a film. He suggested that if Sindh had a dedicated film-making wing, or a similar facility existed in Balochistan, a film should be produced highlighting the entire incident, particularly how the theft was planned and executed and how it was subsequently detected through the Safe City surveillance system. The meeting was attended by Senator Umer Farooq and senior officials from relevant ministries and departments. Records sought from FBR The panel led by Abro also ordered the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) to bring complete records of consumption certificates, payments and verification documents to an in-camera meeting on Nov 16, as it pursued the alleged misuse of the Fata/Pata tax exemption scheme involving imports worth Rs1,120bn and recovery of evaded taxes. The chairman expressed serious displeasure over the absence of the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency’s (NCCIA) DG, questioning the “non-serious” attitude of the authorities, particularly when it had already been decided in the previous meeting that the DG would brief the committee. During the briefing, representatives of FBR and FIA presented their respective positions. The FBR maintained that it had not received any formal notice from the court, whereas the FIA informed the committee that its legal adviser had received the relevant court order. Senator Abro and panel members expressed concern over the apparent lack of coordination and questioned why the FBR had remained unaware of the court proceedings for nearly two months. The committee was briefed on the reconciliation gap between Customs import data and consumption certificates for the period from 2018 to June 2026. It was informed that total imports amounted to Rs1,120.66 billion, against which consumption certificates covered imports worth Rs389.87bn, leaving an apparent unreconciled difference of Rs730.80bn. The sector-wise analysis revealed apparent differences of Rs148.25bn in steel, Rs146.96bn in textile/fabric, Rs100.88bnin food, and Rs76.49bn in ghee and oil. The committee emphasised the need for a comprehensive, transaction-wise reconciliation to ascertain the actual position and determine any potential tax liability or revenue loss. The FIA informed the committee that 512 notices had been issued to various companies in connection with the ongoing investigation, out of which 19 companies joined the proceedings with partial records, while more than 100 notices were returned or remained undelivered. The matter is under examination before the competent court, and proceedings are investigative in nature, aimed at obtaining relevant documents and explanations. Possible corruption, abuse of authority, diversion and wrongful release of securities are being independently examined in accordance with the law, the FIA added. Senator Abro said the committee had been pursuing the matter for a considerable period and the authorities must demonstrate seriousness and take concrete action instead of prolonging the proceedings. The panel was also briefed about the FBR’s reluctance to share relevant records with the parliamentary committee, particularly when the department was prepared to provide information to the court and other authorities. Senator Saifullah Abro chairs a meeting of a sub-committee of the Senate Standing Committee on Interior and Narcotics Control on Nov 10, 2026. — Senate of Pakistan/Website Referring to Article 66 of the Constitution, Senator Abro asked the FBR to clarify the authorities to whom such records could legally be disclosed. The members stressed that parliamentary oversight must be respected and that legal provisions should not be used to delay accountability. The chairman sought a comprehensive explanation of the certificates, the amounts released against them and the supporting documentation. He particularly highlighted 20 certificates involving approximately Rs64bn and directed the FBR to provide complete details, including records and justification for their issuance. He further referred to the terms of reference concerning approximately Rs74bn and questioned the release of payments without adequate verification and scrutiny. Expressing serious concern over the financial implications, the chairman observed that the alleged tax liability associated with the matter could be substantial and that the state must recover every rupee legally due. He referred to an estimated amount of Rs1,120bn and stressed that the FBR must ensure proper assessment and recovery of applicable taxes. Senator Abro directed the FBR to examine the relevant Statement of Requirements (SOR) issued in 2021 and investigate whether the consumption certificates and subsequent releases had been processed in accordance with the applicable legal framework. The chairman also raised concerns regarding the large number of companies and petitioners involved in the proceedings and directed the FBR to examine the list of petitioners, verify their respective positions and issue notices wherever necessary. Referring to reports of individuals possessing substantial assets, large convoys of vehicles and unexplained sources of income, Senator Abro urged the FBR to investigate possible financial irregularities and money laundering. The members stressed that the investigation must also examine financial trails and possible involvement of influential individuals and networks. The committee further discussed the alleged movement and importation of tobacco-related material through the Fata/Pata exemption regime and its subsequent use by companies operating outside the exempted areas. The chairman observed that the issue involved a substantial loss to the national exchequer and required coordinated action by the FIA, FBR, Customs and other enforcement agencies. He directed the authorities to provide complete import records from January 2018 onwards, particularly details of consignments, their movement, destinations and companies involved. He also sought details of companies involved in importing material without payment of applicable taxes and directed Customs authorities to furnish records of imports through Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and former Fata areas, particularly for the period after June 2026. He emphasised the need to examine the tracking and movement of containers and to identify any misuse of the exemption mechanism through companies established in other parts of the country. The committee was informed that a significant number of companies had already been referred to the FIA for investigation, while further cases remained under examination. The chairman stressed that the investigation must be pursued without “fear or favour”, observing that the money involved belonged to the people of Pakistan. He also emphasised that wherever law-and-order constraints prevented officials from accessing certain factories, assistance of law enforcement agencies should be sought. The chairman directed that the next meeting, scheduled for Nov 16, be held in camera to examine sensitive financial and investigative records. The FBR was directed to bring complete details of all consumption certificates issued from Nov 2025 onwards, along with corresponding payments, pay orders, supporting documents and verification records. The authorities were also directed to provide complete details of the remaining companies under investigation without further delay. Furthermore, the KP Customs authorities were given four to five working days to furnish the required import and movement records, taking into account different routes and customs regimes through which consignments had been processed. The chairman directed that all relevant information be compiled and presented before the committee in the next in-camera meeting.

items.title: Soutien aux orphelins des FDS : L’Initiative Pananetugri remet des kits scolaires aux orphelins
items.description: L’Initiative Pananetugri pour le bien-être de la femme (IPBF) a remis à la direction de l'action sociale et des services psychologiques de la gendarmerie Nationale (DASSP-GN) du Burkina 215 kits scolaires au profit des enfants des soldats tombés au front. C’était le vendredi 9 octobre 2026. « Malgré la modestie de ce don, il va encourager, favoriser l'accès à l'éducation des orphelins des FDS tombés au front » a souligné la directrice exécutive adjointe de l’IPBF, Tégawendé Astrid Larissa Sondé A l’occasion de la rentrée scolaire 2026-2027, l’Initiative Pananetugri pour le bien-être de la Femme (IPBF) fait parler son cœur à l’endroit des enfants des soldats tombés au front. Le 9 octobre 2026 dernier à Ouagadougou, elle a remis des kits scolaires d’une valeur de 2 500 000FCFA à la direction de l'action sociale et des services psychologiques de la gendarmerie Nationale (DASSP-GN). Le directeur de l'action sociale et de la cellule psychologique de la Gendarmerie nationale, Maurice Darga a confié que ce geste est un soulagement pour les tuteurs en cette période de rentrée scolaire. Selon la directrice exécutive adjointe de l'Initiative, Tégawendé Astrid Larissa Sondé, ce sont 215 kits scolaires qui seront distribués aux enfants du primaire et du secondaire. « Par ce geste, l’initiative veut réitérer leur soutien et leur engagement aux côtés des autorités et des familles. Ce don va encourager, favoriser l'accès à l'éducation des orphelins des FDS » a-t-elle dit. Elle a salué le travail consentit par la cellule de l’action sociale de la Gendarmerie nationale qui au-delà de l'accompagnement psychologique contribue au soutien les familles face aux épreuves. « Prendre soin de ceux et celles qui servent notre pays, c'est aussi prendre soin de leur famille. La solidarité doit être concrète et doit contribuer à renforcer la résilience et le bien-être des communautés » a-t-elle indiqué. Le directeur de l'action sociale et de la cellule psychologique de la Gendarmerie nationale, Maurice Darga a remercié IPBF pour son geste de solidarité envers ces orphelins. « Un sac, un cahier, un stylo, cela peut sembler modeste, mais pour ces familles, c'est un chemin de l'école qui s'ouvre. C'est l'espoir d'un avenir, c'est la preuve que le sacrifice de leurs parents n'est pas resté vain » a-t-il confié. Il a formulé le vœu que ce partenariat se poursuive, qu'il grandisse et se traduise par d'autres actions concrètes au service du bien-être des veuves et des orphelins. Fleur BIRBA Aïssatou DIARRA(Stagiaire)

items.title: TV anchor's killing: Court extends physical remand of victim's husband by 4 days
items.description: RAWALPINDI: The physical remand of the husband of anchorperson Rabia Ahsan, who was shot dead at home in the Gulshanabad area earlier in the week, was extended by four days by a court on Tuesday. The suspect, Ahsan, was produced before Senior Civil Judge Muhammad Nasrullah Wattoo on Tuesday after completion of his one-day physical remand . During the hearing, the investigating officer informed the court about the progress made in the investigation. He urged the court to extend the remand by seven days in order to interrogate the suspect and complete the investigation. After examining the record and hearing the accused, the court observed that he had been nominated in the first information report (FIR) and that a pistol had also been recovered from him. The court subsequently extended the remand by four days to facilitate the investigation and directed the investigating officer to produce the accused on Nov 14. The court also directed the police to complete the investigation and submit the relevant record. No lawyer appeared on behalf of the suspect during Tuesday’s proceedings. Meanwhile, it emerged that police had decided to conduct a polygraph (lie-detector) test of the suspect, amid alleged inconsistencies in his statements during the investigation. According to the application seeking his physical remand, the polygraph test was scheduled to be conducted at the Punjab Forensic Science Agency (PFSA) in Lahore on Wednesday (Nov 11). Investigators expected to receive its report on Saturday, which they said may help them establish the circumstances surrounding the shooting. Rabia, who was associated with 92 News and had previously co-hosted a current affairs programme with senior journalists Amir Mateen and Rauf Klasra, was shot dead at her residence in the Gulshanabad area on Nov 8. According to the FIR registered at Saddar Beruni police station on the complaint of her brother, Khurram Ahmed, the victim’s mother and sister were present at the house when they heard a gunshot from the bedroom. The complainant stated that his sister, who was living at the house along with their mother, rushed towards the bedroom after hearing the gunshot and found Rabia lying on the floor in a pool of blood. Her husband was allegedly standing nearby, holding a pistol. Meanwhile, amid reports that the complainant had decided to withdraw the murder case, a senior officer told Dawn that it was now up to the trial court to decide whether to accept the request to withdrawal the case, if such a request was filed.

items.title: Finance Ministry considers $80m settlement to revive Teshie desalination plant
items.description: The Finance Ministry has indicated that the government will assume the full financial cost of settling the contractual dispute over the Teshie desalination plant, Executive Secretary of the Public Utilities Regulatory Commission (PURC), Dr Shafic Suleman, has disclosed. The disclosure follows an arbitration ruling ordering Ghana Water Limited (GWL) to pay US$235 million to Befesa Desalination Developments Ghana Limited, the company operating the facility, over a dispute arising from the termination of a water purchase agreement. Speaking on the Citi Breakfast Show on Tuesday, November 10, Dr Suleman said discussions with the company had resulted in an indication that it was willing to accept about US$80 million to settle the dispute and pave the way for the resumption of operations. He said GWL was initially expected to raise US$10 million towards the settlement, but Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Forson had subsequently indicated that government would take up the entire cost. “They said Ghana Water should raise about US$10 million. We have tried our best, but the Finance Minister has indicated that government will take up the entire cost,” he said. Dr Suleman expressed hope that the Finance Minister would make a financial commitment to the company before the end of the year to enable it to resume operations. “We are hoping that, by the grace of God, the Finance Minister can at least make some commitment to the company by the end of the year so they can commence operations,” he added. He confirmed that the facility was capable of operating and would be handed over entirely to GWL for management once the outstanding issues had been resolved. However, he raised concerns about GWL’s capacity to manage the plant effectively in the long term, although he expressed confidence in the technical expertise of its workforce. The dispute followed the termination of a water purchase agreement between GWL and Befesa Desalination Developments Ghana Limited, which is 95 per cent owned by Spanish infrastructure group Cox. Cox announced on September 21 that an International Chamber of Commerce arbitration tribunal had issued two final decisions on September 17, ordering GWL to pay US$235 million, net of taxes. Interest on the award has been accruing since April 1, 2026, until payment is made.

items.title: Wa Naa pledges support for nationwide awareness of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund
items.description: The Wa Naa, His Majesty Fuseini Seidu Pelpuo IV, has called for greater public awareness of the Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF), describing the initiative as a major step towards helping families access expensive specialised healthcare services. The traditional ruler gave the endorsement when the Fund’s Administrator, Adjoa Obuobia Darko-Opoku, and her delegation paid a courtesy call on him during their stakeholder engagement tour of the Upper West Region. He welcomed the decision to take information about the Fund to communities outside the major cities and pledged the cooperation of traditional authorities in educating residents about the programme and helping eligible patients benefit from its support. During the engagement, Ms Darko-Opoku explained that the Fund was established to ease the financial difficulties patients face in seeking treatment for non-communicable diseases, particularly cancer, kidney disease and cardiovascular conditions. She underscored the need for traditional leaders to help bridge information gaps in their communities, noting that eligible patients must be made aware of the assistance available to them, irrespective of where they live.

items.title: Getting Too Close to Trump Was a Mistake
items.description: O ver the past week , following MAGA’s significant losses in the midterms, I have been asked the same questions again and again: How could Silicon Valley have gotten it so wrong? Why did tech leaders not anticipate the consequences of joining themselves at the hip to MAGA straight after Donald Trump won reelection in 2024? What follows is not a critique of the individual tech leaders themselves—some were more restrained than others—nor is it a personal commentary on Mark Zuckerberg, my former boss. I take it as given that they all acted in what they saw as the interests of their own companies. Rather, my critique is of a herd mentality in the Valley that, in this important instance, led to such a serious and wholly predictable misjudgement. It is especially interesting to try and understand why this happened because, measured against their own stated reasons for the great pivot, it has been a near total failure. Three main reasons were given for it at the time. [ Read: Silicon Valley’s very bad night ] First, tech leaders said that uniting the power of Washington and Silicon Valley would help America in its fight with China for AI supremacy. Yet over the past 18 months, China has been closing the gap with the United States by most objective measures, including model performance and chip development. In some important respects, China has outpaced America altogether, deploying open-weight models faster, developing a more sustainable energy strategy, and training world-class researchers and engineers at larger scale. Second, Silicon Valley leaders said that partnering with the government would help assuage public concerns about AI and overcome the “woke” opposition to Big Tech. Yet societal attitudes towards AI in the U.S. are much more negative now than they ever were under President Biden, and worse than almost anywhere else on the planet. Fostering the very backlash they claimed they were trying to confront is a peculiar triumph of hubris and incompetence. Third, tech executives hoped that earning Trump’s good graces would allow them to avoid unwelcome regulatory incursions outside the U.S., especially in Europe. The Trump administration has undoubtedly helped with this in some ways. For example, Commerce Secretary Lutnick has become an important ally for tech leaders trying to fight a number of EU enforcement decisions. But by any other meaningful measure the approach has been a disaster: Anti–Big Tech, and (alas) anti-American, sentiment has never been higher in large parts of the world, and most major economies—including Canada, India, Germany and Brazil—are now scrambling to have less, not more, of what Silicon Valley produces. Since pivoting to Trump, then, Silicon Valley’s scorecard looks something like this: chief rival (China) strengthened; domestic support weakened; global markets infuriated. Having played a peripheral part in some of the discussions at the time—I announced my (not wholly unrelated) departure from Meta as its head of global affairs a few days before Trump’s 2024 inauguration, when the Valley-MAGA union was consummated—I see several reasons why this extraordinary miscalculation occurred: FOMO . In 2024, Elon Musk spent election night at Mar-a-Lago. The sight of one tech leader—especially someone as intimidating to his peers as Musk—backslapping Trump and his entourage galvanized all the others to do the same. The idea that one of their rivals in the cutthroat race for AI supremacy might be able to strike a deal with the highly transactional clique around Trump was clearly too much for them to bear. They all wanted to be there, in case they got left out. Payback . Tech leaders had a lot to be angry about in the run-up to Trump’s reelection. Some felt unfairly treated by traditional media, academia, and cultural elites. Conservatives had long felt unwelcome in the Valley’s traditionally liberal milieu. The Biden administration had clumsily vilified tech leaders rather than work with them on policy and regulation. These factors created a large group of powerful, wealthy, and offended individuals. Stepping into the Trump tent seemed like a good way to even the score. Misunderstanding politics . As someone who spent nearly two decades in elected office and has spent much of my time since working in and around tech, I am always struck how eagerly smart and wealthy people expound on subjects about which they know very little—especially politics. Their commercial success seems to foster in them a view that politics is easy, if only dim-witted officeholders would listen to them. It is this hubris which makes the Valley such an exhilarating and exasperating place. Tech hype cycles . One of the most basic mistakes the tech community makes is to apply their own hype-driven perspective to politics. That’s why so many tech leaders interpreted Trump’s 2024 victory—which was narrow in terms of the popular vote—as a mandate to carry out a sweeping ideological agenda. But voters hate when politicians take their support for granted by pursuing zealous policies that they didn’t feel they voted for. The Brexiteers made the same error in the UK, using a wafer-thin majority in the referendum to impose a hardline interpretation of it. Now a significant majority of Brits think Brexit was a huge mistake. In the same way, many U.S. voters abhor the self-serving cliquiness and extremism of the second Trump administration, and particularly its apparent indifference to their own economic plight. For them, the government’s cozy relationship with the Valley is a significant part of the problem. The pendulum always swings . Many of the tech CEOs who wanted to attach themselves to Trump seemed to think that his victory marked a permanent political shift—that the pendulum would never swing back. So they immediately doubled down. Such decisiveness can be an asset when betting on fast-moving technological trends. But in politics, it’s a hindrance to understanding longer-term societal and political realities. The VC bros . Starting around 2020, an influential set of venture capitalists, including Marc Andreessen and David Sacks, became protagonists in the American culture wars, focusing on what they saw as a conspiracy between the Biden Administration and the big content platforms to censor conservatives, especially during the Covid pandemic. Many of them funded pro-crypto campaigns in the 2024 election cycle, and their success in defeating some prominent pro-regulation candidates apparently went to their heads. They thought that success on a single issue (regulation of the crypto industry) about which most voters didn’t care less, was a blueprint for how they—and, crucially, how the tech sector as a whole—should play for bigger stakes in politics. But there is a world of difference between VC leaders acting on their personal ideological proclivities —on both the right and the left—and executives of major tech platforms doing so. The former should be free to promote their views and spend their money on any cause they wish, in part because they are not themselves building consequential companies but simply investing in them. (I work in VC myself nowadays.) But if you are the leader of a company producing technology that you claim is of immense and disruptive societal significance, your partisan political engagement should be much more restrained. [ From the June 2026 issue: The venture-capital populist ] Why does any of this matter? Why should anyone care that a handful of powerful tech executives messed up trying to play politics? I believe that AI still has the potential to serve humanity’s interests instead of becoming its master. But that potential will only be realized if we have smart, thoughtful people in both Silicon Valley and Washington prepared to work together regardless of partisan allegiance to help spread the technology’s benefits across society. The transactional alliance we have seen over the last couple of years couldn’t be further from that ideal. The Democrats now have every incentive to make life as uncomfortable as they can for Trump-supporting tech leaders. This might discourage them from seeking to skew future elections to suit their own interests. But it could also lead to a cycle of retribution that would be bad for Silicon Valley, bad for innovation, and ultimately bad for Democrats too. Major companies involved in making technologies upon which we all depend are best served by staying out of party politics. Trying to ride the political whiplash from one cycle to the next is a fool’s game. Not long ago, Silicon Valley leaders used to be on the side of individual empowerment regardless of which party was in charge. That was always a more noble calling than opportunistically joining whichever side of the political elite happens to be winning at any one time. Tech leaders should commit to maintaining open, productive relationships with whoever is in power in the future, regardless of party ideology. For their own sake and ours, they should get out of the game of picking political winners and losers.
