items.title: Cholera killed more than 3,000 this year – WHO
items.description: Cholera has killed more than 3,000 people worldwide since the start of the year, the World Health Organization said Tuesday, insisting its goal of cutting global cases by 90 percent by 2030 remained in reach. The disease killed nearly 7,900 people in 2025, making it “the deadliest year for cholera since 1999”, according to Lorenzo Pezzoli, WHO lead for epidemic-prone bacterial diseases. While data for the first nine months of 2026 show a decline in deaths, more than 3,000 people have still died from the preventable and treatable diarrheal infection, he said, with “nearly nine out of 10 of them in Africa”. The WHO also warned that the current El Nino weather pattern could worsen outbreaks, as cholera can be fuelled by both flooding and water shortages. The UN health agency and the vaccine alliance, Gavi, aim to reduce global cholera cases by 90 percent by 2030 through mass vaccination campaigns and improved access to clean water and sanitation. Although cholera was eliminated from high-income countries generations ago thanks to safe drinking water and modern sewage systems, it can still “kill within a matter of hours” if left untreated, Pezzoli said, despite being “easy and inexpensive to treat” with existing medicines. “The 2030 goal is achievable because the work is already under way,” Pezzoli added, pointing to the International Coordinating Group (ICG) on Vaccine Provision, which last year approved the supply of 71 million doses, funded by Gavi. Vaccines and rapid diagnostic tests are also reaching outbreak zones more quickly, helping health workers detect and respond to infections earlier. WHO and its partners are helping countries identify districts where cholera repeatedly resurfaces and develop response plans. Seven countries — Angola, Bangladesh, the DR Congo, Nigeria, South Sudan, Sudan and Yemen — accounted for about 90 percent of global cases and deaths last year. “The collective response is undeniably bearing fruit, but… it remains insufficient,” Pezzoli said. “We must redouble our efforts to help all these countries reach the elimination goal which means ensuring that, by 2030, cholera no longer poses a public health threat in any of them.” The post Cholera killed more than 3,000 this year – WHO appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: F-35 : un rapport américain révèle des défaillances dans le suivi de 31 milliards de dollars de pièces détachées et des pertes colossales non élucidées
items.description: Le Pentagone est une nouvelle fois mis en cause pour de graves lacunes dans la gestion du programme F-35. Selon un rapport du Government Accountability Office (GAO), l'organisme de controle du Congres americain, rendu public le 9 novembre, le ministere americain de la Defense ne parvient pas a assurer un suivi fiable de quelque 26 millions de pieces detachees, representant une valeur totale de 31 milliards de dollars. Les stocks sont destines a l'entretien des chasseurs F-35, developpes par le groupe americain Lockheed Martin. Allant de simples boulons aux moteurs, les composants sont repartis sur plus de 700 sites dans le monde, notamment dans des installations militaires et chez des sous-traitants. Les auditeurs constatent que les registres du Pentagone sont incomplets et que les inventaires ne permettent pas de verifier les quantites reellement disponibles. Plus de 85 millions de dollars de pertes toujours inexpliquees Les defaillances ne se limitent pas a la tenue des inventaires. Le Pentagone reste incapable de clarifier le sort de composants representant plus de 85 millions de dollars de pertes, pourtant signalees par les auditeurs des 2023. En mars 2026, soit pres de trois ans apres les premieres alertes, le bureau charge du programme F-35 ne disposait toujours pas des informations necessaires pour etablir ce qu'etait devenu le materiel. Les pertes concernent plus d'un million de pieces recensees entre mai 2018 et octobre 2022 chez un important sous-traitant. Elles englobent aussi des composants endommages ou detruits et ne correspondent donc pas uniquement a du materiel disparu. Le GAO pointe en outre l'insuffisance des procedures destinees a enqueter sur les pertes et a determiner les responsabilites. En l'absence de controles efficaces, le ministere ne peut en mesurer precisement l'ampleur. Une telle situation accroît les risques de fraude, de gaspillage et de detournement de materiel. Des avertissements repetes, des progres minimes Les faiblesses s'etendent au fonctionnement meme du systeme de suivi. Les informations fournies par les principaux sous-traitants sont integrees a partir de rapports trimestriels, ce qui peut entraîner des retards de plus de trois mois. En mars 2026, quelque 17 000 pieces en maintenance ou en reparation, representant pres de 1,3 milliard de dollars, ne figuraient pas dans la base de donnees concernee. Les dysfonctionnements perdurent malgre plusieurs annees d'avertissements. Le GAO souligne le caractere ancien des problemes de comptabilite et de suivi financier du programme. Depuis 2019, le Pentagone n'a accompli que des progres minimes dans l'application des recommandations formulees par les auditeurs pour y remedier. Les consequences pourraient depasser le seul cadre financier. Selon l'organisme de controle, de telles insuffisances risquent d'affecter la disponibilite operationnelle des F-35. Elles contribuent aussi aux difficultes persistantes du ministere a faire certifier ses comptes. Le nouveau rapport met ainsi en lumiere les problemes de gestion d'un projet militaire deja marque par des retards et des depassements de coûts. Le F-35 demeure le programme d'armement le plus coûteux de l'histoire du Pentagone. Selon les estimations du GAO, son coût total sur l'ensemble de son cycle de vie pourrait approcher les 2 000 milliards de dollars.

items.title: Senate donates N100m to Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, Flamingos
items.description: The Senate has announced a donation of N100 million to Nigeria’s Under-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Rabat, Morocco. The Senate President announced the donation during plenary on Tuesday while presiding over a motion moved by Sen. Abdul Ningi (ADC-Bauchi Central) on the need to congratulate the victorious girls on their achievement. Ningi described the victory as historic, noting that the young players had achieved what several other Nigerian national teams had struggled to accomplish. He said the team’s triumph was particularly remarkable, given the limited expectations that surrounded the players before the competition. The senator expressed concern that the achievement had not received adequate publicity and national recognition, adding that the players deserved to be celebrated for bringing honour to Nigeria and Africa. He also expressed concern that the team did not receive sufficient official recognition upon its arrival in the country. Seconding the motion, Sen. Adams Oshiomhole (APC-Edo North) commended the team for defeating Japan in the final, describing the victory as evidence of the potential and determination of Nigerian youths. Oshiomhole urged Nigerians to appreciate the country’s achievements rather than constantly focusing on its challenges. He also appealed to the Senate leadership to make a donation to the team to support the players’ educational needs alongside their sporting careers. The senate thereafter adopted Ningi’s prayers, congratulating President Bola Tinubu for his support for sports development, Nigerians on the historic victory, and the leadership of the National Sports Commission, particularly its Chairman, Shehu Dikko. It also urged the federal government to provide adequate compensation and rewards for the players in recognition of their achievement. Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, in his remarks, said the victory was a significant achievement for Nigeria and Africa, particularly as the Flamingos defeated football nations, including Brazil and Japan. Akpabio urged the federal government to adequately reward the players and called on the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) to sustain the team and continue developing the players for future competitions. The senate president also appealed to wealthy and sports-loving Nigerians to support the players and encourage other young people to participate in sports. He noted that the N100 million donation by the National Assembly was intended to recognise the players’ achievement and encourage them to continue bringing honour to the country. “I want to commend the Flamingos, the Under-17 youth team of Nigeria, for defeating major countries such as Brazil and Japan to win the Under-17 World Cup for Africa for the first time and for Nigeria. “We also urged, and we pray that the federal government will recognise these children accordingly and give them adequate rewards. “The Nigerian Football Federation, under its leadership, should see the need to keep these children together and develop them further,” Akpabio said. He congratulated the players, the Senate Committee on Sports and all Nigerians on the historic victory. (NAN) The post Senate donates N100m to Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, Flamingos appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Dangote storms Ghana as President Mahama, GIPA’s Madjie lead Investment Summit on November 16-17, 2026
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama’s declaration that Ghana is open for business will take centre stage as the country prepares to host more than 2,000 investors, business leaders, policymakers, diplomats and development partners at the maiden Invest Ghana Summit 2026. The two-day summit, scheduled for November 16–17 at the Kempinski Hotel Gold Coast City in Accra, will bring together local and international stakeholders to explore investment opportunities, facilitate business partnerships and connect investors with projects across Ghana’s 16 regions. Convened by the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA) under the patronage of President Mahama, the summit comes as government intensifies efforts to attract investments that expand industrial production, create sustainable jobs, promote technology transfer and strengthen local supply chains. The summit is under the theme, “Investing in Ghana’s New Economy: Building a Productive Economy that Creates Value and Competes Globally,”. It seeks to shift the investment conversation beyond attracting capital to securing investments that strengthen businesses, expand production and create lasting economic value. Mahama and Dangote to headline investment discussions President Mahama will officially open the summit with a keynote address on “Championing Africa’s Business Prospects through Investing in Ghana.” A major highlight will be a fireside conversation between the President and Aliko Dangote, Founder and Chief Executive of the Dangote Group, on “Building Business Prosperity in Africa in Furtherance of the African Union’s Agenda 2063.” Mr Dangote will also deliver a special address on “Industrializing Africa: Building on African Ingenuity to Industrialize the Continent.” Their participation places industrialisation, African enterprise development and regional economic integration at the centre of the discussions. The opening ceremony will also feature the Minister for Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Madam Elizabeth Ofosu-Adjare, on Ghana’s industrialisation agenda, and Finance Minister Dr Cassiel Ato Baah Forson on the economic outlook and government’s New Economy Programme. Completed investment mapping puts regional opportunities in focus A major development ahead of the summit is GIPA’s completed Investment Opportunities Mapping Project (IOMP), which identifies, documents and showcases investment opportunities across all 16 regions. The project gives the Authority a structured basis for presenting Ghana’s investment potential beyond established commercial centres and connecting regional opportunities with local and international capital. Its focus includes agriculture, agro-processing, manufacturing, tourism, infrastructure and other productive sectors. For communities across Ghana, attracting investment can mean more than the establishment of new businesses. It can create markets for farmers, expand opportunities for local entrepreneurs, strengthen small and medium-sized enterprises and provide employment for young people. Investment in agro-processing, for instance, can help farmers find reliable buyers for their produce, while access to capital and technology can help local manufacturers expand production and compete in wider markets. The second day will focus particularly on regional prospects. The Minister for Local Government, Chieftaincy and Religious Affairs, Mr Mahama Ayariga, is scheduled to address investment opportunities across the regions. Three regional investment deep-dive sessions, covering groups of five, five and six regions, will allow participants to examine opportunities and engage prospective investors. AfCFTA: Positioning Ghana to serve Africa The African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) Investment Breakfast will feature a keynote address by Secretary-General of the AfCFTA Secretariat, Mr Wamkele Mene, on the theme “Produce in Ghana, Serve Africa.” The session will examine how Ghana can leverage its position as host of the AfCFTA Secretariat to attract investment into manufacturing, processing and export-oriented businesses. The continental free trade arrangement offers businesses access to a wider African market, creating opportunities for Ghana to attract investors interested in producing locally and serving consumers across the continent. From investment opportunities to actual deals A defining feature of the summit will be its focus on deal-making. The Ghana Deal Room, Investor Facilitation Hub and Priority Investor Facilitation Clinic will provide platforms for engagement between investors, project promoters, financiers, technical partners and government institutions. The programme also includes memorandum of understanding, investment agreements, partnership signings and investment announcements. Other sessions will examine fintech and the future of financial services, diaspora investment and the factors investors consider when assessing projects. The fintech discussion will feature the Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Mr Samuel Nartey George, and Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama. An investor reverse-pitch session will also give investors, development finance institutions, funds and banks an opportunity to outline the projects and businesses they are looking to support. Madjie champions a new investment narrative GIPA Chief Executive Officer, Mr Simon Madjie says Ghana’s investment drive must focus on building industries, adding value to local resources, strengthening Ghanaian enterprises, expanding exports and creating sustainable jobs. Speaking at the summit’s media launch, Mr Madjie said Ghana was at a pivotal moment as it pursued economic reforms, industrialisation and opportunities arising from the AfCFTA. He said the country’s investment narrative must reflect its ambition to build a prosperous and self-reliant economy that contributes to Africa’s economic transformation. “This narrative must reflect not only the opportunities Ghana offers investors, but also our longstanding aspiration to build a prosperous and self-reliant economy that contributes meaningfully to Africa’s economic transformation,” he said. Mr Madjie is expected to present the summit’s outcomes and next steps, outlining GIPA’s approach to sustaining investor engagement and advancing partnerships established during the event. Ghana Club 100 to follow summit The summit will be followed on November 18 by the 22nd Ghana Club 100 Awards at The Palms Convention Centre in Accra. Established in 1998, the awards recognise leading Ghanaian companies for corporate performance, innovation, growth and contribution to national economic development. The awards complement the investment summit by showcasing domestic businesses that can serve as partners for international capital and contribute to employment and economic growth. Both events are being organised in partnership with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness and Industry, Ghana Export Promotion Authority, Ghana Free Zones Authority and Bank of Ghana, with support from public institutions and private-sector partners. Turning openness into investment The success of the maiden Invest Ghana Summit will ultimately depend on what follows the two days of discussions. For Ghana, attracting investment must translate into expanded production, stronger local businesses, technology transfer, sustainable employment and opportunities across all 16 regions. With the IOMP completed, GIPA has a foundation for presenting the country’s regional investment potential. The summit offers an opportunity to connect those opportunities with investors capable of financing and developing viable projects. For Simon Madjie and his team, the challenge will be to sustain investor interest and help move promising opportunities towards implementation. Ultimately, Ghana’s open-for-business message will mean most when it is reflected not only in investment announcements, but in factories operating, businesses expanding, products reaching new markets and people finding decent employment.

items.title: Anthropic dévoile Fable 5.2, un modèle d’IA plus puissant et moins cher
items.description: Anthropic poursuit sa course à l’intelligence artificielle avec le lancement de Fable 5.2, une nouvelle version de son modèle de pointe présentée comme plus performante et moins coûteuse que la précédente. L’annonce intervient à quelques jours de l’entrée en Bourse très attendue de la start-up américaine, créatrice de l’assistant Claude. Dévoilé lundi 9 novembre, Fable 5.2 sera accessible au grand public. Anthropic présente cette nouvelle génération comme une amélioration significative de son modèle d’intelligence artificielle, alors que la société évolue dans un secteur de plus en plus concurrentiel, notamment face à OpenAI et Google. Avec Fable 5.2, Anthropic cherche à renforcer sa position sur le marché de l’IA générative en proposant un modèle à la fois plus performant et moins coûteux. Cette stratégie intervient alors que les principaux acteurs du secteur multiplient les lancements et cherchent à rendre leurs technologies toujours plus accessibles. Le nouveau modèle sera disponible pour les utilisateurs, contrairement à Mythos 5.2, développé parallèlement par Anthropic et soumis à des restrictions beaucoup plus importantes. Mythos 5.2 réservé à certaines organisations Anthropic a également dévoilé Mythos 5.2, une version conçue pour être moins bridée sur certaines requêtes sensibles, notamment dans les domaines de la cybersécurité et de la biologie. Contrairement à Fable 5.2, Mythos 5.2 ne sera toutefois pas ouvert au grand public. Son accès sera limité à une sélection d’organisations, sur fond de préoccupations croissantes concernant les risques liés à l’utilisation de modèles d’IA particulièrement puissants dans des domaines sensibles. Cette différence entre les deux modèles illustre les précautions prises par Anthropic face aux capacités croissantes de l’intelligence artificielle, notamment lorsqu’elles peuvent être utilisées dans des secteurs présentant des risques en matière de sécurité. Une annonce stratégique avant Wall Street Le calendrier de ce lancement n’est pas anodin. Anthropic doit prochainement faire son entrée à Wall Street, une opération qui pourrait figurer parmi les plus importantes introductions en Bourse du secteur technologique. La start-up devra convaincre les investisseurs de sa capacité à poursuivre sa croissance dans un marché particulièrement concurrentiel, alors que les valeurs technologiques connaissent récemment des turbulences. Avec Fable 5.2, Anthropic entend donc afficher ses ambitions technologiques tout en mettant en avant une approche plus accessible de ses modèles. Face à OpenAI et Google, la bataille pour imposer les modèles d’IA les plus performants et les plus rentables s’annonce plus intense que jamais. The post Anthropic dévoile Fable 5.2, un modèle d’IA plus puissant et moins cher appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Taekwondo : Aïda Touré et Marie Sarr se qualifient en demi-finales
items.description: La jeune Sénégalaise Aïda Touré s’est imposée mardi en taekwondo, lors de son combat contre Ximena Zapata Pena du Pérou en quarts de finale de la catégorie des moins de 63 kg. Chez les moins de 55 kg, Marie Sarr a aussi décroché sa place en demi-finale, face à la Jordanienne Laean Alrawashdeh. Les compétitions se sont déroulées au Complexe Iba Mar Diop, dans le cadre des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse Dakar 2026 (JOJ Dakar 2026). Le Sénégal peut à nouveau décrocher des médailles en taekwondo avec ses deux jeunes athlètes Aïda Touré et Marie Sarr qui ont remporté ce mardi leur match en quarts de finale. Aïda Touré a parfaitement lancé son tournoi. La Sénégalaise (Chung/Bleu) a dominé la Péruvienne Ximena Zapata Pena en deux manches sèches (2-0) lors des quarts de finale des -63 kg dames, ce mardi au Complexe Iba Mar Diop, dans le cadre des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse Dakar 2026. A lire aussi : JOJ Dakar 2026-Basketball 3×3 : le Sénégal bat la France 18 à 12 points chez les femmes Dès les premières secondes, Aïda a pris l’initiative. Enchaînant les coups de pied au corps et à la tête, elle a multiplié les points dans la première moitié du round. Elle a conclu la manche avec cinq touches au corps et deux à la tête, auxquelles s’ajoute le point offert par un gam-jeom infligé à son adversaire. Ainsi, le résultat était de 17 points à 2, et une victoire par écart de points (R-PTG). La Péruvienne n’a trouvé la cible qu’une seule fois, par un coup de pied au corps. Une seconde manche maîtrisée Au retour des vestiaires, Zapata Pena n’a pas trouvé la solution. Toure a géré son avantage avec sérénité, plaçant trois coups de pied au corps, deux à la tête et un coup de poing au corps, pour un total de 13 points contre zéro. Les points se sont faits plus rares que lors du premier round, mais l’écart est resté constant jusqu’au coup de gong final (R-PTF). Une troisième manche n’a pas été nécessaire. Sur l’ensemble du combat, la Sénégalaise totalise 30 points contre 2 pour son adversaire. Elle a réussi douze attaques valides, dont quatre coups de pied à la tête, les plus rémunérateurs de ses techniques, sans recevoir le moindre gam-jeom, à savoir la pénalité officielle infligée à son adversaire lors d'une infraction aux règles du combat. Marie Sarr, une qualification obtenue au bout d’un combat accroché Contrairement à Aïda Touré, chez les moins de 55 kg, Marie Sarr a eu plus de mal à décrocher sa place. Face à la Jordanienne Laean Alrawashdeh, elle a cédé la première manche (27-33), avant de réagir en gagnant les deux suivantes (26-11 puis 18-3). Elle l’emporte ainsi 2 manches à 1. Place maintenant aux demi-finales, où les deux Sénégalaises espèrent se hisser jusqu’à la finale. Marie Sarr montera sur le tatami à 16 h 00 chez les moins de 55 kg, tandis qu’Aïda Touré fera face à l’Iranienne Asal Goltapeh à 16 h 30 chez les moins de 63 kg. Déjà assurées d’une médaille de bronze pour le pays, elles peuvent désormais viser plus haut et offrir au Sénégal une place en finale. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Imran's hospital transfer: Uzma seeks early fixation of contempt plea against govt for third time
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Dr Uzma Khan, sister of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan, on Tuesday again approached the Supreme Court (SC) seeking an early fixation of the contempt plea against the federal government over alleged flouting of the court’s order to shift the ex-premier to Shifa International Hospital (SIH) for medical treatment. On Aug 18 , a three-member SC bench had directed the government to shift Imran to Islamabad’s SIH within the next two days as it heard several petitions concerning his health. However, the government took the PTI founder to the government-run Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) for a check-up and then transported him back to prison. The SC’s office has already turned down Uzma’s two previous requests for an early hearing of the contempt plea, which was filed on Aug 22. The second early hearing request was submitted after the SC had fixed the main petition for Sept 16. However, on that day, the SC deferred the matter in the wake of the Federal Constitutional Court’s (FCC) directives . In both denials, the registrar office had stressed that the fixation policy required proceedings to be conducted turn-wise. It noted that 94 different criminal original petitions belonging to the same category were already pending before the SC for hearing. Subsequently, on Tuesday, a fresh application for early hearing was filed through Advocate Uzair Karamat Bhandari on behalf of Dr Uzma, following the PTI’s claim that Imran’s blood pressure surged above 190 recently. Moved under Order XXXV Rules 5 and 6 of the Supreme Court Rules, 2025, the application requests the SC to order fixation of the contempt plea for next week. The contempt plea had named Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, Islamabad Chief Commissioner Sohail Ashraf, Interior Secretary Ahmed Raza Sarwar, Punjab Inspector General Prisons Mian Salik Jalal and Adiala jail’s Superintendent Sajid Baig as respondents. In the fresh application, Dr Uzma has stressed the urgency in the matter due to reports circulating in the media that the incarcerated leader’s blood pressure recently rose to 192 and that there were serious concerns about his health. “If an early hearing of this matter is not granted, the applicant’s and Imran Khan’s guaranteed rights will continue to be prejudiced,” the application stated, arguing that his fundamental rights, particularly with respect to health and well-being, as well as access to medical advice and facilities and family members, would continue to be violated. The application stated the previous contempt plea had also sought court directives to arrange and facilitate weekly meetings between Imran and his family members, including petitioners and his other sisters, Noreen Niazi and Aleema Khan, along with his cousin Qasim Zaman. It had also sought phone calls between Imran and his sons Kasim Khan and Sulaiman Khan twice a week. On Sept 16, resuming the hearing on petitions concerning Imran’s health, the SC had expressed reservations over the Federal Constitutional Court’s (FCC) directive that cases pertaining to the PTI founder’s hospital transfer be fixed before it. However, the SC had deferred its own proceedings, observing that propriety demanded deferment. At the time, the court said it was adjourning the proceedings for a date after three weeks, and is yet to be fixed for hearing. The FCC had issued the orders, directing the court’s office to requisition the relevant cases from the SC and fix them before it under Article 175-E of the Constitution. The directive was issued on a plea by three Adiala jail inmates seeking relief similar to that provided to Imran by the SC in the Aug 18 interim order. A three-judge SC bench, headed by Justice Shahid Waheed and including Justices Naeem Akhtar Afghan and Ishtiaq Ibrahim, had also observed that fixing cases before the FCC requisitioned from the SC did not fall under clause 5 of Article 175-E of the Constitution. Article 175-E, which was inserted in the Constitution through the 27th Constitutional Amendment, empowers the FCC to call for the record of any case and authorises it to decide matters involving major questions of constitutional law.

items.title: US university suspends fraternity after students filmed on fire
items.description: Ohio State University in the United States has suspended a fraternity after footage emerged showing two young men on fire, local media reported on Monday. The video, which garnered more than 1.5 million views on X, shows the pair surrounded by a group laughing and filming as they roll around on the ground, engulfed in flames. Fraternities — male social clubs common on US campuses — have long come under scrutiny for booze-infused parties and hazing rituals that can lead to sexual assault, accidents and even deaths. The elite Cornell University suspended fraternity parties and social events last month for the remaining academic year following an alleged gang rape at one of its clubs that has horrified Americans. “The university is aware of this extremely concerning incident, and the individuals in question are receiving needed medical care,” Ohio State University spokesman Ben Johnson said in a statement quoted by local news outlet WCMH-TV. “Ohio State has placed the Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity on interim suspension pending a full investigation.” Sigma Alpha Epsilon claims on its website to have “forged men into leaders” since its foundation in 1856. Columbus police said they were also investigating the incident. The post US university suspends fraternity after students filmed on fire appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Spend more in 2027 to boost growth – PwC to govt
items.description: The government must use the 2027 Budget to increase efficient spending and prioritise resources towards productive sectors to stimulate economic growth without undermining the gains made in stabilising the economy, the Country Senior Partner of PwC Ghana, George Arhin, has said. Mr Arhin, who took office nearly a month ago, explained that with the 2026 Budget having achieved its objective of stabilising the economy, the focus of the new budget should be on ensuring that public funds are channelled into sectors capable of generating jobs, boosting productivity and attracting private sector investment under the proposed $10 billion New Economy Programme. Consequently, he said the government must prioritise investments in agriculture, agro-processing, manufacturing, textiles and tourism in the upcoming budget to drive sustainable growth and accelerate the country’s economic transformation. In an interview with the Daily Graphic in Accra last Friday, ahead of the 2027 budget presentation to Parliament on Thursday, Mr Arhin stressed that the government must put in place measures to translate the stability achieved into private sector-led growth. “We have recovered and stabilised, but that stability came on the back of robust monetary and fiscal policies supported by external factors like gold prices. That cannot be sustained because if you are not spending, the economy cannot grow. “So, my expectation is for us to translate the stability we have seen into private sector-led growth. It is very important because it is the private sector that drives the economy and serves as the engine of growth,” he said. Background The Minister of Finance, Dr Cassiel Ato Forson, is expected to present the 2027 Budget Statement and Economic Policy to Parliament on Thursday, marking the third budget of the President John Dramani Mahama-led administration since it assumed office in January 2025. Expected to carry the title, The New Economy, it is anticipated that the budget will outline how the government intends to translate the recent macroeconomic stabilisation into productive investments, decent jobs, improved incomes and business growth. A major focus is expected to be the implementation of the government’s $10 billion New Economy Programme, covering 2027 to 2030, which seeks to stimulate a private-sector-led domestic production expansion, promote local processing and value addition, strengthen Ghanaian businesses and create employment opportunities. Spend more With about GH¢268.8 billion and GH¢302.5 billion earmarked for expenditure programmes in the 2025 and 2026 budgets, respectively, Mr Arhin stated that the government must be able to spend more next year than it did in previous years, but that spending must be efficient and directed at sectors that would help stimulate growth. “We cannot grow the economy simply by increasing expenditure; we must ensure that every investment delivers value, creates jobs and strengthens the productive sectors of the economy. “Agriculture, agro-processing, manufacturing, textiles and tourism were priority areas that required increased government investment to expand productive capacity and create employment,” he said. He stressed that channelling resources into those sectors would also attract private sector investment and support the government’s New Economy agenda. Mr Arhin added that efficient allocation of public funds would be critical to sustaining economic stability while accelerating growth and transforming the economy. New Economy Describing the government’s New Economy Programme as a potential game-changer for the country’s economic transformation, the Country Senior Partner stated that its success would depend on how efficiently the funds were deployed. He said the programme, which focuses on strengthening the real sectors of the economy, presented an opportunity to expand agriculture, manufacturing, agro-processing, textiles, tourism and value addition in the extractive industry. The PwC Senior Country Partner urged businesses and investors to position themselves to take advantage of the opportunities by identifying sectors expected to receive significant government investment and aligning their activities with the programme’s priorities. Mr Arhin stressed that the programme must go beyond government spending to serve as a catalyst for private sector-led growth, formal employment creation and increased domestic revenue mobilisation. “The New Economy is a game-changer. If we are able to focus the money dedicated to it and spend it well, we will move the dial,” he said. Widen tax net Mr Arhin also maintained that agriculture, which contributes about 21 per cent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and employs 33 per cent of the population, accounted for only 0.05 per cent of the country’s tax revenue. He said the disparity highlighted the need for policies to formalise activities in the sector, move smallholder farmers towards commercial production and strengthen agro-processing to expand the tax base. The PwC Senior Country Partner explained that shifting economic activities from the primary sector to the secondary sector would create formal employment opportunities and bring more businesses and workers into the tax net. “It’s not about bringing in new tax handles or increasing the tax rate; it’s about widening the database to include the vast majority of people who are not paying taxes,” he said. Double-digit growth Mr Arhin said although the current economic growth rate of about 5.5 per cent was encouraging, the country needed sustained double-digit growth to achieve meaningful economic transformation. He stated that the economy’s ability to record growth of between five and six per cent despite reduced government expenditure and tight monetary policies demonstrated its potential to expand further. He explained that increased but efficient investment in agriculture, manufacturing, tourism and value addition in the extractive industry would help accelerate growth and strengthen the productive base of the economy. “We need to grow into the double-digit numbers and sustain that growth to transform our economy,” he stressed. Gold windfall On the sustainability of the economic recovery, Mr Arhin cautioned that the country could not rely indefinitely on favourable external conditions, particularly high gold prices, to maintain macroeconomic stability. He explained that the recent stability had been supported by robust monetary and fiscal policies, alongside favourable external developments, including improved gold prices, which could not be guaranteed over the long term. Mr Arhin urged the government to strengthen domestic revenue mobilisation and create an enabling environment for private sector investment to sustain the recovery and build resilience against external shocks. “That stability came on the back of robust monetary and fiscal policies supported by external factors such as gold prices. That cannot be sustained if we are not spending to grow the economy,” he said.

items.title: “The fire around December in GH feels a bit doused” – George Quaye
items.description: Team Lead for ImageBureau, George Quaye, has expressed concern about the apparent lull in activities surrounding the government’s December in GH initiative, saying the brand has lost some of its momentum. Speaking to Kwame Dadzie on Joy FM’s Showbiz A-Z , the creative entrepreneur said while he believed every government had the right to introduce new ideas, he felt the impact of December in GH had not been prominent enough. “It’s just said that the fire around the brand December in GH feels a bit doused. When December in GH was the lead brand that was headlining everything but frankly it’s not that I want to apportion blame. I mean, new king, new law. Everybody has their vision. There is nothing wrong with having a vision and wanting to propagate it,” he said. George, however, added that if an existing initiative had to be changed, there needed to be a superior replacement. “Maybe it’s just more time that we need but I would have wished that what was started some time back that was titled the December in GH which became a global phenomenon would have been jealously guarded and pushed,” he noted. The history of December in GH dates back to the Ghana Tourism Authority’s efforts to position the country as a preferred destination for the festive season, particularly for members of the diaspora. The initiative gained prominence around the 2019 Year of Return, while the popular moniker ‘Detty December’ was coined in 2019 by Ghanaian creative Bernard Kafui Sokpe, popularly known as Mr Meister, during preparations for a December concert for Nigerian musician Mr Eazi. The brand has since become associated with concerts, parties, festivals and homecoming activities. The branding has, however, generated controversy. In May 2025, Speaker of Parliament Alban Bagbin criticised the use of ‘Detty December’, arguing that the name projected a negative image of Ghana and vowing to fight against it. In December 2025, Director of Diaspora Affairs at the Presidency, Kofi Okyere Darko, popularly known as KOD, also expressed reservations about the name, saying he was not a fan of the concept and wanted the season to extend beyond entertainment and nightlife to include business opportunities, investment and networking. Meanwhile, concerns about the perceived decline in the excitement surrounding December in GH have also emerged from sections of the creative industry and the public. Following the 2025 celebrations, a social media post by Black Volta suggesting that the festive season had not lived up to expectations triggered further debate. However, disc jockey and event organiser DJ Mensah disputed the criticism, insisting that December in Ghana had been successful, with hotels recording strong bookings and several events selling out. For the 2026 edition, the Ministry of Tourism, Culture and Creative Arts and the Ghana Tourism Authority have unveiled an official calendar featuring more than 150 events nationwide. Running from 1st December 2026 to 3rd January 2027 under the theme ‘Ghana to the World’, the programme forms part of the Black Star Experience initiative and seeks to showcase Ghana’s music, culture, fashion, food, heritage and hospitality. Government has also called on tourism and hospitality businesses to improve service delivery, promote destinations beyond Accra and ensure that the festive season generates economic opportunities for local businesses and creative industry players.

items.title: Conakry : commémoration du 108e anniversaire de l’armistice de 1918 et honore les anciens combattants
items.description: ​Ce mardi 10 novembre, la Direction générale des pensions militaires et des anciens combattants (DGPMAC) a abrité une cérémonie solennelle de commémoration de la fin de la Première Guerre mondiale et d'hommage aux morts pour la France. Cet événement mémoriel, marqué par la remise de dons aux anciens combattants, a réuni de hautes personnalités civiles et militaires, témoignant de la force des liens unissant la Guinée et la France. ​Un devoir de mémoire partagé face à l'histoire ​Présidée par le Directeur de Cabinet du Ministère de la Défense nationale et placée sous le signe du souvenir, cette journée marque le 108e anniversaire de l'armistice du 11 novembre 1918, date marquant la fin des hostilités de la Grande Guerre. Dans son discours, le Directeur de Cabinet du Ministère de la Défense nationale, le Général David Haba, a rappelé l'importance de préserver ce précieux héritage mémoriel. Poursuivant, l'officier supérieur de l'armée a souligné que l'armistice ne se limite pas à un simple repère historique, mais symbolise le retour à la paix et le sacrifice de milliers d'hommes et de femmes pour leurs idéaux. S'exprimant au nom des anciens combattants, ​le Commandant Bakary Mara a, quant à lui, mis en lumière les sacrifices consentis par les soldats africains, et guinéens en particulier, qui ont traversé les mers et affronté l'adversité pour défendre des valeurs universelles de liberté et de justice. Il a salué la mémoire de figures illustres disparues, tout en insistant sur la nécessité de perpétuer leur exemple auprès des jeunes générations. ​La cérémonie a également été marquée par l'allocution de l'ambassadeur de France en Guinée, Luc Briard, qui a réaffirmé l'engagement indéfectible de la France envers ses frères d'armes guinéens. Le diplomate français a insisté sur le fait que la dette de reconnaissance envers ces combattants est avant tout panafricaine et universelle. ​Dans un geste de solidarité concrète, l'ambassade de France a procédé à la remise de d'importants dons, incluant un lot de médicaments pour le dispensaire des anciens combattants ainsi que des équipements de bureau destinés à l'Office national des anciens combattants et victimes de guerre (ONACVEC). En plus, M. Luc Briard a annoncé une aide complémentaire de 100 millions de francs guinéens, qui sera gérée par une commission paritaire, et qui permettra de soutenir les plus nécessiteux, notamment les veuves et les orphelins. Pour sa part, l​e Directeur général adjoint des Pensions militaires et des anciens combattants, le Colonel Mohamed Korka Damba, a réitéré la gratitude de la Nation envers ces hommes et ces femmes qui ont incarné l'honneur du pays. Il a rappelé que les portes de la DGPMAC restent ouvertes pour veiller au bien-être, à la dignité et au suivi social de ces figures vivantes de l'histoire nationale. La commémoration s'est achevée dans un climat de ferveur et de recueillement, scellant l'engagement commun de la Guinée et de la France à bâtir un avenir fondé sur la paix, la fraternité et le respect mutuel des mémoires.

items.title: Après la fin de la Minurso, le Maroc affiche sa proximité militaire avec Israël
items.description: Mohammed VI a donné une dimension inédite à la visite au Maroc du secrétaire général du ministère de la Défense israélien . Le roi a donné des instructions pour l'accueillir, une première dans les relations entre les deux pays. La visite du haut responsable militaire israélien à Rabat intervient quelques jours après l’expiration du mandat de la Minurso qui n’a pas été renouvelé après le véto russe contre le projet de résolution américain sur le Sahara occidental, vendredi 30 octobre. Le secrétaire général du ministère de la Défense israélien, Amir Baram, effectue, du 9 au 11 novembre, une visite officielle au Maroc, à la tête d’une délégation. Le responsable israélien a été reçu « en exécution des instructions royales » par Abdelatif Loudiyi, ministre délégué chargé de l’administration de la Défense. Amir Baram s’est rendu ensuite au siège de l’état-major des Forces armées royales (FAR) où il s’est entretenu avec Ahmed Berrid qui occupe les fonctions d’inspecteur général de l’armée marocaine. Les deux parties ont abordé des questions en rapport avec l’acquisition par le Maroc, d’équipements et de technologies de défense israéliennes, selon des communiqués officiels. Des responsables israéliens se sont rendus au Maroc ces deux dernières années, mais c’est la première fois que les instructions du roi viennent donner un caractère spécial à cette visite qui intervient dix jours après la fin la Mission des Nations Unies pour l’organisation d’un référendum d’autodétermination au Sahara occidental ( Minurso) dont le mandat a pris fin le 31 octobre dernier. Dix jours après la fin de la Minurso, un haut responsable militaire israélien au Maroc « Ce n’est peut-être pas un hasard que les Israéliens se montrent quand la Minurso fait ses bagages », écrit le journaliste espagnol spécialiste du Maghreb, Ignacio Cembrero sur X. Il a relevé que c’est « la première visite bilatérale rendue publique depuis le début de l’invasion de Gaza en octobre 2023. Auparavant, deux autres hauts responsables israéliens s’étaient rendus au Maroc, mais dans un cadre multilatéral : la conférence mondiale sur la sécurité routière et le Marrakech Airshow ». Israël et le Maroc ont considérablement renforcé leur coopération militaire depuis la normalisation de leurs relations en décembre 2020. En septembre dernier, ils ont signé l’acte II des Accords d’Abraham qui prévoient l’ouverture d’ambassades dans les deux pays. Malgré la guerre à Gaza et l’hostilité de l’opinion publique à la normalisation, le Maroc a multiplié l’achat d’équipements militaires et d’armes d’Israël. Le non-renouvellement du mandat de la Minurso peut ouvrir la voie à la reprise des affrontements armés entre le Maroc et le Front Polisario. Le cabinet Royal a exprimé le 4 décembre dernier « l’engagement total du Royaume en faveur du cessez-le-feu » signé en 1991. Mais en politique, tous les scénarios restent envisageables. L’article Après la fin de la Minurso, le Maroc affiche sa proximité militaire avec Israël est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Marathon Houet de Sidwaya 2026 : Plus de 2 000 coureurs attendus le 14 novembre à Bobo
items.description: Les Editions Sidwaya organisent, le 14 novembre 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso, la 2 e édition du « Marathon Houet de Sidwaya » après le coup de maitre de celle de l’année dernière. Le comité d’organisation a tenu, le mardi 10 novembre 2026 à Bobo-Dioulass, une conférence de presse pour annoncer les couleurs de la compétition où sont attendus plus de 2000 coureurs. La 2 e édition du « Marathon Houet de Sidwaya » aura lieu le samedi 14 Novembre 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso. Ce marathon se déroule en deux compétitions. La première appelée « Elite nationale » se court sur 21 kilomètres et est réservée aux athlètes burkinabè. La deuxième, « Elite régionale », est une épreuve de 10 kilomètres et concerne les populations de la région de Guiriko avec des catégories masculine et féminine. Le départ est prévu à 7 heures devant la direction régionale de l’Ouest des Editions sidwaya située sur la route de Bolomaté. Plus de 2 000 coureurs sont attendus pour cette 2 e édition du marathon. A la date du 10 novembre 2026, ce sont 151 athlètes qui sont inscrits pour les 21 kilomètres et 2003 pour les 10 kilomètres alors que les inscriptions se poursuivent toujours. Ce sont là quelques informations que le comité d’organisation du marathon a livrées aux hommes de médias lors d’un point de presse qu’elle a tenu le 10 Novembre 2026 à Bobo-Dioulasso. Les meilleurs coureurs du marathon auront de nombreux prix dont deux motos données par le sponsor. A l’occasion, le président du comité d’organisation, Jean-Marie Toé, par ailleurs secrétaire général des Editions Sidwaya, a rassuré que ls dispositions ont été prises pour assurer la sécurité des athlètes, des officiels et des populations. Il a révélé que les athlètes vont être récompensés avec des prix motivants pour valoriser leurs performances. Ainsi pour « Elite nationale », les prix vont de 300 000 à 20 000 F CFA pour les 40 premiers concurrents dont 300 000 F CFA pour le premier. Ces prix sont de 200 000 F CFA à 10 0000 FCFA pour les 40 premiers hommes et femmes pour « l’Elite régionale ». En plus des prix officiels, les compétiteurs vont avoir des prix spéciaux offerts par les partenaires et sponsors dont deux motos déjà mises à la disposition du comité d’organisation par APSONIC pour les lauréats. Le comité d’organisation a exprimé sa gratitude à tous ces partenaires mais aussi aux personnalités qui accompagnent cette 2 e édition. La présente édition est placée sous le patronage du ministre de la Communication, de la Culture, des Arts et du Tourisme, Pingdwendé Gilbert Ouedraogo ; sous la présidence du ministre des Sports, de la Jeunesse et de l'Emploi, Annick PIKBOUGOUM/Zingué Ouattara ; et sous l'autorité morale du Chef de Canton de Bobo-Dioulasso. Un marathon pour la cohésion sociale La 2 e édition du marathon Houet de Sidwaya est placée sous le thème « jeunesse et RPP : unis par le sport, engagés pour la paix ». Pour les conférenciers, le sport puissant instrument de rassemblement, de fraternité et de solidarité, est essentiel dans le contexte actuel où le concours de tous est essentiel pour promouvoir les idéaux de paix, de patriotisme et de cohésion sociale. Les Editions Sidwaya entendent ainsi jouer leur partition à travers le Marathon Houet. Les journalistes présents à la conférence de presse ont salué l’initiative des Editions Sidwaya et ont émis des préoccupations liées ente autres au suivi des athlètes. « Le Marathon Houet de Sidwaya entend ainsi apporter sa contribution à cette dynamique nationale en faisant du sport un espace de rencontre, de dépassement de soi et de communion entre les filles et les fils du Burkina Faso », a signifié le président du comité d’organisation. Les journalistes présents à la conférence de presse ont demandé un bilan de la première édition du marathon, et émis des préoccupations liées au suivi des marathoniens, à la sécurité du circuit. A ces différentes préoccupations le président du comité d’organisation, le président de la commission partenariat et sponsoring, Moussa Congo, et le représentant de la direction technique de la fédération d’athlétisme, Salim Bonkoungou, ont chacun, selon son domaine de compétence apporté des éclaircissements. Le président du comité d’organisation, Jean-Marie Toé, a appelé les populations du Guiriko à se mobiliser, le samedi 14 novembre 2026, pour encourager les athlètes et célèbrer les valeurs du sport. En marge de la compétition, les Editions Sidwaya et la commune de Bobo-Dioulasso organisent une marche sportive le vendredi 13 novembre 2026 et un village du marathon du 12 au 15 novembre 2026 à la place de la mairie. Adaman DRABO Credit Photos : Adama DRABO

items.title: Nacee’s KAVOD 26 delivers an evening of drama, laughter and gospel music at National Theatre
items.description: Gospel musician and award-winning producer Nacee brought together drama, comedy and live gospel music for the second edition of his flagship entertainment event, KAVOD 26, held at the National Theatre in Accra on Sunday, November 8, 2026. The show, which began at 6:25 p.m., featured an extensive lineup of musicians, actors and comedians in a production that moved between theatrical storytelling, stand-up comedy and live musical performances. Unlike a conventional gospel concert, KAVOD 26 adopted various entertainment formats, with a dramatic opening setting the tone for an evening that combined humour, social commentary, nostalgia and worship. Drama sets the tone The evening opened with a short comedy-drama featuring GH Poki and Adom Best, who played a prophet and his assistant. Their humorous exchange introduced the story of Nacee, with the prophet recounting the musician’s achievements and contributions to the music industry. Roselyn Felli, who served as the event’s MC, subsequently welcomed patrons and introduced the main theatrical production. The play featured an ensemble cast comprising Vivian Jill, Foster Romanus, Clemento Suarez, Gadede Segbefia, DeLong, Deaconess Abokoma, Eno Fordjour, Jeneral Ntatia, Asafo Powers and other performers. Centred on a family, the production explored themes of neglect, betrayal, compassion, family responsibility and the importance of standing by loved ones during difficult times. At the heart of the story was Akua, played by Gadede Segbefia, a young woman battling fibroids who urgently needed GH¢30,000 for surgery. Her predicament exposed the indifference and selfishness of some members of her family, particularly her financially comfortable brother, played by Foster Romanus, who repeatedly made excuses to avoid helping her despite having the means to do so. Clemento Suarez portrayed the family head, an uncle who secretly received financial assistance from Akua’s love interest without informing her. Vivian Jill played Abrewa Mafia, a carefree aunt whose priorities revolved largely around money and personal enjoyment. Deaconess Abokoma and Eno Fordjour brought additional humour to the production as two village gossips, while Jeneral Ntatia played Wofa Gyata, a family friend who persistently challenged the relatives to take responsibility for Akua’s welfare. The plot took another turn with the arrival of Charles, played by DeLong, a former love interest who had travelled abroad after receiving an opportunity initially offered to him by Akua. Having remained in contact with her uncle and sent money to support her, Charles returned to Ghana hoping to reunite with Akua, only to discover that she had never received the financial assistance. Upon finding her, he offered to pay for her surgery and arrange a better living situation away from the family home. His offer, however, came with an interesting condition. Akua could relocate with one person of her choosing. While her brother assumed he would naturally be selected, she chose Wofa Gyata, the one person who had consistently stood by her. Another comic moment came with the appearance of Killer Ntua, played by Asafo Powers, as an overzealous lawyer who threatened to arrest and sue almost everyone around him. Beyond the humour, the play delivered a social commentary on family neglect, financial irresponsibility and the importance of genuine support during difficult times. Soul Winners and Jacinta take over Following the theatrical production, gospel group Soul Winners took to the stage with a lively live-band performance. The group performed a selection of its familiar gospel classics, drawing patrons out of their seats as the auditorium turned into a praise and dance session. Several audience members sang along to the nostalgic collection. Comedian Jacinta followed with a stand-up performance, entertaining the audience with observations about cultural similarities and differences between Ghana and Nigeria. Nacee makes a dramatic entrance One of the evening’s major highlights came with Nacee’s first appearance. The gospel musician made a dramatic entrance, emerging in a sparkling white outfit to an enthusiastic reception from patrons. He immediately launched into a selection of his popular gospel songs, getting the audience on its feet as patrons sang along to the familiar tunes. As he concluded that segment, Nacee descended from the stage and approached gospel singer Yvonne Menz, personally inviting her to take over the microphone. Yvonne responded with a powerful worship ministration. Her soothing vocals and heartfelt delivery brought a more reflective atmosphere to the auditorium, offering a moment of worship amid the evening’s comedy and theatrical entertainment. Comedy, cash and memorable moments Comedian OB Amponsah subsequently took over, delivering a routine that drew laughter through jokes about his forehead, the challenges of driving small cars in Ghana and the assumption that their owners work as Uber drivers. He also touched on the peculiar experiences of living in Kasoa, drawing on familiar aspects of everyday Ghanaian life. Veteran gospel musician Cindy Thompson followed, returning the auditorium to a worshipful atmosphere with a selection of her well-known gospel classics. Her performance showcased her vocal strength and control, giving patrons another opportunity to sing along. Parrot Mouth was next, bringing his spontaneous humour and familiar Ghana-Nigeria comparisons to the stage. He also took aim at Nigeria’s political situation under President Bola Tinubu. One of the night’s funniest exchanges came when he spotted Prophet Ajagurajah, who was seated in the auditorium, and repeatedly approached him for money. After several attempts, Ajagurajah responded by handing him bundles of cash, prompting excitement and laughter among the audience. In an unexpected gesture, Parrot Mouth subsequently gave one of the bundles to a security officer stationed beneath the stage, earning applause from patrons. Foster Romanus, apparently encouraged by the development, also approached Ajagurajah and secured some cash with Parrot Mouth’s assistance. Jeffrey Nortey delivers another comic highlight Foster Romanus later returned to the stage to introduce comedian and actor Jeffrey Nortey, whose entrance was greeted with loud cheers as patrons chanted his popular signature name, “Nuumo!” Jeffrey delivered a series of punchlines, clever wordplay and witty observations, living up to the audience’s anticipation. He incorporated Ajagurajah into some of his jokes before turning his attention to Nacee, using the musician’s name as the basis for a series of creative wordplays. His closing lines drew on Akan expressions which bore a phonetic resemblance to Nacee’s name to deliver a memorable introduction of the gospel musician. The wordplay earned enthusiastic applause and provided a fitting transition for Nacee’s return to the stage. Nacee pays tribute to Bernice Offei Returning for his second major performance, Nacee treated patrons to another extended musical set featuring more songs from his catalogue. A particularly emotional moment came when he paid tribute to the late gospel musician Bernice Offei, performing some of her songs in her memory. The tribute, which also acknowledged other departed personalities, introduced a reflective dimension to the evening and reminded patrons of the lasting contributions of musicians who have passed on. Nacee subsequently invited Kofi Peprah to the stage, where the gospel musician delivered a performance that was warmly received. Gospel minister Joe Mettle was then called upon to bring the musical proceedings to a close with a ministration that rounded off the evening. KAVOD’s blend of entertainment continues KAVOD 26 continued Nacee’s attempt to create a live entertainment platform that extends beyond the traditional gospel concert format by bringing together theatre, comedy and music. The second edition followed the maiden production in November 2023, which similarly combined a theatrical portrayal of Nacee’s personal journey with live musical performances and comedy. With an extensive cast of actors, comedians and gospel musicians, the 2026 production offered a varied programme that balanced storytelling, humour, nostalgia and worship. From the opening drama and family-themed stage play to the comedy performances, musical tributes and final gospel ministrations, KAVOD 26 gave the National Theatre audience an evening that explored different dimensions of live entertainment under one roof.

items.title: Developing countries’ external debt surges to a record $9.4trn – World Bank
items.description: External debt of developing countries jumped 5.5% to a record $9.4 trillion in 2025, the fastest pace since 2021 and about four times the 2022–24 average, according to the World Bank Group’s International Debt Report 2026. Access to international finance has improved, but the price of finance has not, and high debt burdens in the poorest countries threaten to crowd out essential investments in people. Private financing drove much of the increase. Borrowing from private creditors jumped and bond issuance from public entities rose nearly 35% to $251 billion, the highest level in five years as markets reopened to many developing countries. External debt grew fastest among the most vulnerable countries, increasing 8.1% to $1.3 trillion in countries eligible for concessional financing from the World Bank Group’s International Development Association (IDA).. “The return of private lending to low- and middle-income countries is welcome, but these countries are borrowing more, paying more, and in many cases leaving less for long-term development,” said Haishan Fu, World Bank Group Chief Statistician and Director of Development Data. “Managing debt responsibly means giving everyone—including future generations—a chance to thrive.” Many governments issued new bonds to buy back maturing debt, smoothing repayment profiles without significantly reducing debt stocks, often at higher interest rates. Early 2026 data show continued demand for international bond financing from low- and middle-income countries despite the high costs. By mid-August, more than 10 countries had exceeded their full-year 2025 issuance, while several others returned to international markets. IDA-eligible countries paid an average of 8.2% on new private-creditor commitments in 2025—the highest rate since 1989—and 9.4% on new bonds. The gap between the rates IDA-eligible countries paid to official and private creditors widened from 3.4 percentage points in 2016 to 5.5 percentage points in 2025. In comparison, countries eligible for only non-concessional loans from the World Bank Group’s International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD) paid an average of 5.5% on new bonds, an improvement from the 5.8% rate the previous year. Debt-service pressures remained severe amid elevated global interest rates. Low- and middle-income countries paid $1.4 trillion in principal and interest in 2025, up 1.9% and marking a fifth consecutive annual increase. Payments to bondholders climbed to $363 billion, partly reflecting debt buybacks and prepayments financed through new bond issues. Between 2022 through 2025, developing countries paid $436 billion more in debt service than they received in new financing. The direction shifted in 2025, however, as long-term debt flows turned from a $118 billion net outflow in 2024 to a net inflow of $45 billion. Currency movements also played a role in the reported increase. More than a quarter of the $303 billion increase in public and publicly guaranteed debt reflected the weaker US dollar, which raised the dollar value of debt denominated in other currencies. For several of the largest concessional borrowers, these currency effects outweighed the principal they repaid in 2025, leaving reported debt higher despite continued servicing.

items.title: Trafic de migrants: 262 arrestations et 41 réseaux criminels identifiés en Méditerranée
items.description: INTERPOL a rendu public, ce mardi 10 novembre 2026, le bilan de l’opération internationale Communis Maris, menée du 5 au 8 octobre dernier contre les réseaux de trafic de migrants en Méditerranée et sur la route atlantique ouest-africaine. L’intervention a permis l’arrestation de 262 suspects, l’identification de 41 groupes criminels organisés et l’ouverture de 434 nouvelles enquêtes. Les réseaux de trafic de migrants opérant entre l’Afrique, l’Europe et le Moyen-Orient ont été la cible d’une vaste opération policière internationale. Baptisée Communis Maris, cette initiative coordonnée par l’Organisation internationale de police criminelle (INTERPOL), avec l’appui de plusieurs partenaires internationaux, a mobilisé 16 pays du 5 au 8 octobre 2026. Selon le rapport rendu public, ce mardi 10 novembre, par INTERPOL, l’opération a abouti à l’interpellation de 262 suspects. Parmi eux, 221 sont poursuivis pour des faits de trafic de migrants, 16 pour traite des êtres humains et 25 pour d’autres infractions, notamment la fabrication et l’utilisation de faux documents. Les investigations ont également permis de détecter 1 715 migrants en situation irrégulière et d’identifier 109 victimes potentielles de traite des êtres humains. Au total, 7 660 agents ont été mobilisés pour contrôler plus de 378 000 personnes, surveiller les zones sensibles et renforcer les dispositifs de sécurité aux principaux points de passage. En parallèle, 210 594 consultations des bases de données d’INTERPOL ont été effectuées afin de faciliter l’identification des suspects et le partage de renseignements entre les pays participants. Pour David Caunter, directeur du crime organisé et émergent à INTERPOL, la lutte contre ces réseaux constitue un enjeu majeur de protection des vies humaines. Il rappelle que la Méditerranée demeure l’un des corridors migratoires les plus meurtriers au monde, où les passeurs exploitent la vulnérabilité des candidats à l’émigration, les exposant aux abus, à l’extorsion et à des traversées dangereuses à bord d’embarcations souvent surchargées et inadaptées. Des interceptions de migrants de l’Afrique à la Méditerranée Plusieurs interventions marquantes ont été enregistrées au cours de cette opération. Dans le sud du Maroc, les autorités ont intercepté un bateau transportant 70 migrants potentiels, dont 30 mineurs, après six jours passés en mer. Au large de la Mauritanie, une pirogue en bois transportant 80 passagers, parmi lesquels deux enfants, a également été interceptée grâce à un signalement des autorités sénégalaises. Trois organisateurs présumés ont été arrêtés dans le cadre de cette intervention. En Tunisie, les forces de l’ordre ont empêché un départ clandestin et interpellé trois ressortissants soupçonnés de trafic d’êtres humains. Un bateau, un moteur marin et divers équipements ont été saisis. En Libye, 34 victimes potentielles de traite des êtres humains ont été secourues et trois personnes suspectées d'appartenir à un réseau impliqué dans la traite, le trafic de migrants et l'extorsion ont été arrêtées. D’autres opérations ont été conduites en Algérie, où six suspects ont été interpellés dans le cadre du démantèlement présumé d’un réseau de passeurs, notamment poursuivis pour avoir mis en danger des mineurs. En Syrie, une intervention coordonnée de plusieurs services de sécurité a permis l’arrestation de sept suspects, dont le présumé chef d’un réseau, et l’interception de 22 migrants en situation irrégulière. Les faux documents et le blanchiment d’argent également ciblés Les investigations ne se sont pas limitées aux traversées maritimes. Les contrôles ont également été renforcés dans les aéroports afin de lutter contre l’utilisation de faux documents de voyage et les circuits financiers alimentant les réseaux criminels. À Chypre et en Grèce, des arrestations ont été opérées dans des aéroports pour des tentatives d’utilisation de faux documents. Au Maroc, une personne soupçonnée de fabriquer de faux passeports et de recruter des candidats à la migration irrégulière a été arrêtée. En France, six personnes ont également été interpellées pour des soupçons de blanchiment d’argent, d’aide à la migration irrégulière et d’hébergement d’une personne vulnérable dans des conditions contraires à la dignité humaine. Par ailleurs, les enquêteurs ont repéré de nombreuses publications, des groupes et des comptes sur les réseaux sociaux faisant la promotion de la migration irrégulière et proposant des services de passage clandestin. Ces éléments viennent compléter les 434 nouvelles enquêtes ouvertes à l’issue de l'opération. Des investigations appelées à se poursuivre Au terme de ces quatre jours d'intervention, les services engagés ont identifié 41 groupes criminels organisés impliqués dans le trafic de migrants. Pour INTERPOL et ses partenaires, les renseignements collectés devraient permettre de nouvelles avancées judiciaires, d'autres arrestations et le démantèlement de réseaux supplémentaires dans les semaines et les mois à venir. L’opération Communis Maris a réuni l’Algérie, Chypre, la France, la Gambie, la Grèce, l’Italie, la Libye, Malte, la Mauritanie, le Maroc, le Portugal, le Sénégal, l’Espagne, la Syrie, la Tunisie et la Turquie. Elle a été conduite par INTERPOL avec le soutien d’Europol, de Frontex, d’AFRIPOL, de l’Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM) et de l’Office des Nations unies contre la drogue et le crime (ONUDC). Son financement a été assuré par l’Union européenne dans le cadre du projet Himaya. items.title: Meet only two countries to have won both men’s, women’s U-20 World Cups
items.description: Germany and Spain are the only two countries to have won both the FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup and the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup. The two European nations have achieved the feat by winning titles in both competitions, which showcase some of the world’s best emerging football talents. Germany became the first to accomplish the double, with its men’s team, then competing as West Germany, winning the U-20 World Cup in 1981. The country’s women’s team subsequently claimed the U-20 Women’s World Cup in 2004, 2010 and 2014, taking its tally to three titles in the competition. Spain also joined the exclusive list after winning the men’s U-20 World Cup in 1999, when the tournament was hosted by Nigeria. The Spanish men’s team defeated Japan 4-0 in the final in Lagos to secure its first title. More than two decades later, Spain’s women’s team won its maiden U-20 Women’s World Cup in 2022, defeating Japan 3-1 in the final in Costa Rica. Spain added a second women’s title in 2026, further strengthening its record across both competitions. The achievement places Germany and Spain in a select group of countries that have conquered both sides of FIFA’s U-20 World Cup competitions.
