items.title: South Darfur civilians face ‘dire conditions, suffering beyond endurance’
items.description: Mershing locality in South Darfur, Sudan is facing worsening humanitarian and economic conditions following a sharp decline in agricultural production, driven by insufficient rainfall, shrinking cultivated areas, and encroachments on farmland. The local executive director warns that the near-total failure of the summer harvest is threatening residents’ livelihoods, as families move towards displacement areas in search of assistance. Meanwhile, local authorities are appealing for urgent humanitarian support and working to expand health, water, and education services. The executive director of Mershing locality in South Darfur, Oqba Abdel Hamid, says the summer agricultural season this year has suffered a sharp decline because of insufficient rainfall and a reduction in cultivated areas, as well as encroachments on farmland. He warns that this will have serious consequences for residents’ living conditions in the coming period. In an interview with Radio Dabanga, Abdel Hamid explains that Mershing is an agricultural locality whose economy depends on both summer and winter crops, as well as gardens and fruit and vegetable orchards. However, production during the current summer season has been extremely limited, after many farmers abandoned cultivation while others moved to different areas in search of better conditions. He estimates that only between 40 and 50 per cent of the farmers who normally cultivate their land each year entered this year’s agricultural season. Of those who began planting, only a limited proportion managed to cultivate their land and produce crops, estimated at around 20 per cent. The local official attributes the decline in agricultural activity to insufficient rainfall and economic difficulties, as well as farmers’ fears of repeated encroachments on agricultural land by herders. He says these factors have driven some residents to abandon farming or move elsewhere. He adds that these circumstances have had a direct impact on the harvest, which he describes as virtually non-existent during the current summer season, at a time when residents’ needs for food and humanitarian assistance are increasing. Families moving towards Tawila In a related development, Abdel Hamid reports that families from the locality have been moving towards displacement areas, particularly Tawila and Shangil Tobaya. He notes that some families have been influenced by what he describes as misleading campaigns promoting the availability of humanitarian assistance in other areas. He says intermediaries and brokers have been persuading residents to leave by promising them financial and food assistance immediately upon arrival, alongside information circulated by relatives and acquaintances who had previously been displaced to those areas. Abdel Hamid estimates that between 30 and 40 families have travelled to Tawila recently. He also points out that earlier movements towards Shangil Tobaya resulted in large numbers of families returning after discovering that conditions there did not match the expectations created before their departure. The executive director criticises intermediaries for exploiting residents’ needs, saying some families incur substantial travel expenses only to find that the conditions and assistance promised to them are unavailable upon arrival. He adds that the poorest and most vulnerable families are not necessarily those leaving. Some of the families who have departed had sufficient financial resources to cover transport costs, which he says can reach SDG 100,000 per passenger. “If a family consists of 10 people, the head of the household has to pay one million pounds. This is a substantial amount that could instead help the family meet its needs without having to leave, only to find that what is being promoted there is not available,” he says. Abdel Hamid rejects allegations that the local administration is obstructing humanitarian organisations or preventing them from reaching residents. He insists that the local authorities are working with organisations and contacting them to secure assistance and services. Appeals for urgent humanitarian intervention Abdel Hamid says the locality began engaging with humanitarian organisations and relevant authorities about two weeks ago to secure urgent interventions, amid declining agricultural production and growing needs among residents. He explains that a delegation comprising representatives of displaced people and newly displaced families, native administration leaders, community elders, young people, students, and women held meetings with relevant authorities at state level to present the locality’s needs, particularly in food and essential services. He says one organisation informed them that a programme was being prepared to conduct a new assessment of affected and vulnerable households across the localities, in order to identify beneficiaries of food and other material assistance. The assessment has already begun in other localities and is expected to include Mershing. The local administration is awaiting completion of the procedures agreed with the organisations before following up on the implementation of the interventions needed by families in the coming period. Expansion of health services On healthcare, Abdel Hamid announces that the number of functioning health centres in the locality has increased from four to eight. They are administered through the Ministry of Health, alongside centres providing child nutrition services. He explains that the local administration is working to develop health centres at the headquarters of administrative units and convert them into rural hospitals, completing arrangements for operating theatres and waiting rooms and providing the necessary medical equipment and supplies. He adds that the locality has received medicines for emergency cases, children, and malaria. Training programmes for healthcare workers are also under way in cooperation with the Ministry of Health, humanitarian organisations, the Red Crescent, the Red Cross, and the Academy of Health Sciences. The programmes cover midwives, nurses, paramedics, and health assistants. He says the locality has also been allocated an ambulance, while work is under way to establish an emergency and trauma hospital in Manawashi. Abdel Hamid explains that Manawashi was selected because of its location along one of the main roads and its potential to serve a wide geographical area. He confirms that the project is being developed in partnership with humanitarian organisations working in the health sector. On veterinary services, Abdel Hamid announces the arrival of 5,000 doses of animal vaccines as part of efforts to protect livestock from disease. The locality is seeking to expand vaccination coverage to between 50,000 and 100,000 head of livestock. He says concerns about the spread of animal diseases in neighbouring countries make vaccination programmes a priority for protecting livestock, on which residents depend for their livelihoods. Repairing water pumps and switching to solar power On water supplies, Abdel Hamid says the local administration has begun repairing a large number of hand pumps. More than 70 pumps have undergone maintenance, work is under way on more than 20 others, and a further 12 are included in a comprehensive maintenance programme. He adds that the locality has secured funding to convert the Abu Hamra water station to solar power, as part of a broader plan to switch several water stations to alternative energy sources. He says interventions are being directed towards those areas most in need and those experiencing water shortages, while efforts are under way to extend coverage to places without adequate water sources. In the same context, he announces that a partnership has been signed with organisations to raise the dam in the Wadi Halib area, with the aim of improving water storage over longer periods. This is intended to benefit farmers and owners of gardens and vegetable orchards, while providing water for residents and livestock during the summer months. He points out that the existing dam in Wadi Abor has produced positive results. Schools reopen and education receives support In the education sector, Abdel Hamid reports that 43 of the locality’s 64 schools have reopened, covering primary, intermediate, and secondary education. He says the schools that have resumed operations have teaching staff in place. He adds that arrangements for paying teachers’ salaries have been completed, following an initial period in which payments were made as a grant. The local administration expects regular salary payments to begin in the coming period. He points out that further assistance is needed from humanitarian organisations and the wider community, including school meals, textbooks, exercise books, chalk, blackboards, and classroom furniture. Support is also needed for teachers and young people working in emergency response and humanitarian relief rooms. Reconciliation efforts and reopening trade routes On social cohesion, the executive director says the local administration is working with the organisation Concordis, community leaders, native administrations, and young people to implement reconciliation initiatives, strengthen peaceful coexistence, and reopen roads and commercial streets. He explains that these efforts have included conferences and visits to several areas of the state, including Nitega and Mershing, with activities extending to other locations. Native administration leaders, young people, and security agencies have participated in efforts to rebuild social relations and facilitate commercial movement. The locality has also established community and youth committees in several areas, including Mershing, Manawashi, Doma, Jurf, Yara, Haluf, El Shadida, El Duqi, El Ban Jadeed, El Qardud, Umm El Qura, and Abu Hamra. He says a social peace conference was held in Abu Hamra last week and achieved positive results. On security, Abdel Hamid describes the situation in the locality as stable, saying the security agencies and formations present are working to maintain order. He acknowledges some isolated incidents of insecurity but says they have not reached widespread levels. He confirms that commercial and community activities, as well as sporting events, are continuing in the locality. However, he stresses that despite ongoing efforts, residents’ needs require wider intervention from the government and humanitarian organisations, particularly in food, water, healthcare, and education. Mershing locality continues to face overlapping challenges, including declining agricultural production, growing humanitarian needs, and shortages of services in some areas, making food assistance and improvements to essential services among the most pressing priorities in the coming period. items.title: Guinée vs Érythrée : à 48 heures du match, l’équipe d’Erythrée déjà sur place et le Syli national toujours au compte-gouttes
items.description: A deux jours de sa confrontation avec l’Érythrée, comptant pour la 3ᵉ journée des éliminatoires de la CAN 2027, le Syli national peine à lancer son regroupement à Conakry. Selon nos informations, le sélectionneur Paulo Duarte ne dispose, pour le moment, que de huit joueurs, dont deux évoluant au Horoya AC. Le début de la préparation des hommes de Paulo Duarte enregistre des difficultés. À 48 heures de cette rencontre importante, le technicien portugais ne compte que huit joueurs à sa disposition pour entamer le travail collectif. Parmi les joueurs déjà présents figurent deux éléments du Horoya AC. Un effectif particulièrement réduit qui complique les préparatifs du Syli national à quelques heures de ce rendez-vous face à la sélection érythréenne. Pendant ce temps, l’adversaire de la Guinée a déjà pris ses quartiers dans la capitale guinéenne. Arrivée en petits groupes, la sélection érythréenne aurait même déjà entamé sa préparation en vue de cette troisième journée des éliminatoires. Selon des informations non encore officielles, ce retard dans le regroupement du Syli national serait lié à l’émission des billets d’avion de certains joueurs convoqués. Aux dernières nouvelles, Paulo Duarte devrait diriger sa première séance d’entraînement ce mardi avec seulement huit joueurs à sa disposition. La première manche de la double confrontation avec l’Érythrée est prévue ce jeudi 12 novembre, au stade du 28 septembre de Conakry tandis que le match retour aura lieu le 16 novembre au Caire, en Égypte. items.title: Britain says its bases are safe after US refuelling planes evacuated
items.description: Britain said on Tuesday that its military bases were safe, after the US removed huge refuelling aircraft from a British airbase following what the Wall Street Journal said was a threat from Iran, the second such apparent evacuation in three months. Commercially available flight tracking data showed at least 10 Boeing KC-135R Stratotanker refuelling planes left the Royal Air Force base in Mildenhall, eastern England, on Monday. One flew to a base in Germany, one to Scotland and two to Spain, while the destinations of the other six were not reported. At least three Osprey multipurpose aircraft also departed from Mildenhall and landed at Lakenheath, another RAF base 4 miles away. Video filmed by a member of the public from outside the base and verified by Reuters showed two Ospreys taxiing on the runway after landing at Lakenheath. Asked about the moves, the US European Command said the Air Force moves aircraft between locations for a variety of reasons, and it would not comment on force protection measures for operational security reasons. A spokesman for Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the protection of Britain’s military bases was a top priority, and that the government worked closely with the police and allies to protect them. Security measures were kept under constant review and the government was investing in air defence and counter-drone capabilities, he said. Asked if he was confident that Britain’s bases were safe, he said: “Yes.” The White House and the Pentagon did not immediately respond to requests for comment sent outside regular business hours. US removed bombers in September According to the Wall Street Journal , the evacuations were prompted by a threat from Iran . The precise nature of the threat was under discussion among US officials, it said. Iran has denied any links to specific attacks in Britain , but its Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps (IRGC) have said airbases used by US forces there and in other countries are legitimate targets . Britain has been warning for months that Iran has been planning attacks, recruiting people online to carry them out. In September, the US removed bombers that had been used to strike Iran from another British base, RAF Fairford , on security grounds after a group of men approached the base in white vans. Two men were charged last month in relation to that incident, with prosecutors alleging one of them had tried to assist Iranian intelligence in Britain. Britain’s domestic spy chief Ken McCallum said in a speech last month that Iran-linked operations had led to more than 50 arrests over the past year. Iran was ramping up attempts to hit harder targets such as military sites in the UK, even though its previous activity had been limited by the lack of sophistication of the criminals it used as proxies, he said. The US upgraded the security posture at RAF Mildenhall and another UK base, RAF Lakenheath, to FPCON Charlie, the second-highest defensive threat level, the Wall Street Journal report said, citing a US official familiar with the matter. The Fairford incident, which remains largely unexplained, attracted huge international attention at a time of heightened concern about the security implications for Western states of the war between the United States and Iran. Burnham has said the activity at RAF Fairford was “highly likely” to have been coordinated in Iran.

Lutte contre les addictions: La méthode OUBDA présentée aux hommes de médias
items.description: Le président-directeur général (PDG) d’Argile Santé, Oumarou Oubda, a rencontré des hommes de médias, le dimanche 1er novembre 2026, au siège de sa structure, à Ouagadougou. Cette rencontre avait pour objectif de présenter une nouvelle approche de lutte contre les addictions, dénommée « méthode OUBDA ». Selon les chiffres de l’Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) et du ministère en charge de la Santé, le tabagisme est à l’origine d’environ 4 800 décès par an au Burkina Faso, avec plus de 1 300 non-fumeurs victimes du tabagisme passif. La consommation de substances psychoactives (tabac, alcool, drogues et autres produits) constitue ainsi une préoccupation majeure de santé publique. Au-delà des conséquences sanitaires, les addictions fragilisent les familles, compromettent l’avenir de nombreux jeunes et pèsent lourdement sur la communauté, selon Oumarou Oubda, promoteur de la « méthode OUBDA ». Pour le promoteur, cette méthode constitue une nouvelle approche dans la lutte contre la consommation de substances psychoactives. Elle repose sur l’utilisation de la poudre d’une plante dénommée «Annona senegalensis» et sur un accompagnement psychologique sous forme de thérapie de groupe. Cette dernière vise notamment à rétablir les relations entre la personne concernée par l’addiction et son entourage. Oumarou Oubda présente cette initiative comme une contribution aux efforts engagés en faveur de l’amélioration de la santé des populations, sous l’impulsion du président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. La rencontre avec les journalistes a également été marquée par une séance de présentation et d’expérimentation de la méthode. À cette occasion, certains jeunes désireux de sortir de la dépendance aux substances psychoactives ont accepté de participer à cette expérience. Inoussa Zoromé, agriculteur résidant à Ouagadougou, affirme avoir ressenti des vertiges et une envie fréquente de cracher après avoir consommé le produit. « Mon désir est d’abandonner la cigarette », confie-t-il. Même volonté chez Abdoul Fatah Ouédraogo, commerçant à Ouagadougou, qui explique sa motivation par les souffrances de sa mère face à son addiction au tabac. « Je trouve que ma mère souffre énormément lorsqu’elle me voit fumer. Je veux vraiment abandonner la cigarette », témoigne-t-il. La rencontre a connu la participation de représentants de la Gendarmerie nationale, du commissariat de police, de la mairie de l’arrondissement 11 de Ouagadougou ainsi que de chefs coutumiers. Ces participants ont indiqué être venus s’informer sur la méthode et assister à sa présentation. Représentant le président de la délégation spéciale, le président de la commission des affaires générales, culturelles et sociales de la mairie de l’arrondissement 11, Abdoulaye Tarnagda, a salué une initiative qui, selon lui, vient renforcer les efforts de la municipalité dans la lutte contre le tabagisme. Il estime également qu’elle pourrait contribuer à réduire le banditisme et à sauver des vies. La rencontre a aussi été ponctuée de témoignages. Venue de la commune de Pouytenga, Maimounata Taita affirme avoir accompagné, l’année dernière, l’enfant d’une de ses connaissances auprès du promoteur de la méthode. Selon son témoignage, après près de six mois de prise en charge, le jeune aurait abandonné la consommation de stupéfiants et repris le chemin de l’école. Il vivrait aujourd’hui auprès de ses parents aux États-Unis d’Amérique. Une autre femme, qui a requis l’anonymat, affirme que son frère cadet, autrefois dépendant à la drogue, a également bénéficié de cette méthode. Elle indique qu’il a depuis acquis un tricycle et une machine de lavage automobile, et qu’il mène désormais une activité professionnelle. Selon son promoteur, la méthode OUBDA aurait permis d'accompagner près de 8 000 jeunes confrontés aux addictions. David Demaison NEBIE

Maroc–Israël : une nouvelle visite de haut niveau pour renforcer la coopération militaire
items.description: La cooperation militaire entre le Maroc et Israel continue de se renforcer. En visite officielle a Rabat du 8 au 11 novembre, Amir Baram, directeur general du ministere israelien de la Defense, a ete recu par Abdeltif Loudyi, ministre delegue charge de la Defense nationale. Accompagne d'une delegation, il s'est egalement entretenu avec le general Mohammed Berrid, inspecteur general des Forces armees royales. Au cœur des discussions figurent les achats d'equipements militaires, les technologies de defense, la cybersecurite et la formation. Les deux parties ont surtout evoque la creation d'une base industrielle de defense au Maroc, signe de leur volonte de depasser la simple relation entre fournisseur et client. Les echanges s'inscrivent dans une cooperation militaire structuree, pilotee notamment par une commission conjointe. Une cooperation qui ne cesse de se renforcer Ce rapprochement remonte a la normalisation des relations diplomatiques de decembre 2020, negociee sous l'egide des etats-Unis. En contrepartie, Washington avait reconnu la souverainete marocaine sur le Sahara occidental, territoire dispute avec le Front Polisario. Des 2021, Rabat et Tel Aviv avaient signe un accord de cooperation en matiere de defense, ouvrant la voie a des echanges de renseignements, a des exercices et a des acquisitions d'armements. La cooperation reste active. En octobre, Israel a participe pour la premiere fois au salon aeronautique de Marrakech, ou plusieurs entreprises de defense ont presente leurs technologies, notamment dans les drones et les systemes autonomes. Mais cette proximite strategique contraste avec l'opposition d'une partie de l'opinion marocaine a la normalisation, ravivee par la guerre a Gaza. La visite d'Amir Baram illustre ainsi la volonte des deux gouvernements de preserver leur partenariat securitaire malgre les tensions regionales.

items.title: Prepare to meet us in court – Rent Commissioner tells UGEL management
items.description: Rent Commissioner Frederick Opoku has warned the management of the University of Ghana Enterprises Limited (UGEL) to prepare for possible legal action over its handling of accommodation fee increases at the University of Ghana. He says the Rent Control Department is considering legal action against UGEL for alleged non-compliance with the Rent Act, insisting that the department will no longer tolerate attempts by institutions to disregard its directives. Speaking on Adom FM’s Dwaso Nsem , Mr Opoku disclosed that he had cautioned the UGEL Chief Executive Officer during a meeting about the potential legal consequences of breaching the law, including a possible jail term. “At the meeting, I strongly warned the UGEL CEO that he risks going to jail because the Rent Act provides for a custodial sentence for certain breaches,” he said. The Commissioner added that the department was seeking legal advice from the Attorney-General’s Office and was confident that the matter could proceed to court if UGEL failed to comply with the law. “We are taking advice from the Attorney-General, and I am sure we will be suing them for non-compliance and illegality. I believe the Attorney-General will get them prosecuted, and they will face the full rigours of the law,” he warned. Mr Opoku gave UGEL seven days to demonstrate its willingness to comply with the department’s directives or face possible legal proceedings. “They have seven days to show their muscles or meet us in court,” he declared. He said the department was determined to enforce its mandate, warning that it would no longer allow institutions to treat Rent Control as an authority without the power to act. “A time has come when people are calling the bluff of Rent Control and refusing to face the law. If the GRA, NPA and other regulatory bodies issue directives and people respect them, nobody should think Rent Control is a toothless bulldog. That is no more,” he said. The warning comes amid growing controversy over proposed accommodation fee increases at the University of Ghana, which has triggered student protests and calls for greater transparency in the management of hostel charges. Mr. Opoku has maintained that although landlords and accommodation providers may seek to increase rent, they must follow the prescribed legal procedures and justify proposed increases to the department.

items.title: e-Crime Bureau signs cybersecurity partnership with Smart Africa to strengthen continental digital security
items.description: Cybersecurity consulting firm e-Crime Bureau has signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the Smart Africa Secretariat to support the development of cybersecurity and strengthen digital security across Africa. The agreement was signed in Accra, Ghana, on Monday, November 2, 2026, on the sidelines of the 15th Africa Internet Governance Forum (AfIGF) 2026. The partnership will focus on supporting cybersecurity innovation and building capacity across the continent. It comes as Smart Africa intensifies efforts to promote cybersecurity through a coordinated continental approach, including the development of the Continental Cybersecurity Blueprint in 2023 and the establishment of the African Network of Cybersecurity Authorities (ANCA) as a consultative body for cybersecurity development. Under the agreement, the two institutions will collaborate in three key areas: people, processes and technology. On people, the partnership will focus on developing Africa’s cybersecurity workforce and skills while promoting cooperation among the private sector, governments and the international community. Regarding processes, the parties will work to strengthen governance and risk management, including the protection of critical information infrastructure, as well as promote legal and policy harmonisation across the continent. In the area of technology, they will collaborate on developing and deploying solutions to protect Africa’s digital ecosystem. Speaking at the signing ceremony, Director General and Chief Executive Officer of Smart Africa, Mr Lacina Koné, said Africa’s digital transformation depended on the strength of the systems protecting its digital infrastructure. “Africa’s digital transformation can only be as strong as the systems that protect it. Cybersecurity is a shared responsibility that requires stronger cooperation, coordinated action and sustained investment in our people and institutions,” he said. He said the partnership with e-Crime Bureau would help strengthen cybersecurity expertise, improve institutional coordination and advance the protection of critical digital infrastructure across the continent. Mr Koné reaffirmed Smart Africa’s commitment to working with the Bureau to implement the objectives of the agreement. The partnership follows e-Crime Bureau’s restructuring into a global cybersecurity consulting firm, with operational hubs in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. The restructuring was approved by the company’s Board of Directors in 2026 as part of its Transition & Growth Strategy, which builds on the firm’s 15 years of experience to expand its services across international markets, particularly in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. The European hub, based in Como, Italy, focuses on standards, certifications, regulatory best practices, research, innovation and technology partnerships. It also coordinates engagements with development partners. The Middle East hub leads business development and service delivery, while the African hub, based in Accra, Ghana, concentrates on talent and skills development to support the company’s global operations. Commenting on the development, Executive Chairman of the e-Crime Bureau, Dr Albert Antwi-Boasiako, said the expansion and partnership with Smart Africa marked a new chapter for the company. “Our expansion and our partnership with Smart Africa mark a new era for the Bureau. With global hubs in Europe, the Middle East and Africa, we serve as a bridge that connects expertise, talent, experience, insights and technology, providing our clients with the full strength of the firm, regardless of where they operate,” he said. He added that the company would work with Smart Africa and its partners to advance cybersecurity development across the continent by building the skills, infrastructure and resilience required to support a digital economy. The partnership brings together Smart Africa’s work in cybersecurity and e-Crime Bureau’s technical expertise, with the shared objective of advancing cybersecurity innovation and capacity development across Africa. e-Crime Bureau is a global cybersecurity consulting firm incorporated and operating through its hubs in Europe, the Middle East and Africa. Its consulting practice connects expertise across the three regions, combining established track records, technology solutions, regulatory standards and contextual business knowledge to deliver measurable results to clients. The firm works with governments, private sector organisations and international partners to strengthen cyber resilience. It combines technical expertise with practical experience in global standards, regulations, risk management and business strategy to help clients anticipate threats, respond proactively to incidents and build lasting resilience.

President Mahama to launch Ghana Heritage Series Banknotes on 12 November
items.description: President John Dramani Mahama will officially launch the Ghana Heritage Series Banknotes on Thursday, 12 November 2026, at Bank Square, Accra. The launch introduces a new generation of banknotes designed to enhance security, durability, and efficiency. Speaking ahead of the launch, Dr Johnson Pandit Asiama, Governor of the Bank of Ghana, said the upgraded banknotes form part of the Bank’s efforts to modernise Ghana’s currency and respond to evolving economic and technological developments. Introduced under the theme, “The Cedi, Our Future: Secure, Designed to Last,” the Heritage Series reflects the Bank’s commitment to maintaining a resilient and secure currency system According to the Governor, the current core banknote designs have been in circulation for more than two decades, making periodic upgrades necessary to meet modern security standards and support effective currency management. The new notes incorporate advanced security features, enhanced durability, and contemporary designs that celebrate Ghana’s rich heritage while reflecting the nation’s aspirations for the future. These improvements are expected to strengthen protection against counterfeiting and ensure the banknotes can withstand prolonged circulation. The Central Bank noted that the upgraded series will also contribute to more efficient and cost-effective currency management. It has assured the public that the introduction of the Heritage Series does not invalidate existing banknotes. Current Ghana Cedi banknotes will remain legal tender and will circulate alongside the new series. The public has therefore been advised not to rush to exchange or withdraw existing banknotes following the launch of the Heritage Series. The Central Bank further urged Ghanaians, businesses, traders, and financial institutions to handle banknotes responsibly by avoiding practices such as crumpling, writing on, stapling, spraying, or using currency for decorative purposes, including money bouquets. According to the Bank, proper handling of banknotes helps preserve their quality, reduces replacement costs, and supports efficient currency management. The public is encouraged to embrace the Heritage Series with pride and contribute to protecting the integrity and value of Ghana’s national currency.

items.title: Clôture du SIAO 2026 : La 19e édition prévue du 27 octobre au 5 novembre 2028
items.description: Le Président de l’Assemblée législative du peuple (PALP), Ousmane Bougouma, représentant le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, a présidé la cérémonie officielle de clôture de la 18 e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO), samedi 7 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou La 18 e édition du Salon international de l’artisanat de Ouagadougou (SIAO) a officiellement refermé ses portes, samedi 7 novembre 2026, à Ouagadougou. Elle a été marquée par la Nuit des artisans méritants(NAM) et la remise des chèques et attestations de reconnaissance aux acteurs du secteur. Le PALP, Ousmane Bougouma a exhorté les artisans à persévérer dans la même dynamique pour accompagner l’élan d’affirmation de la souveraineté. « Pendant dix jours, Ouagadougou a été le rendez-vous de la créativité, de l’innovation et de l’entrepreneuriat africain, réunissant artisans, créateurs, entrepreneurs, acheteurs et chercheurs, tous convaincus que l’Afrique peut et doit davantage s’appuyer sur ses propres talents, ses ressources et son savoir-faire pour construire son avenir », a expliqué le Président de l’Assemblée législative du peuple (PALP), Ousmane Bougouma, représentant le Président du Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré. Selon le ministre chargé de l’Artisanat, Serge Gnaniodem Poda, les artisans venus du monde entier ont progressé en qualité. Selon lui, cette édition a accueilli plus de 6 000 exposants, artisans, tenanciers de buvettes, restaurateurs et partenaires issus d’environ 30 pays, plus de 400 acheteurs et visiteurs professionnels, environ 230 rencontres d’affaires B to B et plus de 800 000 visiteurs. 523 journalistes et 96 médias accrédités de sept pays ont assuré la couverture médiatique de l’événement. Pour lui, ces performances confirment la place du SIAO comme vitrine de l’artisanat africain et contribue à la création d’emplois et à la lutte contre la pauvreté. Pour le ministre chargé de l’Artisanat, Serge Gnaniodem Poda, le SIAO dépasse les frontières du Burkina Faso. Selon lui, le Prix spécial Thomas Sankara de la créativité a été décerné à un Burkinabè, Yempabou Tankouano grâce à son Métier à Tissé automatique baptisé Findi. Cette œuvre répond, a-t-il ajouté, au thème principal de cette édition du SIAO et aux idéaux du capitaine Thomas Sankara. Wendaabo Cathérine KOURAOGO Crédit Photo : Edith BAKALA

items.title: Meurtre du chef du canton de Solenzo : 12 accusés sur 19 présents à l’ouverture du procès
items.description: L’audience foraine de la chambre criminelle du Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Dédougou s’est ouverte à Solenzo, le lundi 9 novembre 2026. Un seul dossier impliquant 19 accusés est inscrit au rôle de cette session foraine. Il s’agit de l’affaire concernant la manifestation publique organisée le 24 novembre 2024 dans la capitale de la province des Banwa qui a malheureusement débouché sur la mort tragique du chef du canton de cette localité . Sur les 19 personnes incriminées, 12 ont comparu devant la chambre criminelle du Tribunal de grande instance (TGI) de Dédougou, selon le correspondant de l’Agence d’information du Burkina (AIB) sur place. Il leur est reproché des faits de participation à une manifestation illégale, de destruction volontaire de biens privés et de meurtre à l’encontre du chef du canton de Solenzo au moment des faits, déroulés le 24 novembre 2024. À cette première journée d’audience, huit accusés se sont succédé à la barre pour s’expliquer et répondre aux questions du tribunal. La majorité n’a pas reconnu les faits alors que deux accusés ont reconnu avoir participé à la marche, précise notre source. Cependant, ils sont catégoriques qu’ils n’ont rien détruit au cours de la manifestation encore moins fait quoique que ce soit chez le défunt chef du canton. Ils ont confié que dès que les manifestants sont arrivés à la hauteur du domicile du chef, ils se seraient retirés de la manifestation pour rentrer chez eux et c’est après qu’ils ont appris que le chef du canton a été faussé. L’audience a été suspendue autour de 18h. Elle reprendra le lendemain avec le passage des autres accusés à la barre. Yacouba BELEM

items.title: Ghana’s banking sector urged to embrace AI, technology to remain competitive
items.description: Ghana’s banking industry has been urged to leverage emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), to strengthen operations, improve customer confidence and remain competitive in the rapidly evolving financial landscape. The call was made by the Minister of Education, Haruna Iddrisu, at the 2026 Ghana Banking Conference organised by the Chartered Institute of Bankers, Ghana, under the theme “Banking on the Future: Trust, Technology and Transformation.” Mr Iddrisu said the current macroeconomic stability presents an opportunity for the banking sector to reposition itself and support the country’s broader economic transformation. He stressed the need for financial institutions to take advantage of technological advancements while ensuring that innovation translates into improved services and greater financial inclusion. He also called for stronger financial literacy, particularly at the basic education level, to equip young people with the knowledge to make informed financial decisions. President of the Chartered Institute of Bankers, Ghana, Dr Ellen Ohene-Afoakwa, said the rapid changes in the banking industry make it necessary for professionals to continuously upgrade their skills to remain relevant. She explained that the conference was designed to equip bankers with the knowledge and competencies required to respond to emerging developments in the sector. According to her, the institute is prioritising professional development, ethical conduct and technological advancement to prepare members for the future. She said, “We need to ensure that our members have the skill sets for their future,” adding that the profession must remain relevant as technology continues to reshape banking operations. Chief Executive of the Institute, Robert Dzato, also emphasised the importance of trust in sustaining the banking industry, describing character, competence and conduct as essential foundations of confidence in financial institutions. He said banks must work with other stakeholders to address emerging risks, particularly fraud and cybersecurity threats. “The business of banking is fast. It is the currency in banking, and that trust comes from character, competence and conduct of bankers,” he stated. Mr Dzato further disclosed that the institute intends to submit proposals to government to review the Chartered Institute of Bankers Act, 2019, to reflect developments in the financial services industry. He explained that the existing legislation focuses largely on regulating chartered bankers, although the banking industry has expanded beyond traditional banking practices. He said the proposed review would broaden the institute’s scope to strengthen professional development, ethical standards and sustainability within the sector. Mr Dzato added that the institute would also present its recommendations to relevant policymakers as government prepares the 2027 Budget. Meanwhile, Chief Marketing and Operations Officer at Npontu Technologies, Deborah Asmah, warned that banks risk losing significant business opportunities if they fail to adapt to emerging technologies, particularly tokenisation and artificial intelligence. She said financial institutions must move beyond discussions about technological advancement and begin integrating emerging solutions into their operations. “The banks cannot afford to cede the space as happened with mobile money,” she cautioned, urging financial institutions to build the necessary infrastructure and knowledge base to participate in the emerging tokenised economy. She noted that artificial intelligence presents both opportunities and risks for banks, particularly in fraud detection and cybersecurity. According to her, financial institutions must also recognise that significant transactions are taking place outside traditional banking channels, creating new competition for established banks. Ms Asmah therefore urged banks to take advantage of regulatory opportunities, training and partnerships to protect their market position. The 2026 Ghana Banking Conference brought together banking professionals, policymakers, regulators and industry experts to deliberate on the future of financial services, with discussions focusing on artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, virtual assets, stablecoins, tokenisation, digital transformation and ethical leadership.

items.title: Mali : le général russe Andreï Averianov décoré après avoir été annoncé mort par RFI
items.description: Le Mali a attribue une distinction honorifique a un haut responsable militaire russe dont la mort avait pourtant ete annoncee par RFI en avril dernier. Le lieutenant-general Andreï Vladimirovitch Averianov a ete eleve au grade de commandeur de l'Ordre national du Mali a titre etranger par le chef de l'etat malien, Assimi Goïta, selon un communique de la presidence publie le 9 novembre. La decoration lui a ete remise a l'issue d'une audience accordee par le dirigeant malien a une delegation russe conduite par le general. La rencontre s'est tenue en marge du Salon international de la defense et de la securite de Bamako ( BAMEX ), organise du 9 au 11 novembre. La distinction est motivee par la contribution d'Andreï Averianov au renforcement de la cooperation entre le Mali et la Russie, particulierement dans les domaines de la defense et de la securite. Le general russe a exprime sa reconnaissance, selon le communique. RFI avait annonce sa mort avant de retirer son article L'apparition officielle survient dans un contexte particulier. Le 3 avril 2026, RFI avait publie une enquete dans laquelle le media affirmait, sur la base de deux sources libyennes, qu'Andreï Averianov avait peri lors d'une attaque contre le methanier russe Qendil , au large de la Libye, en decembre 2025. L'information avait ensuite ete dementie par l'ambassade de Russie en Libye, qui avait assure que le general etait vivant et en bonne sante. Des elements contredisant le recit initial de RFI avaient aussi emerge. Le president de l'Assemblee nationale malgache avait notamment indique que le general avait conduit une delegation russe a Madagascar le 20 decembre 2025, soit apres la date supposee de son deces. Des medias russes avaient par ailleurs rapporte une rencontre entre Andreï Averianov et une delegation malgache a Moscou en fevrier 2026. Une photographie de l'entretien avait en outre ete relayee par le collectif All Eyes on Wagner. Face aux contradictions, RFI avait finalement supprime son article, reconnaissant ne pas avoir tenu compte des informations attestant de la presence du general a Madagascar apres la date a laquelle il etait presume avoir ete tue. Le media avait presente ses excuses a ses lecteurs pour les erreurs commises.

items.title: Lutte contre la fraude et l’insécurité : La CNLF saisit un important lot de matériels explosifs dans une gare routière à Ouagadougou
items.description: La Coordination Nationale de Lutte contre la Fraude (CNLF) a réalisé une importante saisie de matériels explosifs, le mercredi 04 novembre 2026, lors d’un contrôle inopiné dans une gare routière à Ouagadougou. L’inspection d’un colis destiné à être expédié sous une fausse identité a permis de découvrir 25 têtes de détonateurs, 495 bâtons d’explosifs et 02 rouleaux de cordons détonants. L’expéditeur avait quitté les lieux après avoir indiqué qu’un inconnu viendrait récupérer le colis à destination. Le Coordonnateur national a souligné la gravité de cette saisie, qui représente une double menace : la possibilité que ces matériels tombent entre les mains d’ennemis de la Nation et le danger qu’ils font peser sur les passagers et les populations riveraines. Il a, par ailleurs, appelé les transporteurs à une vigilance accrue, notamment par la vérification systématique de l’identité des expéditeurs et des destinataires ainsi que de la licéité des colis, rappelant que leur responsabilité pourrait être engagée conformément aux dispositions de l’article 415 du Code des douanes. Les investigations se poursuivent pour identifier les auteurs et leurs éventuels complices afin qu’ils répondent de leurs actes devant la justice. Minute.bf

Prenant la parole, Balla Moussa Fofana a transmis à la famille religieuse, dirigée par Serigne Moustapha Mbacké, les salutations et les remerciements du chef de l’État et de l’ensemble du gouvernement. Il a souligné que la forte délégation gouvernementale témoigne de l’importance accordée par le président de la République à cette célébration et à Mbacké Cadior. Il a également assuré que les services de l’État avaient été mobilisés pour garantir le bon déroulement de l’événement, organisé dans le « berceau de la mouridiyyah ». Il a sollicité leurs prières pour la paix et la stabilité du pays, qu’il considère comme indispensables à la réussite de la mission du chef de l’État. items.title: DDC26 announces speakers to headline Ghana’s largest design conference
items.description: dEX Ghana Foundation has announced the speakers for DDC26, the seventh dEX Design Conference. The conference runs from 12 to 14 November 2026 at the National Theatre of Ghana under the theme Sustainable Design for People, Planet and Profit. Day 1 (People): Headlined by Daniel Ampofo (Founder & President, dEX Ghana Foundation), Day 1 brings together notable leaders across fashion, spatial design, media, UX, and industrial education, including Aisha Ayensu (Christie Brown), Constance Swaniker (DTI Africa), Rachael Tachie-Menson (Author Digital Labs), and Stefania Manfreda (Lokko House). Day 2 (Planet): Anchored by architect DK Osseo-Asare (Low Design Office / Penn State), Day 2 features visionary practice leaders across sustainable manufacturing, environmental storytelling, circular fashion, and eco-conscious design, including Travis Obeng-Casper (Ajabeng), Ama Adi-Dako Seidu (Big Fat African Development), Yayra Agbofah (The Revival), and Makafui Awuku (McKingtorch). Day 3 (Profit): Keynoted by Kwabena Owusu-Adjei (Thirdway Capital / Kenten), Day 3 convenes prominent figures across venture investment, broadcasting, creative strategy, photography, interior architecture, and digital transformation, including KKD, Francis Osei-Owusu, Nana Kofi Asihene, Audrey Forson (Tekura), and Bernard Sokpe (Jambo Spaces). “We chose speakers our community already looks up to and wants to learn from directly,” said Daniel Ampofo, Founder and President of dEX Ghana Foundation. “Every one of them has built something real. Their work shows that design from this continent can be ethical, ambitious and commercially strong at the same time.” Beyond the main stage, speakers will lead workshops and masterclasses across three breakout rooms, and several will take part in speed mentoring sessions with emerging designers and students. Workshops and masterclasses are open to Pro and Full Experience pass holders and are limited by room capacity. Passes are available at ticket.dexghana.org.

items.title: Partnerships key to unlocking Ghana’s mineral wealth – MIIF CEO
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Minerals Income Investment Fund (MIIF), Justina Nelson, has stated that deeper partnerships with international investors are key to unlocking Ghana’s mineral potential and driving greater value addition in the mining sector. According to her, Ghana’s mineral wealth offered significant opportunities for investors, particularly in bauxite, iron ore, manganese and graphite, as the country seeks to move beyond the export of raw minerals towards value addition and industrial production. Speaking on the sidelines of the 2026 China (Guangxi)–ASEAN Mining Cooperation Conference in China on Friday, November 6, Mrs. Nelson presented Ghana’s mineral resource potential and outlined investment opportunities for companies seeking to establish partnerships in the country. The conference on the theme: “Empowering China-ASEAN Mining Cooperation, Innovation and Development” brought together government officials, mining industry leaders, investors and other stakeholders across the world to explore investment opportunities, forge strategic partnerships and promote cooperation across the mining value chain. Ghana has an estimated 920 million tonnes of bauxite resources, while iron ore deposits at Sheini Hills are estimated at more than 1.7 billion tonnes. The country also has about 5.2 million tonnes of manganese resources, alongside opportunities for graphite exploration and further development within the Cape Coast lithium belt. Mrs Nelson outlined several areas for potential investment, including new and existing mining projects, joint ventures between foreign mining companies and Ghanaian contract miners, as well as the local manufacture of mining consumables. She further identified opportunities in alumina refining, smelting technology, iron and steel production, and the manufacture of battery-grade manganese, all of which could support the development of Ghana’s domestic mineral processing industry. A key area she highlighted was the development of an integrated iron and steel industry. According to her, domestic mine-to-steel production could potentially replace about US$528 million in annual iron and steel imports, based on 2023 figures. Mrs Nelson’s engagement at the conference forms part of MIIF’s broader efforts to promote Ghana as an investment destination and position its mineral resources as a catalyst for industrialisation, job creation and sustainable economic growth. Enabling environment The Deputy Minister of Lands and Natural Resources, Alhaji Yusif Sulemana, said Ghana’s laws and policies were open to investment, adding that the government was committed to creating favourable conditions for international businesses. He said the Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources and relevant government agencies remained ready to support investors and facilitate partnerships that would contribute to the development of the mining industry. Therefore, he encouraged Chinese companies to explore opportunities in Ghana’s mining, mineral processing and related industries, emphasising the importance of long-term partnerships that would benefit both countries.

items.title: Businesses must strengthen corporate governance to attract investment – GIPA
items.description: The Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority (GIPA), Simon Madjie, has urged local businesses to strengthen corporate governance, improve financial transparency and formalise their operations to attract domestic and foreign investment. He says the ability of businesses to attract capital depends largely on the trust they build with investors, the quality of their projects and measures to reduce investment risks. Speaking at the Ghana Economic Forum organised by the Business and Financial Times (B&FT), he identified trust, bankable projects and de-risking as three critical factors needed to mobilise capital for businesses. According to him, businesses cannot expect to attract investment without credible financial records and sound corporate governance structures. “You simply can’t attract capital when you don’t have good financials. But we have to go back to the basics. How do we run a local business, and how come we are unable to attract capital?” he said. Mr Madjie urged businesses to move beyond informal operational structures and adopt practices that make them more attractive to investors. He also encouraged local businesses to embrace partnerships and collaboration, arguing that pooling resources could help them overcome capital constraints and expand their operations. “When we work together, we can get the capital that we need. Your 10, it is my 10; when we put them together, that is close to 50 cedis,” he stated. He further called for policies that promote technology transfer, build local capacity and encourage greater participation of Ghanaian businesses in investment activities. Mr Madjie said reforms to Ghana’s investment laws, including the Ghana Investment Promotion Authority Bill, which has now become law, were important for improving investor protection and reducing barriers to investment. However, he stressed that regulatory reforms must be complemented by changes in how businesses operate and collaborate to help Ghana attract the capital needed to drive economic growth.

items.title: Obi will run to Cameroon if confronted with burdens of presidency – Wike
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has accused the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, of lacking the capacity to tackle the myriads of Nigeria’s challenges but would instead flee to Cameroon if handed the responsibilities of the presidency. Wike spoke on Tuesday at the Abaji Area Council Rainbow Coalition and Stakeholders’ Meeting in Abuja, where he urged FCT residents to back President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. He said Obi would run away from the country’s problems instead of tackling them headlong, unlike Tinubu, whom he praised for taking difficult decisions. According to the minister, Nigeria needs a president who can confront hard situations and not abandon the country when challenges arise. He argued that the presidency is not a position for political theatrics or public relations but one that demands courage, capacity and the willingness to take responsibility. Wike asked the Abaji leaders to prove their support for Tinubu at the polls. He warned political leaders against making promises they cannot fulfil and said he would judge them by their ability to deliver their wards for the President in 2027. “Let me repeat what I said yesterday. To the people of Abaji, through their chairman, councillors and leaders, you come from different wards. You have told me you will vote for Tinubu. I have no problem with that. I want to see it,” he said. He specifically charged the Abaji Area Council chairman and other leaders to secure victory for Tinubu in their wards, stressing that leadership must be shown through electoral results. The minister said the FCT must not only match Rivers State in electoral performance but surpass it, adding that he was ready to apply the same political mobilisation strategy in Abuja. “Nobody is competing with Rivers. I don’t know what you all think. The only people who are going to compete with Rivers are the FCT. Whatever I will do there, I will do it here. So make sure you beat Rivers,” Wike said. Wike also cautioned residents against repeating what he described as the mistake of the 2023 elections, when they allegedly voted for candidates who did not keep in touch with their constituents after winning. “You went and elected somebody you don’t know. Is it not correct? Have you seen the person again? Has he come to address you? Has he asked you what your problems are? Has he moved anything that will affect the interest of the FCT?” he asked. The minister disclosed that he would meet FCT youths on Wednesday to discuss political mobilisation and other issues affecting their participation in the forthcoming elections. He assured stakeholders that the resources and arrangements for the electioneering campaign were being put in place and expressed confidence in the readiness of the Rainbow Coalition to mobilise support for Tinubu. Wike also reiterated his determination to have the electricity challenge in Abaji addressed before the 2027 elections and directed the area council chairman to intensify efforts to restore power supply. He urged residents to hold aspirants accountable for the development problems in their communities. items.title: Ogun Gov Poll: PDP candidate’s name not in party’s register, INEC tells court
items.description: … as LP chieftain alleges plot to compromise judge By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has explained to the Federal High Court in Abuja why it excluded Ogun State PDP candidate Mr Ladi Adebutu from its list of candidates cleared for the 2027 general elections. In a counter-affidavit deposed to by Mr Mustapha Mohammed, a Chief Program Analyst in its Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Department, the Commission told the court that Adebutu’s name was not found in the register of members the PDP earlier submitted to it. It told the court that it found only the name of the PDP’s deputy governorship candidate in the state, Kolapo Lateefat Oyeyemi, in the register. INEC’s counter-affidavit was in opposition to a suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/2573/2026, which the PDP and its Ogun State governorship candidate, Adebutu, filed against it. While the PDP is the 1st plaintiff in the matter, Adebutu is listed as the 2nd plaintiff, with INEC named as the sole defendant. It will be recalled that INEC had omitted Adebutu’s name from the final list of 13 candidates cleared to contest the Ogun State governorship election billed for February 6, 2027. Dissatisfied with the action, the PDP approached the court for an order compelling INEC to reverse its decision by recognising Adebutu’s candidacy. However, in the process it filed to challenge the competence of the suit, INEC said it had done due diligence before the final list of candidates for the election was published. According to the deponent, “I know as a fact that before the Governorship Candidates Final List was published, the ICT department conducted a search on the membership register submitted by the 1st plaintiff and during the search, the ICT department found the name of the 1st plaintiff’s candidate fielded as Deputy Governor of Ogun State (Kolapo Lateefat Oyeyemi) in the register but could not find the name of the 2nd plaintiff. “The search was also conducted to find a possible match for the name of the 2nd plaintiff, but no possible match was found in the Ogun State membership register. “That I know as a fact that all the queries conducted on the membership register in the flash drives (PDF/read only) submitted to the defendant by the 1st plaintiff do not contain the name of the 2nd plaintiff. “That the flash drive attached to the plaintiff’s affidavit and further affidavit in support of the Originating Summons was shown to me and I have carefully examined it, and I state that the contents of the flash drive are not the same as those submitted to the defendant. “That the first flash drive submitted by the 1st plaintiff to the defendant on 22 April 2026 had files named Ogun 01-038, while the second flash drive submitted to the defendant had files named Ogun 01-04, with serial numbers of members 1–18,973 and 1–19,308 respectively. “That serial number 1536 on the membership register submitted by the 1st plaintiff to the defendant contains the name of one Lugboso Sunday Seun and not the name of the 2nd plaintiff,” INEC’s witness further averred. It told the court that two flash drives were submitted to it alongside the hard-copy membership register, and neither contained the name and particulars of the 2nd plaintiff, Adebutu. Following the adoption of final addresses by the parties, Justice Peter Lifu fixed Friday for judgment. Meanwhile, a chieftain of the Labour Party (LP), Arabambi Abayomi, has alleged a plot to compromise the court into bypassing the Supreme Court judgment that activated Section 287(1) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, and compelled INEC to exclude political parties that failed to comply with Section 77(5)–(7) of the Electoral Act, 2026, in relation to the fielding of candidates. Abayomi, in a statement he made available to newsmen, further accused the Ogun State PDP candidate of perjury, alleging that he made false claims in an affidavit he deposed to in support of the suit against INEC. “The specific serial number Adebutu swore belonged to him—Serial Number 1536—actually belongs to one Lugboso Sunday Seun. INEC’s searches of the authentic registers found no match for Adebutu’s name whatsoever. “For a litigant to approach the Federal High Court and swear to an affidavit containing demonstrably false particulars is perjury. “It is an affront to the administration of justice. The evidential weight against Adebutu is not merely unfavourable, it is devastating,” Abayomi stated. Besides urging the Attorney General of the Federation to initiate an investigation into the alleged perjury, he called on the Chief Justice of Nigeria and the Chief Judge of the Federal High Court to look into the alleged plot to influence the outcome of the case. The post Ogun Gov Poll: PDP candidate’s name not in party’s register, INEC tells court appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: GWL says it lacks capacity to provide 24-hour water supply to all consumers
items.description: The Ghana Water Limited (GWL) says its current operational capacity does not allow it to provide uninterrupted water supply to all consumers across the country. The company says it is managing its available resources to ensure that communities receive water, although it cannot guarantee a round-the-clock supply. The Chief Manager for Corporate Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation at GWL, Michael Tawiah Klutse, said geographical differences, particularly the elevation of communities, also affect the distribution of water. He explained that residents in areas situated at higher elevations face greater difficulties accessing water because additional infrastructure and interventions are required to generate sufficient pressure to transport water to those locations. Mr Klutse said communities in lower-lying areas generally have better access because water can reach them more easily through the existing distribution network. He noted that the company’s limited capacity makes it difficult to maintain a continuous supply to every household. “We don’t have the capacity to serve every single person 24/7 at the moment. What we have is what we are managing for everybody to get something,” he said on Citi Breakfast Show on Tuesday, November 10. He added that additional measures were necessary to increase water pressure in communities located above the normal flow level. “If an area is a bit at elevations that are higher than our normal flow, we need to put in interventions to be able to build up pressure to those areas,” he explained.

items.title: France : une proposition de loi contre le commerce avec les colonies israéliennes adoptée en commission
items.description: La commission des affaires economiques de l'Assemblee nationale francaise a adopte, le 9 novembre, une proposition de loi visant a interdire les relations commerciales avec les colonies israeliennes etablies dans les territoires palestiniens occupes et sur le plateau du Golan syrien occupe. Porte par le premier secretaire du Parti socialiste, Olivier Faure, le texte sera examine le 19 novembre en seance publique. La proposition entend interdire l'importation, l'achat et la commercialisation de marchandises provenant des colonies israeliennes, considerees comme illegales au regard du droit international. Elle vise egalement les prestations de services, notamment financiers, susceptibles de contribuer a leur developpement ou a leur maintien. Les activites touristiques, comme la location de logements dans ces territoires, pourraient ainsi etre concernees. Opposition du RN et des Macronistes Pour Olivier Faure, cette initiative ne constitue pas une sanction generale contre Israel, mais vise a « mettre fin au financement d'une illegalite ». Le depute socialiste souhaite ainsi mettre les relations economiques francaises en conformite avec la position diplomatique de Paris, qui condamne la colonisation israelienne. Cosignee par plus d'une centaine de deputes issus de huit groupes parlementaires, la proposition a obtenu le soutien de la gauche et du MoDem. Elle a toutefois rencontre l'opposition des deputes macronistes et du Rassemblement national. Le depute Renaissance Sylvain Maillard denonce notamment un dispositif juge juridiquement imprecis, susceptible, selon lui, d'etre censure par le Conseil constitutionnel. Le texte prevoit jusqu'a un an de prison et une amende pouvant atteindre 5 % du chiffre d'affaires annuel mondial pour certaines prestations de services interdites. Si plusieurs pays europeens ont deja engage des demarches similaires, l'adoption definitive du texte francais reste incertaine. Son examen en seance publique promet de raviver les divergences sur les relations economiques avec Israel.

items.title: Protection des barrages: la police de l’eau libère les berges pour préserver durablement la ressource
items.description: Du 27 au 31 octobre 2026, la Direction générale des ressources en eau et de l’hydraulique (DGREH), à travers la Police de l’Eau, a conduit des opérations de contrôle et de libération des bandes de servitude autour de plusieurs barrages du Burkina Faso. Une action qui répond à un impératif : préserver les berges pour garantir la durabilité des ouvrages et la disponibilité de la ressource en eau. Ces opérations ont concerné les barrages de Samandéni et de Loumana, dans les régions du Guiriko et des Tannounyan, ainsi que celui de Ziga, dans la région de Oubri. Les barrages jouent un rôle stratégique dans l’approvisionnement en eau potable, le développement des activités agricoles et pastorales ainsi que la satisfaction des besoins des populations. Leur pérennité repose notamment sur la préservation de leurs berges. En effet, les bandes de servitude, espaces réglementairement réservés autour des retenues d’eau, contribuent à limiter l’érosion, à prévenir l’ensablement et à protéger la qualité de l’eau. Cependant, ces espaces font l’objet d’occupations diverses, notamment à travers l’installation de cultures, de campements de pêcheurs et d’équipements de pompage. Ces pratiques fragilisent les berges, favorisent leur dégradation et augmentent les risques de pollution des eaux. À terme, elles peuvent réduire les capacités de stockage des barrages et compromettre la disponibilité de la ressource pour les différents usages. Face à ces occupations, la Police de l’Eau a conduit les opérations avec l’appui d’une équipe de supervision de la DGREH, chargée d’accompagner les équipes régionales et de veiller à la bonne exécution des interventions. Les actions menées ont notamment porté sur la sensibilisation des occupants installés dans les bandes de servitude et la remise de sommations aux occupants concernés en vue de la libération des espaces irrégulièrement occupés. Un délai de trois mois a également été accordé aux responsables des installations de pêche pour se conformer aux exigences de protection des berges. Au-delà des opérations de libération, la mission a mis en évidence la nécessité de renforcer la surveillance des berges, de poursuivre les actions de sensibilisation auprès des populations riveraines et d’assurer un suivi régulier des sites concernés afin de prévenir de nouvelles occupations irrégulières. La préservation des barrages ne saurait se limiter à des interventions ponctuelles. Elle exige une vigilance permanente et une responsabilisation de l’ensemble des acteurs concernés. items.title: Mahama announces new offshore oil discovery in Deepwater Cape Three Points block

Speaking at the 2026 Petroleum Commission Local Content Conference and Exhibition in the Western region on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, Mahama described the find as an important milestone for Ghana’s petroleum industry, noting that it marks the country’s first successful test of a Cenomanian-Turonian carbonate play as a primary exploration target. “The hydrocarbon discovery at the N1 GDA 9 1 X well in the Deepwater Cape Three Points contract area marks an important milestone for Ghana. It is the country’s first successful test of a Cenomanian-Turonian carbonate play as a primary exploration target,” he said. The President said the well also targeted the Albian formation as a secondary exploration objective. “Today, the well also targeted the Albian as a secondary objective,” he added. The discovery adds to exploration activity in the Tano Basin, one of Ghana’s offshore petroleum areas. items.title: GRA exceeds 10-month revenue target with GH¢185.5bn collection as at October 2026
items.description: The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) has exceeded its revenue target for the first ten months of 2026, collecting GH¢185.5 billion against a target of GH¢184.4 billion. The collection represents a GH¢1.1 billion surplus over the January to October target, with the authority also surpassing its total revenue of GH¢182 billion recorded in 2025. Commissioner-General of the GRA, Anthony Kwasi Sarpong, disclosed this at the Ghana Economic Forum organised by the Business and Financial Times, expressing confidence that the authority will achieve its GH¢237 billion revenue target for 2026. “As at October 2026, we had collected GH¢185.5 billion against a target of GH¢184.4 billion for the 10-month period,” he said. He attributed the performance to ongoing reforms in tax administration, legislative reviews and the adoption of digital technologies to improve revenue mobilisation. Mr Sarpong said the authority’s broader ambition is to double its 2024 revenue collection of GH¢153 billion to approximately GH¢310 billion by December 2028. “Our ambition is to double the 2024 revenue to about GH¢310 billion by December 2028,” he stated. He highlighted the use of artificial intelligence in customs classification, the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) and planned implementation of fiscal electronic devices in 2027 as key measures to improve revenue collection. The Commissioner-General stressed that the GRA’s strategy is to broaden the tax base rather than increase the burden on existing compliant taxpayers. “Our objective cannot be to collect more and more from the same taxpayers, year after year. That approach has limits, and it places an ever-heavier burden on those who are already compliant,” he said.

items.title: Kompany returns to Bayern’s training ground for first time since collapse
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany returned to the club’s training ground on Tuesday for the first time since collapsing last month, beginning a gradual return to work ahead of the Bundesliga match against Cologne on November 20. The 40-year-old was at Bayern’s Säbener Straße complex shortly after 10am, according to German media reports. He worked from his office, spoke with assistant coach Floribert Ngalula and sporting director Christoph Freund, and watched injured players complete a recovery session. His return to the training ground does not mean he has resumed all his duties, as he is expected back in the dugout after the international break. Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching a training session involving Bayern’s reserve team. He was hospitalised and diagnosed with meningeal irritation, an inflammation affecting the tissue around the brain or spinal cord. He was later discharged to recover at home. Assistant Aaron Danks took charge during Kompany’s absence, overseeing four wins and a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund. Bayern beat Freiburg, Magdeburg, Atlético Madrid and Mainz. Danks said the club had instructed him to keep football discussions away from Kompany while he recovered. “I have clear instructions from Max [Eberl] and Christoph [Freund] not to engage in discussions, first of all, and to keep Vince focused on nothing other than his health and spending time with his family,” he said. “We want him to rest and recover properly so that, when he returns, he is fully fit and can help us in the best possible way. We are being very strict here and keeping football completely out of it.” Kompany’s father, Pierre, had previously described his son’s demanding work routine in an interview with Bild. “He works 18 hours a day most days and, on a typical day, barely sees his children,” he said, adding that Kompany was often at the training ground early and left late. Bayern are scheduled to host Cologne on November 20, when Kompany is expected to return to the touchline.
