items.title: Productions animales : Al Moutmir mise sur l’entrepreneuriat des jeunes
items.description: Faire de l’élevage un véritable levier d’entrepreneuriat et de création de valeur pour les jeunes constitue l’un des enjeux du développement des filières animales. Au-delà des activités d’élevage, le secteur offre des perspectives dans plusieurs domaines, de l’alimentation animale à la transformation, en passant par les services vétérinaires et la commercialisation. La production animale offre de réelles perspectives d'entrepreneuriat et de création de valeur pour les jeunes. Au-delà des activités d'élevage, les filières animales ouvrent des opportunités dans de nombreux domaines : alimentation animale, amélioration des pratiques d'élevage, services vétérinaires, transformation, valorisation des productions, commercialisation et développement de solutions innovantes. Faire de ce secteur un choix professionnel attractif pour les nouvelles générations suppose toutefois de dépasser les modèles traditionnels et de favoriser l'émergence d'activités plus professionnelles, productives, compétitives et économiquement viables. L'enjeu est de permettre aux jeunes de ne pas être uniquement les futurs éleveurs, mais de devenir des entrepreneurs, des innovateurs et des acteurs à part entière du développement des filières animales. La CoP Animal Productions : révéler les opportunités et accompagner les ambitions entrepreneuriales La troisième édition de la Communauté de pratique Animal Productions, organisée par Al Moutmir à Benguerir, a réuni une soixantaine de participants autour du thème de l'entrepreneuriat des jeunes dans les productions animales. Cette rencontre a placé les aspirations des jeunes, leurs initiatives et leurs perspectives d'investissement au cœur des échanges. Elle a permis de mettre en lumière les opportunités offertes par le secteur, tout en abordant les questions concrètes qui jalonnent le parcours entrepreneurial : comment identifier une opportunité et construire son projet ? Quels modèles d'activité privilégier ? Comment accéder aux compétences, aux ressources, aux services et aux financements nécessaires ? Comment s'organiser collectivement pour mutualiser les moyens et renforcer la viabilité des initiatives ? Les échanges ont notamment souligné que l'attractivité des productions animales repose sur la capacité à accompagner les jeunes dans la construction de véritables projets économiques. Cela implique de renforcer leurs compétences techniques et entrepreneuriales, de promouvoir des modèles d'installation adaptés aux réalités des territoires, d'améliorer la maîtrise technico-économique des activités et de faciliter l'accès aux services et aux débouchés. Les coopératives et les organisations professionnelles constituent, à cet égard, des leviers importants pour mutualiser les investissements, faciliter l'accès aux équipements et aux services, organiser les activités et renforcer la valorisation des productions. Une dynamique partenariale et écosystémique pour transformer les opportunités en réussite La réussite entrepreneuriale des jeunes ne dépend pas uniquement de leur motivation ou de leurs compétences. Elle repose également sur la qualité de l'environnement dans lequel ils entreprennent. La diversité des besoins, depuis la formation et l'accompagnement technique jusqu'au financement, aux infrastructures, aux services et à l'accès aux marchés, appelle une mobilisation coordonnée de l'ensemble des acteurs de l'écosystème. Institutions publiques, organismes de recherche et de formation, structures d'accompagnement entrepreneurial, acteurs financiers, organisations professionnelles, entreprises privées et professionnels des filières ont ainsi un rôle complémentaire à jouer. L'enjeu est de dépasser une logique d'interventions isolées pour construire de véritables parcours d'accompagnement intégrés, connectant les jeunes aux expertises, aux ressources et aux opportunités dont ils ont besoin à chaque étape de leur projet. Cette approche partenariale doit également favoriser l'émergence de solutions adaptées aux réalités territoriales et encourager les dynamiques collectives au sein des filières. Dans cette perspective, la CoP Animal Productions portée par Al Moutmir ambitionne de constituer un espace de convergence entre les besoins du terrain, les connaissances, l'innovation et les acteurs économiques et institutionnels. À travers le partage d'expériences, l'apprentissage collectif et la mise en relation des parties prenantes, elle contribue à faire émerger des réponses concrètes aux défis des productions animales et à renforcer les complémentarités au sein de l'écosystème. Faire des productions animales un secteur d'avenir pour les jeunes nécessite ainsi une ambition collective : révéler les opportunités, accompagner les initiatives et fédérer les compétences et les partenariats pour transformer le potentiel des filières en projets entrepreneuriaux viables, créateurs de valeur et durables pour les territoires. Des éleveurs témoignent de nouvelles perspectives Les participants ont également mis en avant les retombées des échanges et les perspectives ouvertes par cette rencontre, notamment en matière d'amélioration des performances des exploitations et de développement de projets entrepreneuriaux. « Cette rencontre a été pour nous un véritable espace d’échange, d’apprentissage et de réflexion entrepreneuriale. À travers les ateliers et les discussions avec les experts et les autres éleveurs, nous avons découvert de nouvelles pistes pour développer nos activités laitières et les transformer en projets plus performants et rentables. Nous avons notamment échangé sur les indicateurs à suivre pour améliorer la production, mesurer la rentabilité et mieux piloter nos exploitations. Cette CoP nous a également permis d'explorer des opportunités de business et de partenariat, essentielles pour accompagner les jeunes éleveurs qui souhaitent faire évoluer leur activité et construire un véritable projet entrepreneurial », détaille Abdelhadi Mouktad, éleveur laitier à Sidi Bennour. Pour sa part, Abdessamad Khayroun, éleveur à Sidi El Yamani près d'Assilah se réjouit de cette rencontre, « car nous avons bénéficié de l’expertise des cadres et des spécialistes sur des questions essentielles comme l’amélioration génétique de nos troupeaux, l’optimisation de la production et la recherche d’un équilibre entre performance technique et rentabilité économique. Au-delà des conseils techniques, cette CoP constitue un véritable espace d’entrepreneuriat qui nous ouvre de nouvelles perspectives pour développer nos projets d’élevage. Les échanges nous ont permis de mieux comprendre comment structurer nos activités, saisir les opportunités offertes aux jeunes entrepreneurs et identifier les partenariats susceptibles de nous accompagner. C’est aussi une occasion de passer d’une logique de production à une véritable vision de business agricole, avec des objectifs clairs et des perspectives de croissance ». The post Productions animales : Al Moutmir mise sur l’entrepreneuriat des jeunes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: GRA targets GH¢310bn revenue by 2028, rules out overburdening compliant taxpayers
items.description: The Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) is targeting revenue mobilisation of GH¢310 billion by December 2028, with plans to broaden the tax base and improve compliance without placing additional pressure on existing taxpayers. Commissioner-General of the GRA, Anthony Kwasi Sarpong, says the authority is focused on building a revenue system that grows with the economy and supports private-sector investment. “Our objective cannot be to collect more and more from the same taxpayers, year after year. That approach has limits, and it places an ever-heavier burden on those who are already compliant,” he said. Speaking at a Ghana Economic Forum organised by the B&FT, Mr Sarpong disclosed that the GRA collected GH¢153 billion in 2024 and GH¢182 billion in 2025. For 2026, the authority has set a target of GH¢237 billion. As of October, it had collected GH¢185.5 billion against a target of GH¢184.4 billion for the period. He attributed the improved performance to tax reforms, digitalisation and the use of artificial intelligence in customs classification. He also highlighted the rollout of the Integrated Tax Administration System (ITAS) and plans to fully implement fiscal electronic devices in 2027 to strengthen VAT compliance. Mr Sarpong said the authority is committed to making tax administration more efficient and supportive of businesses, particularly manufacturers importing raw materials and other production inputs. He argued that stronger domestic revenue mobilisation would reduce the government’s reliance on borrowing and free up more financing for private-sector businesses. “Every cedi that the state raises from a fair and broad-based tax system is a cedi it does not need to borrow from the finance market. That is fiscal space, and fiscal space is investment space,” he said. He urged businesses to meet their tax obligations while engaging the GRA on challenges that increase the cost of doing business. He said the ultimate goal is to make domestic revenue mobilisation a foundation for investment, industrial expansion and job creation.

items.title: Centralisation des salaires : Bjijou rassure les syndicats et confirme le maintien des garanties des fonctionnaires
items.description: La réforme du système de santé ne devrait pas remettre en cause le statut administratif des professionnels concernés ni les garanties dont ils bénéficient. C’est le message qu’a tenu à faire passer le ministre de la Santé et de la Protection sociale, Youns Bjijou, devant la Commission des secteurs sociaux à la Chambre des représentants, mardi 10 novembre, lors de l’examen du projet de budget sectoriel pour 2027. Il a notamment assuré que l’État continuera de prendre en charge les rémunérations des fonctionnaires concernés, ainsi que de préserver leurs droits et leurs acquis. Cette intervention intervient dans un contexte marqué par les interrogations suscitées par la centralisation de la gestion des salaires, alors que se poursuit le déploiement des groupements sanitaires territoriaux. Plusieurs professionnels de santé et partenaires sociaux ont exprimé leurs inquiétudes, notamment au sujet des crédits inscrits au titre des dépenses de personnel. Face à ces préoccupations, Bjijou a tenu à préciser que la centralisation des rémunérations ne procède pas d’une décision individuelle ou d’un dispositif transitoire. Elle s’inscrit, selon lui, dans un cadre juridique et réglementaire précis. Le ministre a notamment invoqué l’article 23 de la loi de finances pour 2025, qui prévoit le maintien de la prise en charge des salaires des fonctionnaires concernés par l’État. Il a également rappelé que les décrets encadrant les groupements sanitaires territoriaux prévoient la poursuite du traitement et du versement des rémunérations par la Trésorerie générale du Royaume. Une disposition destinée à garantir la continuité des engagements de l’État, alors que l’organisation du système de santé connaît une profonde évolution. Au-delà de la question salariale, le ministre a voulu lever toute ambiguïté sur le statut administratif des personnels. Celui-ci sera maintenu, a-t-il affirmé, excluant toute remise en cause, aussi bien à court terme qu’à l’avenir. Les garanties relatives aux rémunérations, aux droits et aux acquis professionnels resteront également préservées, conformément aux dispositions légales en vigueur. « Le maintien de ce statut constitue une garantie institutionnelle fondamentale pour assurer la stabilité des professionnels et préserver leurs droits, ainsi qu’un pilier essentiel de la confiance dans cette réforme », a-t-il déclaré. Le ministre a par ailleurs insisté sur la nécessité de maintenir le dialogue avec les professionnels de santé. Reconnaissant les inquiétudes que peuvent susciter les changements en cours, il a plaidé pour un renforcement de la communication et des mécanismes de concertation, afin de rassurer les personnels, de consolider leur mobilisation et de fédérer leurs efforts autour des objectifs de la réforme. Le dialogue social apparaît ainsi comme l’un des leviers de l’accompagnement des transformations engagées. Il doit notamment permettre de répondre aux interrogations des personnels, de clarifier les modalités de mise en œuvre des nouvelles dispositions et de préserver un climat de confiance entre le ministère, les professionnels et les partenaires sociaux. Pour Youns Bjijou, la réussite de cette transformation institutionnelle dépend également de la place accordée aux ressources humaines. La modernisation du système de santé ne saurait se limiter aux investissements et aux changements organisationnels : elle suppose aussi de motiver les personnels, de valoriser leurs compétences et de préserver leurs acquis. Les professionnels médicaux, infirmiers, techniques et administratifs constituent, à cet égard, un maillon essentiel du dispositif. Ce sont eux qui assurent la traduction concrète des investissements et des programmes engagés en prestations de soins au bénéfice des citoyens dans les établissements de santé. Le ministre a d’ailleurs souligné que sa conviction quant au rôle déterminant des professionnels dans la réussite de la réforme était profonde. Il a ainsi établi un lien direct entre la valorisation de leurs missions, la préservation de leurs acquis et la réussite de la transformation du système sanitaire. La stabilité des personnels représente, dans cette perspective, un investissement à part entière dans la performance de l’ensemble du dispositif. L’enjeu est aussi opérationnel. Le renforcement des capacités des établissements, l’amélioration de la qualité de la prise en charge et l’élargissement de l’accès aux soins nécessitent des équipes qualifiées, mobilisées et rassurées sur leur avenir professionnel. Autant de conditions jugées indispensables pour accompagner durablement les mutations du secteur. À travers ses déclarations devant les députés, Youns Bjijou entend ainsi dissiper les craintes entourant les conséquences administratives et financières de la réforme. Le maintien du statut de fonctionnaire, la continuité du versement des salaires par l’État et la préservation des droits et acquis constituent, selon ses assurances, des garanties qui accompagneront le processus de transformation du système de santé. La construction d’un service public de santé plus performant passe, a-t-il rappelé, par la reconnaissance du rôle de ses personnels et la garantie de leur stabilité au service des citoyens. items.title: Co-Conspirators in Malfeasance: The legal case for arresting both bribe-givers and public officers
items.description: Recent administrative petitions submitted to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs regarding the procurement of diplomatic passports have thrust a glaring spotlight on deep-seated administrative corruption. At the heart of these petitions lies a disturbing narrative: individuals allegedly paying off state officials to secure high-level sovereign travel documents to which they have no lawful right. When a petitioner attempts to utilize administrative channels to complain that a corrupt arrangement failed, a dangerous legal and moral fiction is exposed. The petitioner often attempts to cast themselves as an aggrieved customer cheated out of a service, but in reality, they are an active, willing participant in a corrupt enterprise. Under domestic anti-corruption frameworks, both the citizen who offers the bribe and the public official who accepts it are equally culpable. True institutional accountability demands that law enforcement agencies, including the Criminal Investigation Department, look past the self-serving framing of these petitions and arrest both parties. A cornerstone defense often floated in administrative corruption scandals is the claim of exploitation under the premise that state actors took their money. However, this argument collapses the moment legal eligibility is examined. A diplomatic passport is not a commercial commodity or a luxury item available to the highest bidder; it is a high-security instrument of state representing sovereign trust, international immunity, and official representation. By law, such credentials are strictly reserved for accredited diplomats, qualifying government officials, heads of state delegations, and designated high public officials under established administrative guidelines. If a petitioner is fundamentally ineligible for a diplomatic passport, every unit of currency handed to an official is an intentional inducement designed to subvert the law. The petitioner is not paying for a legitimate service, but rather for illegal state-sanctioned misrepresentation. By willingly participating in a scheme to bypass statutory vetting, the petitioner commits active bribery—an offence that treats the corrupt inducer with the same severity as the corrupt receiver. Conversely, the public officer who accepts money to issue or facilitate an unmerited passport commits a profound betrayal of public trust. Public servants take an oath to uphold the laws and constitution of the state, serving as custodians of national integrity. When an official monetizes administrative bottlenecks, creates artificial barriers, or sells sovereign travel credentials to unqualified applicants, they act as economic mercenaries within the civil service. This behaviour violates service regulations and degrades the international standing of the nation’s travel documents. When foreign border authorities realise that diplomatic credentials can be purchased through back channels, the security value and diplomatic courtesy extended to every legitimate passport issued by the state are severely compromised. This systemic threat requires rigorous enforcement of statutory instruments, notably the Criminal Offences Act, 1960 (Act 29), and the Criminal Offences (Amendment) Act, 2020 (Act 1034). Section 239 of Act 29 penalizes official corruption, wilful oppression, and extortion by public officers, while Section 252 strictly prohibits active participation in corrupting public officers through unlawful gratification. Furthermore, the legislative reforms introduced under Act 1034 reclassified corruption offenses to carry severe custodial sentences ranging from 12 to 25 years imprisonment. These stringent penalties reflect the legislative intent to eradicate corruption across both public and private sectors, ensuring that neither the bribe-giver nor the bribe-taker escapes judicial scrutiny. A half-baked anti-corruption campaign that targets only the bribe-taker while shielding the bribe-giver creates a dangerous moral hazard. It encourages citizens to treat state bribery as a viable transactional cost, operating under the assumption that if an application is rejected, they can simply pay their way through, and if caught, claim victimhood. To dismantle this cycle, the law must be applied uniformly. Without citizens willing to subvert rules with cash, corrupt networks within public offices would starve. A petition complaining that an illegal payment did not deliver the desired outcome is nothing less than a criminal confession wrapped in a grievance. When an ineligible applicant attempts to buy a diplomatic passport, both the hand that gives the bribe and the hand that takes it are tearing down the rule of law. The Criminal Investigation Department and relevant investigative bodies must treat these petitions not as civil disputes over service delivery, but as direct evidence of a criminal conspiracy. Interdicting compromised officials is a necessary administrative first step, but true justice requires the immediate arrest and prosecution of both the corrupt officers and the ineligible petitioners who sought to buy what they never deserved. The writer is Gilbert Attipoe, who can be reached at: Gilbertattipoe90@gmail.com

items.title: Ablekuma–Pokuase trotro drivers begin three-day demo over GPRTU charges
items.description: Trotro drivers plying the Ablekuma–Pokuase route have embarked on a three-day demonstration over what they describe as excessive increases in road charges allegedly imposed by the Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU). The drivers say charges at various loading points along the route have increased from GH¢10 to GH¢15, while fees at some locations have also risen from GH¢15 to GH¢20. They have expressed dissatisfaction with the increments, insisting that the new charges are placing additional financial pressure on their operations. The demonstration follows reported confrontations at some loading points, where drivers allege that land guards attacked colleagues who resisted attempts to compel them to load passengers at certain bus stops. The drivers reportedly called the police following the confrontation, leading to the arrest of some individuals alleged to be land guards. Meanwhile, some passengers who spoke to Adom News have expressed frustration over the demonstration, saying the disruption has left them stranded and affected their ability to commute. The affected passengers have appealed to the relevant authorities, the GPRTU and other stakeholders to intervene and resolve the dispute to restore normal transport services along the Ablekuma–Pokuase stretch. The drivers are demanding an immediate review of the road charges and measures to address what they describe as harassment and attacks at the various loading points.

items.title: Lawyer says Shah Mahmood Qureshi taken to hospital days after suffering fall
items.description: LAHORE: The lawyer representing Shah Mahmood Qureshi said on Tuesday that the senior PTI leader, who is currently incarcerated at Kot Lakhpat jail, was taken to the Punjab Institute of Cardiology (PIC) days after suffering a fall. Qureshi has been indicted in multiple cases pertaining to the May 9, 2023 riots and has remained behind bars since August 2023. In July 2024, the PTI leader was indicted by a Lahore anti-terrorism court in a case registered by the Shadman police over allegedly attacking and burning the police station. Speaking to Dawn , his counsel Rana Mudassar Umar said: “[Qureshi] was taken to PIC today as he fainted and suffered a fall a few days ago. We had submitted an application in the anti-terrorism court; however, due to holidays, the issue was delayed.” He said that Qureshi was being held under observation for 24 hours, “after which it will be decided whether he has to be admitted to the hospital”. Last week, Qureshi’s daughter, Meher Bano, in a post on the social media platform X, said that she had learnt about her father’s fall from “family after they met him in Kot Lakhpat jail”. “Three-and-half years ago a hale and hearty lion heart was sent to jail on trumped up charges … For over two years, he has been in Kot Lakhpat jail now facing ludicrous and false charges relating to May 9. He has been acquitted multiple times but [remains] behind bars due to the government’s malafide,” she alleged. Qureshi’s son, Zain, said on Wednesday that he met his father in jail, where he mentioned that he had collapsed while walking within his jail barracks. “I request the prison authorities to immediately arrange for a CT scan so that his health condition can be thoroughly assessed. Furthermore, he should be taken to a qualified dentist for the treatment of a cracked tooth,” he said on X. On Nov 6, a meeting of the PTI core committee also expressed concern over Qureshi’s “fall and the resulting impact on his health”. The committee called for the relevant courts, the government and the prison administration to immediately transfer Qureshi to a hospital and ensure his complete medical examination and necessary treatment. In December last year, Qureshi, who is also a former foreign minister, underwent a procedure to remove his gallbladder at the Pakistan Kidney and Liver Institute. Prior to that, he was taken to the PIC in May after complaining of heart pain.

items.title: 2027: Nnaji vows to end excessive taxation in Enugu
items.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has said he is contesting the 2027 election to rescue the state from what he described as excessive taxation and its impact on businesses and residents. Nnaji alleged that the high tax burden was forcing businessmen and investors to relocate from the state, adding that Enugu had become one of the most expensive places to do business in the country. He spoke while addressing indigenes of Enugu State resident in Aba, Abia State, under the umbrella of the Enugu State Consultative Forum, Abia State chapter. The former Minister of Science and Technology pledged to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, job creation and measures to address insecurity and unemployment. He said he had been consulting Enugu indigenes living outside the state to draw their attention to what he described as the challenges facing the state and seek their support ahead of the election. Nnaji expressed concern over what he described as the return of armed robbery in parts of Enugu, attributing the development to unemployment, hunger and economic hardship. He promised to establish industries that would create employment opportunities, reduce poverty and take more than 50,000 youths off the streets. “What is happening in Enugu State is condemnable. Enugu is for all, but today, businessmen and investors are relocating from the state due to excessive taxation. And the state government doesn’t care. “Our people are suffering from excessive taxation, even in the rural areas. Traders in rural communities only open their businesses in the evening when tax officials have left. Government collects N36,000 from traders in the villages, when most of them do not make such an amount annually. “Tax is based on profit, not on shops, as they are doing in Enugu. People are hungry. Armed people now invade homes at midnight to collect phones, computers and food items such as rice, beans and garri. This is something that happened more than 20 years ago,” he said. The PDP candidate also questioned the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR), claiming that it had risen from N26 billion to N406.7 billion. He compared the figure with the revenue generated by Abia and Anambra states, arguing that the high revenue collection raised questions about the state’s taxation policies and their impact on businesses. Nnaji further alleged that Enugu’s debt profile had increased significantly under the current administration, although he did not provide figures to substantiate the claim. He said government should focus on creating wealth and improving the living conditions of residents rather than imposing taxes that could undermine businesses. “We have set up the Enugu State Recovery Committee, with me as chairman. This is why we are visiting Enugu people residing outside the state, telling them about the poor situation of things in their state. “Last week, we were at Alaba International Market, and we have visited many places. I want to recover Enugu. Once we win, we will build industries based on coal, iron ore and cement. There will be no more excessive taxation in Enugu when I win,” he said. He also expressed concern over the condition of roads in Isi-Uzo Local Government Area, questioning how the state government had utilised its internally generated revenue and monthly federal allocations. In their separate remarks, the Director-General of the Uche Nnaji Campaign Organisation, Chuks Ndukwe, and Chief Uche Ugwu said the PDP candidate’s campaign was focused on industrialisation, employment generation and economic recovery. They criticised the state’s taxation policies, arguing that they had placed pressure on businesses and traders. The campaign officials also expressed confidence in the PDP’s grassroots support, describing Enugu as a traditional stronghold of the party. PDP senatorial candidates, including Nweke Kingsley Chizoba (Enugu East) and Nestor Ezeme (Enugu North), urged Nnaji to remain committed to his ambition, expressing confidence in his support among residents. Earlier, the President of the Enugu State Consultative Forum, Hon. Sunday Okonkwo, said Nnaji’s manifesto addressed issues affecting the state, including industrialisation, security and youth empowerment. He said the forum was interested in governance proposals that would address the challenges confronting businesses and residents of Enugu State. items.title: AFCON 2027Q: Nuamah remains confident of Ghana’s qualification
items.description: Ghana international Ernest Nuamah remains optimistic that the Black Stars can turn around their poor start to the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifying campaign and secure a place at next year’s tournament. Ghana are yet to pick up a point after losing their opening two matches against Côte d’Ivoire and The Gambia, leaving their qualification hopes hanging in the balance. Ahead of the crucial double-header against Somalia at the Essipong Stadium, Nuamah, who will miss both encounters through injury, has backed his teammates to rediscover their form and keep Ghana’s qualification hopes alive. The winger insists Ghana’s pedigree as one of Africa’s traditional football powerhouses should count for something, despite the team’s recent struggles. “Ghana has always been one of the top countries in Africa. It’s just that we haven’t really had good results recently, and it has been difficult for us. But at the end of the day, we are still Ghana. “We are going to come up like before, and we are really going to do what we can to qualify for the AFCON. It’s not done yet, even though we have struggled a bit. We are going to achieve our goals and be there for the tournament,” he said. Ghana’s recent struggles have been reflected in their failure to qualify for the 2025 AFCON in Morocco, missing out on the continental showpiece for the first time in 20 years. The Black Stars have also endured a prolonged drought at the tournament, having failed to win an AFCON match since 2019.

items.title: OSP opens investigations into NSA World Cup visa scandal
items.description: The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) has opened investigations into suspected corruption involving some officials of the National Sports Authority (NSA) and alleged financial irregularities surrounding Ghana’s participation in the 2026 FIFA World Cup. The investigations cover allegations of abuse of public office, irregularities in the selection of sponsorship beneficiaries, visa facilitation arrangements and the collection and management of money from prospective travellers. In a statement, the OSP said it had received petitions alleging corruption and corruption-related offences in the award of contracts by the NSA to various service providers. It is also examining claims that some individuals who won competitions organised under World Cup sponsorship initiatives were excluded from the final lists of beneficiaries submitted to foreign diplomatic missions. The investigation will seek to establish how beneficiaries were selected, who authorised the allocation of travel opportunities and whether public officials or private individuals improperly benefited from the arrangements. The latest development adds another layer to a controversy that has already triggered a police investigation, a presidential inquiry and the suspension of former NSA Director-General Yaw Ampofo Ankrah. JoySports’ investigations, published on MyJoyOnline on September 14, 2026, first exposed allegations that more than $623,000 had been collected from prospective travellers seeking assistance to obtain visas for the tournament in the United States and Canada. The investigation tracked about nine victims who said they had paid between $4,000 and $25,000 for visa assistance through individuals connected to the NSA. Information gathered by JoySports suggested over 170 people paid money to a chain of NSA officials for visa assistance to the USA. 46 were denied. 34 never got an appointment date. 50 were not processed at all. Of these, approximately 37 secured visas. All applicants seeking Canadian visas were unsuccessful. The investigation implicated Mr Ankrah and the NSA’s former Chief Operations Officer, Yaw Gyamfi Kusi Awere, alongside Nana Boateng Gyimah, Chief Executive Officer of TRIBE Culture Fest. A petition submitted to the Criminal Investigations Department (CID) of the Ghana Police Service by Mr Awere alleged that Mr Ankrah received $56,000 in commission from money collected from prospective travellers. Mr Gyimah was also accused of receiving $511,000. Mr Awere, who acknowledged the allegations to JoySports, said he had been involved in collecting money from applicants and that the funds were subsequently shared among individuals connected to the arrangement. Mr Ankrah, however, has denied wrongdoing, insisting that he neither collected money from prospective travellers nor participated in any arrangement to facilitate visas. The controversy took another turn in October when JoySports reported that $26,000 had been paid to the police on behalf of Mr Ankrah. The payment, reported on October 20, was made by a friend of the suspended NSA boss, with his approval and that of his lawyers. Sources familiar with the transaction told JoySports that the amount formed part of the $56,000 Mr Awere alleged Mr Ankrah had received as commission from proceeds linked to the visa arrangements. The individual who made the payment had reportedly undertaken to settle the outstanding balance. The payment followed Mr Awere’s petition to the police seeking assistance to recover the alleged commission and facilitate refunds to prospective travellers who had paid for visa assistance but were unsuccessful. When contacted by JoySports on October 15 for a response to the reported payment, Mr Ankrah did not respond. He has maintained that although he exchanged money with Mr Awere over the years, he was unaware that any of the funds represented commissions from prospective travellers. He has also challenged anyone to produce evidence that he collected money to facilitate visas. On October 1, President John Dramani Mahama suspended Mr Ankrah as Director-General of the NSA pending investigations by the CID. The decision followed a report submitted to the Presidency by Sports and Recreation Minister Kofi Adams after allegations of financial impropriety emerged. Professor Emmanuel Osei Sarpong was subsequently appointed Acting Director-General of the Authority. The suspension came after JoySports published details of the alleged visa arrangements, including claims that an office at the Accra Sports Stadium had been used by individuals connected to the operation. The NSA has denied authorising visa facilitation activities or permitting its premises to be used for collecting money from prospective travellers. The Minority in Parliament has also questioned the roles of the NSA, Ghana Tourism Authority, Ministry of Sports and Recreation and TRIBE Culture Fest in the arrangements. Vincent Ekow Assafuah, Ranking Member of Parliament’s Youth and Sports Committee, has raised concerns about discrepancies in lists submitted to foreign diplomatic missions. He alleged that only 15 of 102 individuals presented as NSA personnel could be verified as employees of the Authority. The Minority has called for a broader independent investigation into the institutions and individuals involved. President Mahama has also established a committee chaired by Professor Francis Dodoo to examine the allegations. The OSP’s intervention means the controversy will now face scrutiny beyond the police investigation into the alleged collection of money for visa assistance. The inclusion of NSA procurement contracts introduces a separate area of inquiry into how the Authority awarded contracts and whether public officials or private entities benefited improperly. The OSP says it will provide further information on the investigations in accordance with its disclosure policy. It has cautioned that the commencement of investigations does not establish wrongdoing and that all individuals and institutions concerned remain presumed innocent until proven guilty.

items.title: Akosua Manu declares intention to contest Adentan NPP primary
items.description: Former Deputy CEO of the National Youth Authority (NYA), Akosua Manu, has announced her intention to contest the New Patriotic Party (NPP) parliamentary primary in Adentan ahead of the 2028 general elections. She announced it on her social media handles on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, reaffirming her commitment to the constituency and her readiness to continue the political journey she began with constituents in 2024. The announcement marks her first formal indication of plans to return to the Adentan parliamentary race after contesting the seat on the NPP ticket in the 2024 general elections. In her post, Akosua Manu, who is also Special Advisor on Gender and Social Protection to Dr Bawumia, described her political journey in the constituency as unfinished, insisting that the vision she shares with residents remains relevant and that she is prepared to pursue it with renewed energy. “The work we started together in Adentan is far from over, and the vision we share for our constituency remains as important today as it was when we first began,” she stated. She said her resolve to continue the journey had strengthened, and she expressed confidence in the collective effort required to achieve their shared ambitions for the constituency. “Let’s run it back. Let’s finish the job in 2028,” she added. Her announcement is expected to reignite political activity among her supporters in Adentan, particularly those who backed her during the 2024 parliamentary contest and have been anticipating her return to the constituency’s political landscape. The declaration also sets the stage for a keen contest within the NPP as prospective aspirants position themselves ahead of the party’s parliamentary primaries.

items.title: GWL arrests 4,395 over alleged water theft in Accra crackdown
items.description: Ghana Water Limited (GWL) says it has arrested 4,395 people from households and commercial establishments over alleged water theft as part of an ongoing crackdown on illegal connections and unauthorised water use. The arrests follow an enforcement exercise launched in August 2025 to identify individuals and businesses suspected of diverting water illegally from the company’s distribution network. GWL’s Chief Manager of Corporate Planning, Monitoring and Evaluation, Michael Tawiah Klutse, disclosed the figures during an interview on Tuesday, November 10. He said the scale of water theft uncovered during the exercise had been worrying, with both households and commercial establishments implicated. “From the time we started this exercise in August 2025 up to date, you will be surprised what you’ll see. But we have almost about 4,395 households and establishments,” he said. Mr Klutse said GWL had deployed 12 enforcement teams across Accra to identify illegal connections, water diversion and other forms of unauthorised use. He expressed concern about the growing practice of water theft, warning that it undermined the company’s operations and efforts to provide reliable water services. He further disclosed that some cases uncovered during the exercise had been referred to court, with prosecutions currently underway. GWL says the crackdown will continue as it seeks to protect its distribution network and ensure consumers access water through authorised connections.

Government proposes three-tier royalty system for petroleum operations based on water depth
items.description: The government is proposing a new royalty framework for petroleum operations, with payments to be determined under a three-tier sliding scale linked to the water depth of oil and gas projects. Energy and Green Transition Minister John Abdulai Jinapor announced the proposed arrangement during his keynote address at the 2026 Local Content Conference and Exhibition, as part of a package of reforms aimed at attracting new investment into Ghana’s petroleum industry. Under the proposed system, the existing approach to royalty payments would be replaced with a three-tier structure that takes account of water depth. The measure is among seven legislative and fiscal changes the government is considering to improve the country’s petroleum investment framework. The other proposals include reducing GNPC’s initial carried interest from 15% to 10%, replacing signature bonuses with commerciality bonuses and introducing an R-factor-based Additional Petroleum Tax in place of the Additional Oil Entitlement. The government is also considering extending petroleum agreement durations from 25 to 30 years and increasing the tax-loss carry-forward period from five to ten years. Mr Jinapor said the broader reform agenda is intended to attract investment and position the petroleum industry to contribute more meaningfully to national economic transformation.

items.title: Abiana to release three-track project ‘3rd Harmony’ on November 14
items.description: Ghanaian singer-songwriter Abiana is set to release her latest three-track project, 3rd Harmony , on Saturday, 14th November 2026. The project is a musical and visual journey exploring love, connection, transformation and permanence, brought together in what is envisioned as a Symphony of Now and Forever. Conceived as more than a music release, 3rd Harmony takes listeners through three conceptual movements: NOW, BECOMING and FOREVER. The first celebrates living in the present and embracing who we are; the second explores growth, transformation, love and self-discovery; while the third reflects on legacy, eternal love and relationships that stand the test of time. These themes are expressed through three songs: What We Do for Love , One X One and We Will Always Be Together . Each offers a unique perspective on affection, commitment, companionship and the enduring bonds that connect people. The project features production from two Ghanaian talents. He-Brew produced and mixed What We Do for Love and produced One X One , while Nana Kofi (Finurse) produced We Will Always Be Together . It also features contributions from bassist Dangrahl, guitarists Ebenezer Oware and Emmanuel Kyei Baffour Adjei, keyboardist Kwesi Turkson, and additional vocalist Rigwell Ofori. Together, the collaborators provide a musical foundation that complements Abiana’s soulful vocals and expressive songwriting. Through 3rd Harmony , Abiana celebrates the love people give and receive, as well as the connections that shape their lives. The project further reflects her artistic identity, which she describes as Soul Life, blending elements of soul, highlife, neo-soul and contemporary African sounds. With its storytelling, instrumentation and distinct creative direction, the project continues Abiana’s commitment to creating music that resonates with audiences and celebrates the shared human experience. Project details Project title: 3rd Harmony Artist: Abiana Release date: Saturday, 14 November 2026 Format: Three-track musical project Producers: He-Brew and Nana Kofi (Finurse) Tracklist: What We Do for Love One X One We Will Always Be Together About Abiana Abiana is a Ghanaian singer and songwriter celebrated for her expressive vocals and distinctive musical style, which brings together elements of soul, highlife, neo-soul and contemporary African sounds. Her artistry, which she describes as Soul Life, is rooted in emotional storytelling, musical depth and an appreciation of the richness of African musical expression. Through her music, she continues to connect with audiences with songs that speak to love, life, identity and the shared human experience. 3rd Harmony will be available on major digital streaming platforms worldwide from 14 November 2026. items.title: Audits énergétiques au Burkina Faso : Le taux de réalisation au cœur d’un atelier organisé par l’Agence Faso Vêenem
items.description: Sur 1 151 structures assujetties aux audits énergétiques au Burkina Faso au 31 décembre 2025, seules 123 avaient effectivement réalisé cet exercice. Cette situation a été au centre d’un atelier d’échange organisé par l’Agence Faso Vêenem, ce 10 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, autour du cadre réglementaire et du dispositif opérationnel des audits énergétiques. La rencontre vise à renforcer la compréhension des obligations réglementaires et à identifier des solutions pour accélérer la réalisation des audits et l’application de leurs recommandations. Participant à cette rencontre, le secrétaire général du ministère en charge de l’Énergie, Doulaye Sanou, a indiqué qu’au 31 décembre 2025, sur les 1 151 structures assujetties recensées, seulement 123 avaient été auditées. Ce constat met en évidence les difficultés liées à l’application du dispositif réglementaire, mais aussi à la mise en œuvre des mesures préconisées à l’issue des diagnostics. Pour le représentant du ministère, la réalisation d’un audit ne suffit pas à garantir une réduction effective de la consommation énergétique. Les structures concernées doivent également s’engager dans l’application des recommandations, dont la faisabilité technique et économique, les coûts et les modalités de suivi doivent être examinés. « Une chose est d'avoir été auditée, une autre est de s'engager à mettre en œuvre les recommandations issues de l'audit » , a souligné Doulaye Sanou. Il a ainsi appelé les participants à examiner les obstacles rencontrés par les entreprises et à formuler des propositions susceptibles d'améliorer le fonctionnement du dispositif. Des obstacles à lever pour appliquer les recommandations-©Faso7 Les échanges doivent notamment permettre de faire le point sur le cadre juridique et réglementaire de l’efficacité énergétique, ainsi que sur les actions conduites par l’Agence Faso Vêenem entre 2019 et 2025. Selon Florent Nignan, ingénieur de conception au sein de cette structure, l’atelier prévoit également une présentation de l’agence, créée à la suite de la fusion de l’Agence nationale des énergies renouvelables et de l’efficacité énergétique (ANEREE) et de l’Agence burkinabè de l’électrification rurale (ABER). Il a expliqué que l’un des enjeux majeurs consiste à amener les gros consommateurs à comprendre l’intérêt des audits énergétiques. Ces diagnostics permettent d’identifier les causes de surconsommation et de proposer un plan d’action pour réduire les dépenses énergétiques, accompagné d’une analyse économique. Toutefois, la mise en œuvre des recommandations nécessite souvent des investissements importants. Pour faciliter leur réalisation, l’Agence Faso Vêenem entend notamment promouvoir les contrats de performance énergétique (CPE), un mécanisme qui permet de réunir différents intervenants autour d’un même projet, notamment les partenaires chargés du financement, les entreprises d’exécution des travaux et les structures de coordination. Les gros consommateurs au cœur du dispositif Au Burkina Faso, le dispositif d’efficacité énergétique mobilise plusieurs catégories d’acteurs. Florent Nignan cite notamment l’Agence Faso Vêenem, chargée de la coordination opérationnelle, les auditeurs énergétiques agréés par le ministère en charge de l’Énergie et les structures considérées comme de gros consommateurs. Ces dernières sont particulièrement concernées par les obligations d’audit prévues par la réglementation. Le diagnostic énergétique doit leur permettre de mieux maîtriser leurs consommations et d’identifier les investissements susceptibles d’améliorer leurs performances. Les seuils de consommation constituent l’un des critères permettant de déterminer les structures assujetties aux audits énergétiques obligatoires. Selon les précisions apportées par Florent Nignan, ingénieur de conception à l’Agence Faso Vêenem, cette obligation concerne notamment les bâtiments et les industries dont la consommation annuelle d’électricité dépasse 100 000 kWh, ainsi que les sociétés de transport consommant plus de 100 000 litres de carburant par an. Ces seuils permettent ainsi d’identifier les gros consommateurs d’énergie concernés par le dispositif réglementaire. L’obligation d’audit énergétique est notamment encadrée par le décret du 26 octobre 2017 portant fixation des seuils de consommation énergétique, de la périodicité des audits et des modalités d’exercice de cette activité ainsi que de l’agrément technique des auditeurs. À travers cet atelier, l’Agence Faso Vêenem entend favoriser une meilleure appropriation de ce cadre réglementaire et renforcer la collaboration entre les acteurs. Pour Doulaye Sanou, l’efficacité énergétique dépasse les seules préoccupations du ministère et de l’agence. Elle constitue un enjeu national, notamment dans la perspective de la souveraineté énergétique et du développement économique du Burkina Faso. items.title: Wapda says no threat to Tarbela Dam's integrity, critical structures after rock collapse at project site
items.description: SWABI: A press release issued by the Water and Power Development Authority (Wapda) said on Tuesday that there was no threat to the integrity of Tarbela Dam or any of its critical structures a day after a rock collapse at the 5th Extension Project (T-5) site caused a surge of water to enter nearby work areas. On Monday, a rock mass collapsed at the T-5 construction site. An emergency was declared following the collapse; construction work was suspended and workers were directed to move to safer areas. However, no loss of life was reported in the incident. In a statement issued on Tuesday, the authority said Wapda Chairman retired Lt Muhammad Saeed visited the site on Monday and Tuesday in the wake of the incident to review the situation. “The chairman visited … the intake structure, tunnel, power house and other important sites of the project. The consultants, contractor and Wapda project management briefed him on the current situation and the measures taken so far,” it said. Following this, the chairman presided over a meeting at the project site, where the possible causes of the incident were discussed in detail, it added. “Short, medium and long term preventive measures to handle such situations and strategies to address the current issue were deliberated upon. Immediate response measures were also finalised and their execution initiated,” it said. “However, the consultants, contractor and Wapda teams were unanimous in their assessment that, as of now, there is no threat to the integrity of main Tarbela dam or any of its critical structures,” the statement said. According to the handout, the Wapda chairman directed the consultants to submit a detailed report covering all aspects of the incident at the earliest. He further directed the consultants, contractor and Wapda project team to execute remedial measures immediately, and to finalise the contingency plan to minimise the delay in the overall completion of the project due to the incident. He also ordered a departmental inquiry to probe the incident. “The Ministry for Water Resources had also sought initial assessment report of the incident from Wapda which has been submitted today,” it said, adding that the Minister for Water Resources Mian Muhammad Mueen Watto had also been briefed by the Wapda chairman. Meanwhile, Wapda engineers and technical team were busy restoring and repairing the damaged parts of the project on Tuesday, according to officials. “The public should know that the situation is completely under control and no one should worry about the incident,” Swabi Deputy Commissioner Nasarullah Khan said. He said that he, the deputy commissioner of Haripur and the officials concerned were dealing with the situation under a coordinated strategy. DC Nasarullah said that the increase in the flows of the Indus River downstream had been authorised by Wapda’s technical team under safety and technical measures. Separately, an official present at the site of the project urged the public not to pay heed to unconfirmed reports and to refer only to information from official sources.

items.title: CAF Awards 2026: Lagos s’apprête à couronner les rois et reines du football africain
items.description: La Confédération africaine de football (CAF) a officialisé, ce mardi 10 novembre 2026, la tenue de la cérémonie des CAF Awards 2026 le 2 décembre prochain à Lagos, au Nigéria. Au total, 18 catégories de distinctions sont au programme pour célébrer les acteurs qui ont marqué le football africain au cours de l’année. Les meilleurs talents du continent seront bientôt à l’honneur. Joueurs et joueuses, entraîneurs, gardiens de but, jeunes espoirs, clubs et équipes nationales sont concernés par les différentes récompenses prévues lors de cette édition. Parmi les trophées les plus convoités figurent ceux de Joueur africain de l’année et de Joueuse africaine de l’année. Selon la CAF, Lagos renouera avec l’organisation de cette prestigieuse cérémonie pour la première fois depuis 2014, soit douze ans après sa dernière édition dans la métropole nigériane. En attendant le verdict, le processus de vote, lancé le 5 novembre, reste ouvert jusqu’au 20 novembre. Il concerne aussi bien les catégories masculines que féminines et mobilise notamment les associations membres de la CAF, les clubs, ainsi que les entraîneurs et capitaines remplissant les conditions requises. Soucieuse de préserver la crédibilité du scrutin, l’instance dirigeante du football africain annonce également la mise en place d’un contrôle indépendant destiné à garantir l’intégrité du vote et la transparence dans le choix des différents lauréats. Le rendez-vous est fixé au Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts, plus connu sous l’appellation de National Theatre. Les regards du football africain convergeront ainsi vers Lagos, le 2 décembre, pour découvrir les figures qui seront consacrées au terme de cette édition 2026. items.title: JOJ Dakar 2026 : le Mali termine sans médaille
items.description: Le Mali quitte les Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse (JOJ) Dakar 2026 sans medaille. Engages dans cinq disciplines, les cinq athletes maliens n'ont pas reussi a monter sur le podium. Cette premiere experience olympique organisee sur le continent africain leur a toutefois permis de se mesurer a la concurrence internationale et d'ameliorer certaines performances. Le parcours malien s'est acheve avec l'elimination de Thierno Hady Thiam en escrime. Engage dans l'epreuve individuelle, le dernier representant du Mali a ete elimine des le premier tour. Son entraîneur, Raphael Dembele, retient neanmoins son courage et les efforts fournis, malgre quelques difficultes rencontrees durant la competition. En athletisme, Awa Diarra a termine a la derniere place de la finale du 800 metres dames. Elle a cependant realise une performance encourageante en ameliorant son record personnel de neuf secondes. En taekwondo, Mariam Diallo a atteint les quarts de finale avant d'etre eliminee. De son cote, Moussa Koïta, engage en judo dans la categorie des moins de 55 kg, a concede deux defaites consecutives. En natation, Younoussa Maïga a egalement tire profit de cette competition pour progresser. Il a notamment ameliore ses chronos au 100 metres nage libre et au 50 metres papillon. Des acquis pour les prochaines competitions Malgre l'absence de medailles, les representants maliens repartent avec des enseignements importants. L'amelioration de certains records personnels et la confrontation avec des athletes venus de plusieurs pays constituent des acquis pour la suite de leur parcours. Cette participation aux JOJ Dakar 2026 pourrait ainsi servir de tremplin a ces jeunes sportifs dans la preparation de leurs prochaines echeances internationales. Les porte-drapeaux Mariam Diallo (MLI) et Younoussa Maiga (MLI) portent le drapeau national du Mali lors du defile des drapeaux des CNO, durant la ceremonie d'ouverture au stade Abdoulaye Wade, a l'occasion des Jeux olympiques de la jeunesse de Dakar 2026, a Diamniadio (Senegal). Samedi 31 octobre 2026. Photo : OIS/Felix Diemer. items.title: 11 dead, dozens injured in motorway pileup
items.description: Eleven people died and dozens were injured on Tuesday in a mass pileup on a motorway in southeastern Bulgaria, whose roads rank as the most dangerous in the EU. Crashes in thick fog snared dozens of vehicles heading in both directions of the highway linking the capital Sofia to the Black Sea city of Burgas. An estimated 50 cars and trucks were involved in the accident near the city of Yambol, regional governor Georgi Chalakov told the BTA state news agency, as government officials rushed to the scene. Images showed overturned and smashed cars and trucks mangled together, as well as burnt-out vehicles. “The toll at this point is 11 dead and 48 injured,” Prime Minister Rumen Radev told reporters. Radev was meeting EU chief Ursula von der Leyen, who is on a visit to Bulgaria, but the prime minister cancelled his official events scheduled for later Tuesday. The injured were transported to hospitals in nearby cities. The government dispatched two aircraft equipped with stretchers and medical teams. Bulgaria saw 71 road fatalities per million inhabitants in 2025, the highest rate in the European Union, according to European Commission figures. Victims blame the Balkan nation’s high number of traffic deaths on reckless driving, poorly maintained roads and an inefficient justice system. Stricter penalties Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said one Romanian was among the injured and expressed “deepest condolences” to the victims and their families in a post on X. European Council chief Antonio Costa also said on X he was “deeply saddened to learn of the tragic traffic accident in Bulgaria this morning”. A total of 456 people were killed in road traffic accidents in Bulgaria in 2025 — down five percent from the previous year and 27 percent lower than in 2019. The EU in 2019 introduced a target to reduce road deaths and serious injuries by 50 percent by 2030. A European Commission report in October said that although the EU remains “one of the world’s safest regions for road travel”, the majority of member states were not yet on track to meet the safety target. The report said that just five of the EU’s 27 countries — including Bulgaria — were on track to meet the target. However, “despite their progress since 2019, Bulgaria and Romania, alongside Croatia, continue to have the highest fatality rates in the EU when measuring deaths per million inhabitants”, the report said. In 2023, Bulgaria’s parliament adopted stricter penalties for anyone found to be driving under the influence of drugs. The cars of accused drivers are now impounded until the trial, even when the suspects have no previous criminal record. Bulgaria’s busy road traffic due to its position as a gateway to the EU is one of the main factors behind the high accident rate, according to experts. But Bulgaria’s status as the EU’s poorest member state also plays a role, with around half of the cars registered more than 20 years old. items.title: Orange Burkina Faso : La confiance, l’attention et la responsabilité au cœur de la 14e édition de l’Ethics & Compliance Day
items.description: La performance d’une entreprise ne se mesure pas uniquement à ses résultats, elle repose également sur les valeurs qui guident ses décisions et ses relations avec ses parties prenantes. C’est autour de cette conviction qu’Orange Burkina Faso a organisé, le 5 novembre 2026 à Ouagadougou, la 14e édition de l’Ethics & Compliance Day, placée sous le thème : « Nos valeurs humaines en action : la confiance, l’attention et la responsabilité au cœur de l’éthique ». Rendez-vous annuel, cette journée a offert aux managers un espace de réflexion sur leurs pratiques professionnelles et sur leur rôle dans la promotion d’une culture d’entreprise fondée sur l’intégrité, la vigilance et la confiance. Dans son allocution d’ouverture, la Directrice Générale d’Orange Burkina Faso, Nafy COULIBALY SILUÉ, a insisté sur la nécessité de traduire les valeurs de l’entreprise en comportements quotidiens. Selon elle, la confiance ne se décrète pas : elle se construit au fil des relations professionnelles et peut être fragilisée par un seul comportement. « La confiance, c’est celle que nous construisons jour après jour avec nos équipes, nos clients et nos partenaires. L’attention, c’est savoir remarquer ce qui ne va pas, mais aussi le ou la collègue qui hésite à parler. La responsabilité, c’est s’engager et assumer nos décisions, y compris lorsqu’une situation ne relève pas directement de notre périmètre » , a-t-elle expliqué. Elle a également souligné le devoir d’exemplarité des managers, dont les comportements influencent directement les pratiques de leurs équipes. Leur disponibilité et leur capacité à accueillir les préoccupations des collaborateurs contribuent à instaurer un climat de confiance et de transparence. Dans cette dynamique, elle a réaffirmé l’engagement du Groupe en faveur de la tolérance zéro face à la corruption, évoquant notamment le dispositif « Hello Éthique », qui permet aux collaborateurs de signaler de bonne foi des situations préoccupantes, sans crainte de représailles. Elle s’est par ailleurs félicitée de la reconnaissance accordée à l’entreprise par les structures nationales de lutte contre la corruption et de contrôle de l’État, qu’elle attribue à l’engagement collectif des équipes d’Orange Burkina Faso. Abdramane Diallo, Directeur de Cabinet de la Directrice Générale, en charge de l’Innovation, et Chief Compliance Officer, a pour sa part rappelé que l’éthique et la conformité constituent des piliers de la pérennité de l’entreprise. Il a souligné que cette journée permet aux managers de réfléchir aux valeurs communes qui doivent guider leurs relations avec les salariés, les clients, les partenaires et les institutions. « Pour durer, il faut des valeurs qui nous réunissent. Autrement, on peut connaître une performance, une réussite ponctuelle. Mais pour durer dans la performance et rester au service de nos clients de façon systématique, il faut des valeurs communes, des règles éthiques et un fonctionnement conforme à des normes », a-t-il déclaré. Au-delà de la réflexion collective, il a insisté sur la nécessité pour chaque manager d’incarner ces principes dans son environnement professionnel : donner l’exemple à ses équipes et promouvoir des comportements conformes à l’image d’une entreprise responsable. Quatre panels ont constitué le temps fort de cette édition. Animés par des responsables internes et par un expert externe, le Pr Florent HIEN, Directeur du Centre de Formation et de Recherche Anticorruption (CFRAC) du REN-LAC, ils ont abordé différentes problématiques liées à l’éthique et à la conformité. Les participants ont ainsi pu partager leurs expériences, exprimer leurs préoccupations et identifier des pistes d’amélioration. À travers cette 14e édition, Orange Burkina Faso entend maintenir l’éthique et la conformité au cœur de son fonctionnement, avec une conviction essentielle : la confiance des clients, des collaborateurs et des partenaires se gagne avant tout par des actes. items.title: Only 36% of Nigerians have access to improved toilets — FG
items.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has disclosed that less than 36 per cent of Nigerians have access to improved toilet facilities, raising concerns over persistent sanitation challenges and the associated public health risks. The Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas Lawal, disclosed this on Tuesday during a press briefing in Abuja to commemorate the 2026 World Toilet Day. Lawal, who was represented by the Director of Pollution Control and Environmental Health, Mrs Omotunde Adeola, said many public places, including markets, motor parks, schools and communities, still lacked adequate and functional toilet facilities. He warned that the situation was contributing to open defecation, contamination of food and water sources, and the spread of sanitation-related diseases such as cholera and typhoid. According to him, inadequate sanitation poses serious threats to public health, environmental safety and human dignity. The minister said women, girls, children, older persons and persons living with disabilities were particularly affected by the shortage of appropriate sanitation facilities. He stressed that no child should miss school because of inadequate toilet facilities, while no woman or girl should be forced to compromise her safety and dignity because of the absence of suitable toilets. Providing a global perspective, Lawal said about 4.5 billion people worldwide still lacked safely managed sanitation, while 892 million continued to practise open defecation. He said the figures underscored the need to accelerate efforts towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those relating to clean water and sanitation, gender equality, good health and sustainable communities by 2030. Government interventions On efforts to address the challenge, the minister said the Federal Ministry of Environment, in collaboration with relevant ministries, state governments and development partners, was implementing programmes to improve sanitation and promote safe excreta disposal nationwide. He listed the initiatives to include capacity building for Environmental Health Officers on faecal sludge management and toilet design, the Clean and Green Programme, and the Community-Based Waste Management and Open Defecation Control Programme. Other interventions, he said, included integrating sanitation into climate adaptation and circular economy initiatives, as well as partnering with private sector operators to provide environmentally friendly sanitation facilities. Lawal announced that the ministry would convene a National Dialogue on Faecal Sludge Management on November 23, 2026, involving seven selected states across the six geopolitical zones and the Federal Capital Territory. He said the dialogue would enable participating states to assess their experiences, share challenges and develop practical recommendations for improving faecal sludge management. As part of activities marking the World Toilet Day, the ministry will also organise a community sensitisation campaign at Kpadna Community, Utako, Abuja, on November 19. The campaign is expected to engage residents, traders and food vendors on proper sanitation, hand hygiene and safe waste disposal through health talks, interactive discussions and practical demonstrations by Environmental Health Officers. He added that the commemoration would take place simultaneously across the 36 states and the FCT through community sensitisation, advocacy campaigns and sanitary inspections of public places. The minister called on state and local governments to strengthen faecal sludge and wastewater management systems, while urging households to embrace proper toilet use, handwashing and environmental cleanliness. He also urged the private sector to invest in affordable sanitation technologies and climate-resilient infrastructure, while calling on development partners and civil society organisations to sustain their support for sanitation advocacy and infrastructure development. Lawal further stressed the need for women and girls to participate actively in designing, implementing and monitoring sanitation interventions, rather than being treated merely as beneficiaries. This year’s World Toilet Day is themed, “Sanitation and Gender Equality,” with the campaign tagline, “Safe Toilets. items.title: Dialogue social : la ministre Ramatoulaye s’engage à instaurer un dialogue permanent avec les syndicats et dévoile cinq chantiers prioritaires
items.description: La ministre de l’Emploi, du Travail et de la Protection sociale, Ramatoulaye Camara, a rencontré, ce mardi 10 novembre 2026, les responsables des centrales syndicales guinéennes à la Bourse du Travail, à Conakry. Cette première prise de contact avec les partenaires sociaux a permis à la nouvelle ministre de réaffirmer sa volonté de faire du dialogue social un pilier permanent de son action et de présenter les principaux axes de travail de son département. Les syndicats réclament leur implication dans le programme Simandou 2040 Prenant la parole au nom du mouvement syndical guinéen, la vice-présidente a salué cette démarche de rapprochement avec les partenaires sociaux, tout en mettant en lumière les principaux défis auxquels le département doit s’attaquer. Parmi les priorités évoquées figurent la promotion de l’emploi des jeunes et des femmes, l’application effective du Code du travail, le respect des conventions collectives, l’amélioration des conditions de travail ainsi que l’extension de la protection sociale aux travailleurs du secteur informel. Elle a particulièrement insisté sur la nécessité d’associer pleinement les organisations syndicales au suivi social du programme Simandou 2040. Selon elle, ce vaste projet de développement ne doit pas se limiter à l’exploitation des ressources minières, mais doit également favoriser la création d’emplois décents, la qualification de la main-d’œuvre nationale et une meilleure protection des travailleurs. « Le Simandou 2040 ne sera pleinement une réussite que s'il est aussi une réussite sociale », a-t-elle déclaré, plaidant notamment pour le respect des droits des travailleurs, des normes de santé et de sécurité au travail, de l’égalité de traitement ainsi que pour la priorité à accorder à l’emploi local. La ministre Ramatoulaye Camara mise sur un dialogue social permanent En réponse aux préoccupations soulevées par les représentants syndicaux, la ministre a salué le choix de la Bourse du Travail pour abriter cette rencontre, estimant qu’il témoigne du respect accordé à l’histoire et au rôle du mouvement syndical dans le pays. Elle a également transmis les salutations du président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, avant d’assurer que les préoccupations des travailleurs occupent une place importante dans les priorités du gouvernement. Forte de son expérience auprès des partenaires sociaux, notamment lors des négociations nationales de 2022, Ramatoulaye Camara a réaffirmé sa volonté de maintenir une collaboration étroite avec les organisations syndicales, y compris en cas de divergences. À cet effet, elle a pris trois engagements : la régularité des échanges, la sincérité des discussions et le suivi effectif des engagements pris. « Le dialogue social se juge aux réponses qu’il apporte aux travailleurs », a-t-elle souligné, insistant sur l’importance de maintenir des échanges permanents, y compris en dehors des périodes de crise, afin de prévenir les incompréhensions et de parvenir à des solutions concertées aux difficultés du monde du travail. La ministre a, par ailleurs, appelé les centrales syndicales à privilégier la cohésion et l’unité d’action, tout en respectant l’indépendance de chaque organisation. Elle a également annoncé que son département travaillerait avec les acteurs concernés à la mise en place des conditions nécessaires à l’organisation des élections de représentativité syndicale, dans un cadre transparent et respectueux de la liberté syndicale. Abordant la question du programme Simandou 2040, elle a assuré que les travailleurs guinéens seraient associés aux différentes démarches liées à sa mise en œuvre et devraient bénéficier concrètement des opportunités qu’il offre. Pour la ministre, la transformation économique du pays doit aussi se mesurer à la qualité des emplois créés, à la dignité des travailleurs et à l’amélioration de leurs conditions de vie. Cinq chantiers prioritaires pour le monde du travail Au cours de son intervention, Ramatoulaye Camara a décliné cinq axes prioritaires autour desquels elle entend mobiliser son département et les partenaires sociaux. Le premier concerne l’emploi et l’insertion professionnelle des jeunes, avec une attention particulière à l’adéquation entre la formation et les besoins des employeurs, ainsi qu’à la valorisation de la main-d’œuvre locale. Le deuxième porte sur l’extension de la protection sociale aux travailleurs du secteur informel, notamment dans l’agriculture et l’artisanat. Le troisième vise le renforcement de l’application de la législation du travail et l’amélioration des conditions professionnelles, à travers notamment le contrôle du respect des droits des travailleurs, de la rémunération et des normes de santé et de sécurité au travail. Les deux autres axes concernent la prévention des conflits sociaux, à travers le dialogue, la médiation et la négociation, ainsi que la promotion de la participation des femmes et des jeunes aux instances de représentation et de décision, aussi bien dans les entreprises qu’au sein des organisations syndicales. Dans le domaine de la protection des travailleurs, la ministre a également salué la publication du décret relatif aux maladies professionnelles indemnisables dans les secteurs public et privé, qu’elle a présentée comme une avancée importante pour le bien-être des travailleurs guinéens. À l’issue de cette rencontre, les deux parties ont affiché leur volonté de consolider leurs relations autour de la concertation, de la confiance et de la recherche de solutions concrètes aux préoccupations du monde du travail. Ramatoulaye Camara a enfin assuré que sa porte resterait ouverte à l’ensemble des centrales syndicales, dans un esprit d’impartialité et de respect des responsabilités de chacun. Youssouf Keita L’article Dialogue social : la ministre Ramatoulaye s’engage à instaurer un dialogue permanent avec les syndicats et dévoile cinq chantiers prioritaires est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: MOSOP accuses Niger Delta governors of mismanaging 13% derivation funds
items.description: ….Group calls for amendment of derivation law, commends NDDC’s development efforts By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — The Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (MOSOP) has accused successive governors in the Niger Delta of mismanaging the 13 per cent derivation funds, calling for an amendment of the law to ensure that oil-producing communities directly benefit from the revenue. MOSOP President, Fegalo Nsuke, made the call on Tuesday in Port Harcourt during activities marking the 31st anniversary of the execution of environmental activist Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni leaders by the military government of the late General Sani Abacha. Nsuke said the objectives of the derivation fund had not been achieved because state governors allegedly exercised excessive discretion over its allocation, rather than directing the resources to communities where oil and gas were extracted. He argued that the sacrifices of Saro-Wiwa and other Ogoni martyrs would have limited impact on the lives of people unless laws governing resource benefits specifically addressed the needs of communities bearing the consequences of oil exploration. “The idea of derivation funds was to address the underdevelopment in the Niger Delta region. However, the structure of administration of the funds makes it vulnerable to abuse and has left the funds at the discretion of state governors. This needs to be addressed,” he said. According to Nsuke, the intention behind the derivation arrangement was to address underdevelopment in oil-producing areas, but the funds were not being adequately directed towards those communities. Citing Ogba/Egbema and Andoni communities in Rivers State, he said areas responsible for significant oil production had yet to receive what he considered adequate development funding. He argued that allowing governors to determine spending priorities without directly channelling an appropriate share to oil-producing communities had undermined the objectives of the derivation arrangement. Commends NDDC Despite his criticism of the management of derivation funds, Nsuke commended the current management of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) for what he described as its visible development impact across the region. He urged the commission to sustain and expand its interventions, noting that the agency emerged from the struggles for justice and development championed by Saro-Wiwa and other Niger Delta activists. “It is important that the areas from where resources are extracted should get their due rewards and a proportionate injection of the derivation funds. The structure for the administration of the derivation funds needs to change if we must achieve that. “I am pleased that the NDDC under its present management is making some impressive impacts. MOSOP will encourage them to do more,” he said. Nsuke blamed persistent poverty in the Niger Delta on what he described as the mismanagement of derivation revenues, arguing that the funds allocated to oil-producing states over the years should have made a significant difference in addressing underdevelopment. He also called for greater unity among Niger Delta communities, saying collective action would strengthen their ability to demand accountability from state governments. “It is important for the people to be united and hold their governments to account. I think what comes to the oil-producing states is significant enough to deal with basic issues such as water provision, security and infrastructure, and it is sad that the revenues are being largely mismanaged by the governors because the people are not holding them to account,” he said.
